It all started with an innocent WhatsApp message.

“Has anyone got any spare eclipse glasses? I left it too late and can’t seem to find any!”

Little did I know it but this benign missive, sent to my local community choir group on Monday morning by a nice woman called Sarah, was the unwitting catalyst for what would quickly become a deranged, Race Across the World style quest to secure a pair for myself. My own personal Odyssey, if we want to be culturally relevant.

Within minutes of her original plea, there were multiple replies. “The print shop have got some, I think – heading there ASAP!!!”

“Try the newsagents on Bouverie Road, I got some from there yesterday but they were limited to five pairs per person?”

“This link looks good – currently saying will deliver before Wednesday [prayer hands emoji].”

I’ll be honest – while I’d heard some chatter about the solar eclipse happening on 12 August, prior to this stream of “hot tips” and warm leads I had given it almost zero thought. But the funny thing is, as more messages came pinging in – “sold out online!”; “print shop has run out!”; “newsagent out of stock!” – I suddenly wanted, more than anything else in this solar system, to get my mitts on a pair. The scarcity mindset had officially set in. I struggled to focus on anything else for the rest of the day.

“They’re being stupid – it must be possible to buy them on the internet,” I thought, scornfully. “You can buy anything on the internet. That’s why it’s killing off independent businesses so effectively!”

But, of course, my lovely choirmates weren’t stupid at all. I was the idiot – blithely assuming I’d be able to casually buy a pair two days before the UK’s most complete eclipse event in 27 years.

open image in gallery Persistence pays off: Solar eclipse glasses secured at Old Spitalfields Market ( Helen Coffey/The Independent )

The more I looked online, the more panicked I became. Every single purveyor was either out of stock or advertising a delivery date of Friday 14 August at the earliest, two days after the fact. Yes, even on Amazon Prime. Getting hold of a simple strip of cardboard with black plastic lenses that would ensure I could safely look upon a burning orb 93 million miles away was proving not just tricky but nigh-on impossible.

Still, this was all currently playing out in my humble hometown in Kent. Heading into London to go to the office, I reasoned things would be different in the capital. The Big Smoke, the economical hub of this great nation, would surely be selling specs on every corner.

Alas, the situation in Folkestone was indicative of what was unfolding across the country. A cursory Google search showed that the market in London was just as much shaped by supply < demand and, consequently, the only viable strategy was to comb through a random assortment of Reddit threads and Facebook posts like a detective on the trail of the Zodiac killer.

Jessops were said to be selling pairs, but whether or not there would be any by the time one arrived was unclear. Greenwich Observatory seemed to be the safest bet, but they warned of limited stocks (and, quite honestly, it was a mission from the City).

open image in gallery Solar Eclipse London are doing strategic 'drops' of glasses across London ( Helen Coffey )

There were whispers of some being sold under the counter at a specific bakery by Bond Street tube station, rumours of a single convenience store near Aldgate East that had a fresh batch. Booze and Essential Putney “had 90 pairs this morning”; Snax Wimbledon “just got 300 pairs, apparently”.

It was while picking through the comments underneath a post from “Muswell Hill Group and Friends” Facebook group in response to the news that Fresh Bakery in Finsbury Park had been flogging them that I realised I had accidentally become part of something – a new tribe of people driven slightly insane by a dearth of resource. “Anybody know if it is open now and if they have two pairs in stock??” wrote one anxious soul. “Driving all the way from Muswell Hill.”

And it was while dissecting a separate social media thread based on the key words “solar eclipse glasses”, “where”, “buy”, “TODAY, FOR THE LOVE OF GOD” that I happened upon my best, most tangible lead yet: an underground WhatsApp group called Solar Eclipse London.

That’s where things truly got weird. This mysterious enterprise, whose WhatsApp community had only sprung into being on Sunday, seemed to have “ISO 12312-2 certified” eclipse inventory up the wazoo and was deploying it strategically across London. Different locations at different times; limited “drops”, with hype built by trailing cryptic clues about the next ballpark area without details of the exact whereabouts.

I realised I had accidentally become part of something – a new tribe of people driven slightly insane by a dearth of resource

“Finsbury Park, we’re coming soon.”

“We have a big surprise for everyone. There is a location with over 2,000 waiting for you all. Will reveal at 2.30pm.”

“Hint being sent below”, with a picture of the glasses against a backdrop of Big Ben.

And, my personal favourite, “The location rhymes with Chutney??”

The marketing was flawless, as was the entrepreneurial nous; within the space of a few hours, the WhatsApp community had grown from under a thousand-strong to over 7,000 (and by the end of the day it had hit 9,000). And then they hinted Liverpool Street was the next station for a forthcoming “shipment”, which just so happened to be around the corner from my office (#blessed). The exact location, however, would be shared on their Instagram – with instructions to “FOLLOW AND LIKE!”, another excellent marketing ploy for engagement – and pairs would be limited to two per person. Each one would cost £5, cash only. Oh, it was on.

I grabbed two colleagues to ensure we could obtain the requisite number of pairs and headed out into the unknown, refreshing the Insta account every 10 seconds like a woman possessed. Finally, aha! “Old Spitalfields Market”. Still vaguely imprecise, but enough to go on.

open image in gallery Solar eclipse glasses have sold out across the UK ( AFP/Getty )

The nearer we got, the more suspicious we felt. Was this all a weird prank? Was someone going to jump out and shout “Punked!” in our faces, like a Noughties Ashton Kutcher, as we stumbled around the precinct?

But any reticence disappeared once we spotted that most British of spectacles: a queue. And not just any queue. This one was long, winding, and stretching into the distance as far as the eye could see. Word had obviously spread quickly and, within minutes, the line had grown so long I could no longer see the end of it.

No point wondering how the heck hundreds of people had arrived before us – witchcraft seemed to be the only plausible explanation – we were in it now.

“This is the second location I’ve tried today,” shared the man directly behind us in the queue, with a mildly manic, desperate air. “Finsbury Park sold out this morning – I’ve just been waiting around for the next drop!”

I briefly wondered whether, if I managed to obtain some and he didn’t, I’d be altruistic enough to give up mine to this more deserving soul. No, came the disconcertingly cold answer from deep within. You snooze, you lose.

This is the second location I’ve tried today – I’ve just been waiting around for the next drop!

Still, there was a conviviality about the whole thing – a curiously carnival-esque spirit. People in the queue caught eyes and smiled shyly, or exchanged tales of their previous attempts to obtain a pair by trekking the width and breadth of London based on little more than hope and hearsay. Perhaps it was being drawn together around the same wholesome event, but a similar feel to that of the World Cup prevailed among these stressed yet jubilant Londoners: we were experiencing another common cause to unite us in these increasingly divided times.

We shuffled forward excruciatingly slowly, every passing minute cranking up the tension another unbearable notch. Unlike some of the other WhatsApp updates, this one had failed to include the number of spectacles on offer. There could be 30, or 300, or 3,000; there was no way of knowing.

After 20 minutes of inching along, we could finally see the front of the line. This, I knew, would be the exact moment they ran out of stock – when we were in first spitting, then touching, distance. The universe’s sick sense of humour all but guaranteed it. We were eight people from the front now. Five. Three. But, wait… They weren’t going to run out! The universe was on our side!

As we arrived at the kiosk, handed over our crisp, £10 notes, joyfully took our strips of cardboard gold and punched the air in triumph, I felt what can only be described as a shot of pure exhilaration.

Sure, it was more work than clicking “next day delivery” on Amazon – but a victory earned through the thrill of the hunt? That tastes all the sweeter.

News.title: Transfer news LIVE: Liverpool eye cut-price Barcola deal, Arsenal blow, bid rejected for Man Utd target
News.content:
Premier League transfer round-up

Liverpool are hoping to swiftly add to the loan signing of Ronald Araujo by hashing out a deal for Paris Saint-Germain winger Bradley Barcola after reaching a reported agreement over personal terms. Barcola leads Liverpool’s list of transfer targets and the Reds are in talks with PSG over a fee, though the European champions are demanding £145m to sell the winger.

Arsenal have offered Myles Lewis-Skelly to multiple Premier League clubs, including rivals Chelsea and Manchester United, but both clubs have reportedly turned down the chance to sign the teenager, who is believed to want to fight for his place despite increased competition. As reported by The Independent last week, there was a chance Arsenal would reconsider their position on Lewis-Skelly after completing the signing of Bruno Guimaraes.

Meanwhile, Ferran Torres appears set to swap Barcelona for PSG, while Rodri looks set to leave Manchester City amid interest from Barcelona and Real Madrid. The World Cup winning captain is into the final year of his contract and favours a move to Barca – who are considering a second bid after an initial offer of £38m was rejected. City seem to be making preparations for that outcome as they close in on the signing of World Cup breakout star Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille.

Follow all of the latest news, rumours and done deals with our live blog below

News.title: Tui profits slump as travellers avoid flying during Middle East conflict
News.content:

Holiday operator Tui has seen its quarterly earnings drop sharply as cautious consumers continue to delay booking their trips until the last minute amid ongoing uncertainty surrounding the Iran war.

Pre-tax profits for Europe’s largest travel company fell 43 per cent to €153.4 million (£131 million) during its third quarter to the end of June.

The business was hit by escalating fuel costs caused by the Middle East conflict, alongside pressure to drop prices due to subdued demand and heightened competition.

Underlying earnings decreased 27 per cent over the latest quarter to €233.8 million (£199.7 million), while overall customer numbers dropped 3 per cent to 9.9 million.

Tui reported an €81 million (£69.2 million) financial hit across the first nine months of its financial year so far, stemming from the Iran war and Jamaican hurricanes. This included a €20 million (£17.1 million) "direct" impact on its cruise division during quarter three from Middle East conflict.

During March, the company had to repatriate roughly 5,000 guests from two cruise liners moored in Abu Dhabi, which then stayed in Gulf ports until the middle of May.

open image in gallery Pre-tax profits at Europe’s largest travel operator tumbled 43 per cent to €153.4 million (£131 million) in its third quarter to the end of June ( PA Archive )

Sebastian Ebel, chief executive of Tui, stated that the group has navigated these difficult trading conditions, though travellers are continually leaving bookings until closer to departure.

He said: “2026 is no ordinary year.

“Tui has held its own well in a difficult global environment.

“Our business model is proving to be resilient. Travel remains highly relevant to people’s lives, but the timing of travel decision has shifted.”

Mr Ebel added: “Wars and geopolitical tensions, consumer caution, economic weakness and rising inflation in Europe’s core markets – all these factors have influenced consumer sentiment and the timing of purchasing decisions.”

Tui’s markets and airline business, which includes its traditional tour operator division, swung to a €17.4 million (£14.9 million) underlying loss from profits of €49.7 million (£42.4 million) a year earlier.

open image in gallery Sebastian Ebel, chief executive of Tui, said the group has weathered the tough trading conditions, but that holidaymakers are increasingly booking trips later towards their departure date ( TUI/Blue Lagoon Village, Kos )

Its holiday experiences arm – which includes its differentiated cruise liners and hotels as well as TUI Musement tours and activities – proved more resilient with underlying earnings slipping 5.6 per cent to €277.8 million (£237.3 million).

Tui kept its full-year outlook unchanged as it said bookings were improving.

Booked revenues in the firm’s markets and airline business were 6 per cent lower over the summer season – marginally improved since May – while it has seen a 7 per cent rise in the past four weeks “indicating a recovery in demand”.

Greece and Spain – including the Balearic and Canary Islands – continue to be in high demand, while destinations in the Eastern Mediterranean have also started to pick up again in recent weeks, according to Tui.

News.title: Rihanna shares rare video of her children visiting Barbados street named after her
News.content:
Rihanna has shared a rare video of her three children as she took them back to her childhood home in Barbados.

On Tuesday (11 August), the 38-year-old singer revisited Westbury New Road, the street that she grew up on, which has since been renamed in her honour.

“One minute I feel like that kid from Westbury…the next minute I’m bringing my own kids back to ‘Rihanna Drive’,” she wrote as she shared photographs and footage from the visit.

“Trippy how life works,” reflected the businesswoman, who rarely shares pictures or does public appearances with her children, whom she shares with rapper A$AP Rocky.

News.title: Watch: The Office star Lucy Davis rings cancer bell as she announces incurable diagnosis
News.content:
The Office star Lucy Davis has revealed she has been diagnosed with incurable breast cancer as she shared a video of herself ringing an end-of-treatment bell.

On Tuesday (11 August), the actor, 53, said that she was first diagnosed a year-and-a-half ago, and since then, the cancer has “metastasized” to her bones, including her “spine, right hip and ribs”, adding that "it is too late for chemotherapy”.

Sharing a video of her ringing a bell, the actor read out a rhyme to signal the end of her treatment.

Davis, who is best known for playing Dawn Tinsley in the BBC sitcom, added: “As of now, I’m trying to live out whatever might be left of my life in as fun a way as I possibly can.”

An F-16 fighter jet was forced to intercept a civilian plane over Geneva, Ohio, as President Donald Trump attended the Patriot Games, the second such incident in a week.

North American Aerospace Defense Command said in a statement its jet had fired flares to catch the attention of the pilot, who had violated temporary flight restrictions imposed on the area, before escorting the plane to safety Tuesday.

The incident occurred at approximately 6:15 p.m. ET, shortly after the president had arrived at Spire Academy in Ashtabula County to see the conclusion of the White House-organized youth athletic competition, an event that was immediately compared to the dystopian Hunger Games franchise when it was first announced.

NORAD’s forced intervention came just days after it was compelled to do the same when at least three planes crossed over Trump’s golf club in Bedminster, New Jersey, while the president was at the site, his trip coinciding with the venue’s staging of the four-day LIV Golf New York championship.

open image in gallery An F-16 fighter jet had to be scrambled over Geneva, Ohio, Tuesday to escort a civilian plane out of airspace restricted to allow for President Donald Trump’s attendance at the Patriot Games (file photo) ( AFP/Getty )

TFR violations also occurred at the FIFA World Cup Final in New Jersey last month, which likewise caused the command to send out jets on three occasions to shepherd 10 planes away from the MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford.

The Independent has reached out to NORAD for further comment.

The three-day Patriot Games was organized by the Trump-aligned Freedom 250 committee as part of America’s 250th anniversary celebrations.

The president entered the hosting school’s arena Tuesday in a hail of sparklers alongside ESPN’s Pat McAfee as he led out a group of competitors who had battled against delegates from all 50 states and various U.S. territories and tribal nations to make it to the finale.

He later gave a brief interview to the sports broadcasting network in which he praised the national pride of the participants.

Trump also did his “YMCA” shimmy at the close as the winners celebrated receiving their medals and $125,000 checks – bearing his familiar signature – in a rain of confetti.

open image in gallery Trump celebrated with the victorious athletes at the Spire Academy in Ashtabula County and even busted out his signature shimmy dance ( Getty )

The organizers – who were also behind this summer’s poorly-attended Great American State Fair on the National Mall in Washington, D.C. – were reportedly so worried about turnout they had “bombarded” people with emails in advance urging them to attend.

The event’s ticketing website was still open for business on the morning before the finale was due to take place.

The games themselves were also marked by controversy after some of the athletes taking part told The Washington Post they were unnerved to see that the majority of those chosen to compete were white.

“It’s a little startling,” one participant said. “This is supposed to be the best high school athletes… It just feels a little concerning not to see very many different types of people.”

News.title: Madagascar forced to divide and share mpox vaccine as epidemic takes off
News.content:
Authorities in Madagascar are being forced to split single vaccines into fifths to try to protect as many people as possible during an ongoing mpox outbreak.

The method, known as “fractional dosing”, is authorised by the World Health Organization (WHO) in emergencies when there are critical vaccine shortages, but is not routinely recommended and carries a level of risk.

Madagascar, the African island with a population of roughly 33 million people, is currently battling its largest-ever outbreak of the virus formerly known as monkeypox, with at least 4,000 cases recorded so far.

Another one million people are thought to be at risk of contracting clade 1b mpox, a fast-spreading strain of the virus that emerged from the Democratic Republic of the Congo in late 2023.

High risk groups include sex workers, young children, and people living with HIV/Aids. Medical workers are also at risk.

“Public health authorities in Madagascar have been given too few doses to protect the at-risk population; they were initially given 30,000 doses in May, and a subsequent 30,000 have just arrived at the end of July,” said Akhil Bansal, a doctor of internal medicine working on the mpox response in Madagascar and a policy fellow at the Centre for Global Development.

“However, we need to vaccinate more than one million people, so we have been “fractionally dosing”, or splitting vaccines, into fifths, to stretch the supply as far as we can.

“This is a somewhat established approach for vaccines, but even then, the number of doses we have is insufficient,” said Dr Bansal.

News.title: Sudan exodus threatens humanitarian catastrophe in Chad
News.content:
Trapped in a desert encampment in Chad, Abakar Adam, 70, dreams of returning to his small farm in neighbouring Sudan, nearby to the village where he was born.

But Mr Adam can’t go home.

Hidden from sight, he watched soldiers set fire to his farmhouse and slaughter his livestock three years ago. One month later, after resettling in the city of El Geneina in West Darfur he heard 40mm grenades rain down on hospitals while patients fought for their lives inside and witnessed civilians executed in the street.

Shortly after, a bullet from the rifle of a Rapid Support Force (RSF) soldier ripped through his gut, and he recalls how he struggled to pull his daughter from the blood-soaked sand after her eye was gouged out by a militiaman during their escape from Sudan.

Now, sitting outside his rotting, wooden shelter in eastern Chad, just 20 miles from the border with Sudan, he tells The Telegraph that he can’t forget the faces of the blind and disabled who he witnessed being thrown onto piles of hay and burnt alive.

Adam’s story is not unique and the refugee camp where he finds himself with tens of thousands of others is on the brink of collapse.

News.title: Telegraph Fantasy Football 2026/27: Everything you need to know and FAQs
News.content:
What’s new for 2026/27?





You’ll need to re-register

When signing up to Telegraph Fantasy Football this season you will notice your old logins do not work.

New for this season you will need to register or login to an existing telegraph.co.uk account to play.

NOTE: you do not need to subscribe in order to play Telegraph Fantasy Football - it is free to play.

Having trouble making a new account or logging in to an existing telegraph.co.uk account? Click here and look at our troubleshooting guide that can guide you through the process.



We’ve had a makeover and Leagues have moved

Over the summer we changed game provider meaning the site was built again from scratch. We hope you like the new look and feel.

We know nobody likes change, but take your time to get to know the new layout as some aspects of the site may have moved slightly.

The most notable change is that Leagues are now created and joined below your team selection.



Back to basics

With such a short space of time to get the TFF live for this season, the game has been stripped back to basics.

You’ll notice there are no Public Leagues and no prizes for Weekly and Monthly Leaderboard winners. Assistant Manager has also not been integrated for launch.



The Fixture Tracker

Whilst the game has been stripped back to basics, you’ll notice a new fixture tracker above your team selection. This is there to help you make transfer decisions and we hope you like it.



No rule changes.

Whilst some things may have changed, the rules remain unchanged.

Telegraph Fantasy Football is fantasy football at its purest. No gimmicks, no boosts, no captains. Simply pick the best XI players you can.



Assists

However, this season assists will no longer follow Opta’s “Fantasy Assist” definition and revert back to standard assists.



Did you miss it? League Cup fixtures and five more transfers

In case you missed it last year, this season will also feature League Cup fixtures meaning all competitive domestic football containing Premier League fixtures will count towards your Telegraph Fantasy Football points tally.

Why the change? Well for years the general advice early in the season is to hold onto your transfers and we thought that was getting a bit stale. With League Cup fixtures starting as early as Game Week 3 some seasons, you’d be a fool not to take advantage of some fixture gains against lower-league opposition.

To help with the additional fixtures we have also added five more transfers to your season total.



Paid leagues are no more

Unfortunately Plucky Paid Leagues are not integrated this season.



Three new teams

Ipswich are no strangers to Telegraph Fantasy Football as they both return from relegations in 2025. They bring with them a host of talent including two big names you might recognise, including Jaden Philogene (£2.9m) and Leif Davis (£2.6m).

It has been a fair few years since Hull City (2016/17) and Coventry City (2000/01) last featured in Telegraph Fantasy Football - memories may even flood back of posting in your transfers for the Sky Blues’ players. Both clubs are favourites to go down, but with some exciting signings like Tzolakis (£2.5m) and Thomas-Asante (£2.7m) they will certainly put up a fight.

Start creating your team >



FAQs





When does Telegraph Fantasy Football start?

The 2026/27 edition of Telegraph Fantasy Football will launch in the two weeks leading up to the start of the Premier League. The scoring will commence on Friday August 21, 2026 at 8pm when the Premier League champions Arsenal host Coventry.



How do I register for Telegraph Fantasy Football?

You will need to create a new, or use your existing telegraph.co.uk account in order to play Telegraph Fantasy Football. Simply click “SIGN UP”, then “Continue with Telegraph” and you will be temporarily taken to telegraph.co.uk to login with your existing Telegraph account or create a new account, before automatically returning back to the Telegraph Fantasy Football site.

Note: this account is not the same as your account from previous Telegraph Fantasy Football seasons.

Having trouble making a new account or logging in to an existing telegraph.co.uk account? Click here and look at our troubleshooting guide that can guide you through the process.

How much does it cost to play Telegraph Fantasy Football?

Telegraph Fantasy Football is completely free to play. All managers compete for the £5,000 prize pool as well the chance to challenge friends, family, colleagues and fellow managers in private mini-leagues.



How many players can I pick in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

You only have to pick a squad of XI players in Telegraph Fantasy Football. With no bench to rely on, finding players who get minutes on the pitch is key and we help you out there by allowing transfers right up until every kick-off.



How many teams can I pick in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

You can create up to five teams in Telegraph Fantasy Football with a budget of £50m for each, meaning you have a better chance of being in contention for the prizes come the end of the season if some of your selections prove to be unsuccessful.



How many transfers can I make in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

Up until the first game on Friday August 21, 2025, there is a transfer amnesty, meaning you can make as many changes as you like. After the season has started you have 45 transfers for the whole campaign with a maximum of five per Game Week (00:00 Tuesday to 23:59 Monday).





How do I join a private league in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

Leagues have now moved below your team selection.

This should make it easier for managers to see which league the team is in that they are making changes to.

To join a league click “Join a league” and then add the 6 digit code that the League Chairman will have access to.

To create a league click “Create a league”, name the league and then copy the league code generated to share with your fellow managers.

League Chairmen will have the ability to lock and unlock a league to new joiners.



Do ALL Cup games count in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

Yes. All League Cup fixtures plus all FA Cup games involving Premier League sides count towards your TFF points tally. This adds a great dimension to the game as you will want to load your teams with players who make the latter stages for an advantage over your competitors. However, one thing to note is that penalty shoot-outs do not count towards your score.



How many players are in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

You can expect to compete against more than 100,000 other teams in Telegraph Fantasy Football – a vast but tight-knit community of players where you have every chance of winning one of our many prizes on offer throughout the year.

We aim to include every player in a squad who has a chance of getting some game time. From time to time we may miss a youngster on debut, but rest assured they will soon be added to the player list and feel free to let us know on Facebook or Twitter if you feel someone is missing.

Having technical issues with TFF? Check our Troubleshooting page for help.



What else do I need to know?



Get your strategy right. Getting the balance of your team right can be a tricky business, especially with limited funds, but there are a few tried and trusted methods that will stand you in good stead:



Pick regular starters

Okay, so this isn’t always straightforward in the world of squad rotation where world-class players routinely find themselves sitting on the bench. That said, there are certain players who, if fit, are almost always the first name on the team sheet. Think Bruno Fernandes at Manchester United, Jordan Pickford for Everton and Liverpool’s Virgil van Dijk.



Find a couple of budget ‘gems’

Igor Thiago, Nico O’Reilly and James Garner were among a crop of players who began last term in the ‘unfancied’ category and were must-have ‘enablers’ by the time the season was over. If you’re able to identify one or two of this type of player early in the season, you could be on to a winner.



Be transfer savvy

We’ve all been there – you spend hours selecting your team for the big kick-off then half of them don’t start, the other half have stinkers and your star striker gets a season-ending injury. If you do get off to a slow start, don’t panic. Lurching from one strategy to another could do more harm than good, wasting precious transfers in the process. Trust your instincts, tweak where necessary and the points will come.



Read our weekly Selection Guide

The best advice comes from experts at the Fantasy Football Hub who make our weekly selection guide a prolific source of Telegraph Fantasy Football tips and Telegraph Fantasy Football match facts.

If you subscribe to the weekly newsletter this will hit your inbox on Friday around lunchtime; alternatively it can be found on our social channels or Telegraph Fantasy Football content hub.



Telegraph Fantasy Football Player List

We aim to keep our player list up to date with all comings and goings in the transfer window and the first place to look is our trusted Stats Centre. However, if you fancy yourself as a bit of a Telegraph Fantasy Football expert like the team at Fantasy Football Hub, you can find a player list below in a spreadsheet format so you can do your own analysis.

On the document simply click “file”, then “make a copy” and you will have your own version of the player list at that time to edit as you please.



Download the Telegraph Fantasy Football App

Never miss a chance to make a transfer and download the Telegraph Fantasy Football App which is available on iOS and Android.





You can follow the latest Telegraph Fantasy Football news and discussions throughout the year on Facebook, Twitter and Fantasy Football Content Hub.

News.title: Telegraph Fantasy Football: transfers explained and top transfer tips
News.content:
As the new Telegraph Fantasy Football season approaches, the fantasy football experts at Fantasy Football Hub will continue to bring you the very best in fantasy football knowledge, tips and tools to help you rise up the ranks and win your mini-leagues.

To join the Hub and get access to all their great resources and expert tips you can take advantage of its 50% pre-season discount here.



Transfers explained



A good place to start is by explaining the Telegraph Fantasy Football rules on transfers. First thing to note is the pre-season transfer amnesty, so you can make unlimited changes to your teams right up until the first scheduled kick-off on Friday 21 August, 20:00.

45 is the magic number of transfers you receive during the season, five more than last season to help negotiate the new League Cup fixtures. This equates to a little more than one a week. You can use a maximum of five transfers in any Game Week which run from 00:00 on Tuesdays to 23:59 on Mondays.

Four seasons ago we scrapped the two-hour rule, meaning you can make transfers right up until a game kicks off. However, we don’t suggest you leave it that late as if a transfer is not completed in time you will not gain any points for the game from the player transferred in. Starting XIs are released an hour before kick-off so you have an ample window to implement any changes.

Scrapping the two-hour rule also means that this year you can be more flexible with your transfers each week. Once a player’s game has started you will amass their points for the entire game and are free to transfer them out for another player who may be kicking off while the previous game is being played, thus benefiting from two players’ points.



Top transfer strategy tips



1) Utilise fixture gains



Telegraph Fantasy Football is unique amongst other fantasy games in that you can transfer a player out as soon as they’ve played for a player yet to play that day or match week. So if Haaland (£8.3m) played in the 12.30pm Saturday kick-off, managers can transfer him out for Saka (£6.0m) who plays in the 3pm kick-off, and score points for both. Picking up extra fixtures each time a transfer is made is key to TFF success.



2) Find enablers early and stick



To fit in a combination of Erling Haaland (£8.3m), Bruno Fernandes (£6.5m) and Cole Palmer (£6.2m) or similar, requires TFF managers to find cheaper players to balance teams. Finding those players early into the season, and sticking with them to utilise transfers on the other strategy tips, can ensure avoiding wasting transfers on constant restructuring of squads.



3) FA Cup and League Cup (new for 2025/26)

Players in TFF gain points for the League Cup and FA Cup as well as the Premier League, so often players topping points charts at the season end have progressed far in the competition. When seeing lineups for early League Cup and FA Cup Rounds, if big hitting players who are regulars in the league start against lowly opposition, it’s a prime opportunity to stock up on those assets.

New for this season League Cup fixtures have been included which will make the early stages of the season even more exciting when Premier League teams who are not competing in Europe will gain a fixture against the rest.



4) Favourable fixture runs

Picking players who are playing against weaker opposition often score more points, therefore keeping an eye on the fixtures for teams is important.



5) Balance transfers out over the season

There are ~37 gameweeks in the season, so averaging around one transfer a week is a rule of thumb that keeps managers from running out early. The start of the season is the only time your team is reset, so it’s important to set a structure that works for you so that you don’t need to use too many moves at the start to identify those players who are likely to shine. It’s a marathon, not a sprint, so keeping pace early isn’t a necessity, and often keeping a few extra back until the end run sees TFF managers get a late boost.

News.title: Telegraph Fantasy Football points: a complete guide to scoring
News.content:
How many points for a Goal?

A regular source of goals is often the first thing a manager looks for in a fantasy football team. The highly-priced Erling Haaland is a go-to signing for many, but last season saw the continuation of mid-priced forwards getting in on the action too with the likes of Igor Thiago racking up 22 goals in Telegraph Fantasy Football.

Players get five points per goal scored which, added to starting appearance points (two), mean a regularly starting goal scorer can be a huge asset.



How many points for an Assist?

It won’t take a master tactician to work out that players who rank highly in the goalscoring charts often also feature in the upper echelons of the Assists table.

Bruno Fernandes was head and shoulders above the rest with regard to assist points last season with 21 in total (nine clear of his closest rival).

An assist will earn three points.





What counts as an Assist?

An Assist is the final touch (pass, pass-cum-shot or any other touch) leading to the recipient of the ball scoring a goal.

Outside of fantasy football, if the final touch is deflected by an opposition player, the initiator is only given a goal assist if the receiving player was likely to receive the ball without the deflection having taken place. Own goals, directly taken free kicks, direct corner goals and penalties do not get an assist awarded.

In a change to previous years, Fantasy Assists are not being used.



How many points for a Tackle?

A slightly more nuanced aspect of scoring is the points a player earns for a successful tackle. Managers will need to cast their nets wide to capitalise on tackling points as the highest scorers tend to come from mid-table and even lower-table teams.

Everton’s James Garner was a key beneficiary of tackle bonus points last season with 120 tackles in total. His closest rivals have been very popular this summer with Wolves’ Joao Gomes, now at Aston Villa, and Nottingham Forest’s Elliot Anderson, now at Manchester City. It’s clear from this that deeper lying midfielders are more likely to amass points here.

Players earn a point for every two tackles made during a match and only midfielders are eligible.



What counts as a Tackle?

A tackle is defined as a player connecting with the ball in a ground challenge and successfully taking the ball away from the player in possession. The tackled player must have clearly been in possession of the ball before the tackle was made.

The final destination of the ball (to the tackler, to a teammate, to an opposition player or out of play) is not considered. A tackle will only be deemed unsuccessful if the player tackled retains possession of the ball.

A player cutting out a pass does not count as a tackle.

Players earn a point for every two tackles made.



How many points for a Clean Sheet?

Attainable by goalkeepers and defenders, the top-scorers in the clean sheet category last season mostly came from Arsenal.

There are five clean sheet points on offer for a player who has played at least 60 minutes of a match and two points if the player has played less than an hour where the game has finished with their team conceding zero goals.



How many points for a Save?

In addition to clean sheet points, goalkeepers can earn one point for every two saves made in a match. Much like points for tackling, save points introduce a new angle to team selection with keepers from teams further down the table likely to face more shots than those who generally dominate games. Last season Mark Flekken came out on top with 153 saves for Brentford, so it will be interesting to see how Caoimhin Kelleher gets on this season.



What counts as a Save?



A save is a goalkeeper preventing the ball from entering the goal with any part of his body when facing an intentional attempt to score by an opposition player.

Saves have the following attributes:

Body part: Hands/Feet/Body

Save type: Caught/Collected/Parried Safe/Parried Danger area/Fingertip

Goalkeeper position: Diving/Standing/Reaching/Stooping

News.title: Arsenal lose second successive pre-season friendly after parading Guimaraes
News.content:
Premier League champions Arsenal continue their preparations for the new season as they take on Borussia Dortmund in the Emirates Cup. Arsenal beat Spanish side Athletic Bilbao 3-0 in the 2025 edition, with goals from Viktor Gyokeres, Bukayo Saka and Kai Havertz sealing victory. These sides met during the 2014/15 Champions League group stages, with both games being won 2-0 by the home side.

Arsenal beat Girona 4-1 just over a week ago but fell to a 3-1 defeat to Real Betis in Dublin on Wednesday night. Reflecting on that defeat, Mikel Arteta expressed his frustration at the way his side conceded the goals.

“I am disappointed with the result,” Arteta told Arsenal’s in-house media. “We are here to win football matches. We had some fantastic moments in the first half, the way we played, the way we opened them up. We have to score first, clearly, in the two chances that we had before the score.

“I am very disappointed in the manner that we conceded the first goal, the two giveaways leading to the other two goals. It is true that the finishing quality from them was exceptional, but to win a football match, you have to compete at a different level, especially in those areas of the pitch and that is the learning from today [last Wednesday].”

This is in fact Arsenal’s first game at the Emirates since being crowned Premier League champions, as they sealed the title with a game to spare, with that final match of last season being away at Crystal Palace. After today, Arsenal have two more games, including the Community Shield in a week’s time, before they kick off the defence of their Premier League crown at home against newly-promoted Coventry. The likes of Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Martin Zubimendi are still yet to return after their World Cup exploits.

Dortmund, led by Niko Kovac, finished second in the Bundesliga last season, 16 points off winners Bayern Munich. They have played four pre-season friendlies thus far, winning twice and losing twice. The likes of Karim Adeyemi, Julian Brandt and Niklas Sule have left the club this summer.

Sports.title: Man City boss Enzo Maresca admits the night he sank two England managers in one go is highlight of his playing career
Sports.content:
ENZO MARESCA admits the night he sank two future England managers in one go ranks as the highlight of his playing career.

The new Manchester City boss was part of the Sevilla team who met Steve McClaren’s Middlesbrough in the 2006 Uefa Cup final.



It was the Boro chief’s final game in charge before he left to take the Three Lions job a couple of months later.

His skipper that night in Eindhoven was Gareth Southgate, who stepped up to be Boro boss after McClaren’s departure.



Maresca started the game and scored two late on in a clash that ended 4-0 to the Spaniards.

Former midfielder Maresca, 46, played for 11 clubs over two decades but says that night was one of his most memorable moments.

The Italian recalled: “I got two and I could have had a hat-trick.

“It was a good team. Dani Alves was there and Adriano.

“I remember the Middlesbrough team with Southgate, and McClaren was leaving to go to England.

“Jimmy Floyd Hasselbaink also played and he mentioned the game when we worked together at Chelsea.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

“Scoring twice in that final was a career highlight. Then after, when you win that trophy you play against the team that wins the Champions League in the Super Cup.

“Barcelona had beaten Arsenal 2-1 in Paris so we faced them. Messi was there and we beat them 3-0. And I scored again! So the two European finals probably were the best moments.”

Maresca started out as an AC Milan youth-team player and was sad to hear Rossoneri legend Franco Baresi had passed away, aged 66, last month.

He said: “There was never a central defender like him but it wasn’t just him — that team had Marco van Basten, Ruud Gullit, Frank Rijkaard, Roberto Donadoni, Carlo Ancelotti, Paolo Maldini and Alessandro Costacurta.



“They won the Champions League and it was the best team. Arrigo Sacchi was manager and at that time he changed football like Pep Guardiola did in the last 20 years.”

When he looks back on that golden era in Italian football in the 1990s, he finds it hard to believe his home nation have not made an appearance at the last three World Cups.

Maresca added: “The best players, best manager, the best football was in Italy at that time. But now… three World Cups out.

“Now we don’t produce enough players and there are too many foreign players who are not at a high level — but they are cheap.”

The Brazilian giants confirmed they will NOT renew the 32-year-old’s contract in a bid to protect the club’s “financial health”.



Depay claims he had already agreed a TWO–YEAR extension which had been signed off by the club president and several departments.

And the furious Dutchman has now threatened to take action against Corinthians over what he branded “unacceptable behaviour”.



In his statement on X, the former Man Utd star wrote: “Very disappointed to read that Corinthians decided not to honour our agreement in place to extend my contract for two more years.

This seems to be the beginning of the end for Depay in Sao Paulo after he moved to Brazil nearly two years ago.

Sports.title: Championship club have ‘vomitory’ feature approved for 21,944-seater stadium as council sets stringent condition
Sports.content:
TURF MOOR’s new “vomitory” could soon have Burnley fans pouring in after the council gave it the green light.

The Clarets have been granted permission by Burnley Council to build the new access point at the 4,500 capacity Barnfield Stand.



Despite its peculiar name, a vomitory is just a large passage or staircase designed to quickly funnel crowds in and out of the stadium.

And the word actually comes from the Latin “vomere” that means “to spew forth”.



The new staircase will make it easier for fans heading to the upper section of the stand, while also being an extra fire escape.

Plans state that the all-weather structure will be covered in “sympathetic” black metal cladding – and the inside will feature Burnley’s usual Claret red.

But the Championship side may have to dig a little deeper before they start work with a large layer of coal sitting beneath the stadium.

Burnley Council attached a condition to its approval following consultation with the Coal Mining Authority over concerns about the stability of the ground.

The authority warned: “While the proposed development is a relatively lightweight structure any increased loading could induce further instability of the workings.”

Officials have therefore demanded tests before building begins, they added: “This investigation should comprise a series of at least three boreholes advanced approximately 15m into solid bedrock.”

Sports.title: Netherlands make shock move for ex-Premier League boss after Arne Slot snub
Sports.content:
Netherlands make shock move for ex-Premier League boss after Arne Slot snub

The Netherlands are looking for a new manager after parting company with Ronald Koeman and have found a new contender for the role following failed talks with Arne Slot

View 2 Images Arne Slot walked away from the Netherlands job

Roberto Martinez is in talks to become the next manager of the Netherlands, a month after leaving his role with Portugal. Martinez left Portugal after they were knocked out of the World Cup by Spain in the last 16 - but could be set for a swift return to international management.

‌



The Netherlands parted company with Ronald Koeman after they were knocked out of the World Cup in the last 32 by Morocco in June. The penalty shoot-out exit was a painful way to end the tournament and Koeman stepped down from his second spell in charge.

‌



Arne Slot had appeared heavy favourite to succeed Koeman following his departure from Liverpool at the end of last season. But talks with the KNVB (Royal Dutch Football Association) did not lead to a contract offer.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Cristiano Ronaldo marries Georgina Rodriguez as football icon shares ring picture READ MORE :

Tottenham hold the key to Arsenal transfer after Mikel Arteta changes target READ MORE :

Slot has since explained that he withdrew from the process due to his desire to stay in club football. De Telegraaf now reports that Martinez is in the frame to take over the side.

The 53-year-old started out in club management, with stints at Swansea, Wigan and Everton, but has spent the past decade in international football. He spent six years with Belgium before joining Portugal in 2023.

‌



Martinez led Belgium to third place at the 2018 World Cup and No.1 in the FIFA world rankings, but left after being knocked out in the group stages of the 2022 World Cup. He won the Nations League with Portugal last year before this summer's disappointment in North America.

View 2 Images Roberto Martinez is available after leaving Portugal (Image: Zhizhao Wu/Getty Images)

Despite being criticised for his conservative playing style, it seems he is the KNVB's second choice for the Netherlands gig after Slot ruled himself out.

‌



"Over the past few weeks, and particularly the past few days, various reports have appeared regarding the vacancy at the Dutch national team, suggesting that I had withdrawn from the process after lengthy negotiations, including regarding salary and contract duration," the former Liverpool boss told Voetbal International.

“That speculation is incorrect. We simply never reached that stage of the talks. At this stage of my career, I prefer to see myself on the training pitch with my players every day. Something that is simply not possible in the same way with a national team.

“And (this is) why I chose not to continue the talks and not to start negotiations on what a possible contract might look like. I have enormous respect for the national team and for the KNVB and can only be positive about the professional manner in which the talks proceeded that week.

Article continues below

“For now, I believe that club football still has a lot to offer me. It would be a great honour to represent my country as national coach one day. However, this was not the right moment for me.”

Sports.title: Paul Pogba set to have contract torn up as injured ex-Man Utd star searches for new club
Sports.content:
Paul Pogba set to have contract torn up as injured ex-Man Utd star searches for new club

Paul Pogba is now understood to be on the lookout for a new team, despite reports claiming the ex-Manchester United midfielder was offered a deal

View 3 Images Paul Pogba's future is uncertain (Image: DARREN STAPLES, AFP via Getty Images)

Ex-Manchester United ace Paul Pogba is on the verge of having his contract torn up by Monaco. Last summer, he signed a two-year contract with the European heavyweights.

‌



However, he may be set for a several month long absence after suffering a hamstring injury during Monaco's recent pre-season tour at St George's Park. It's a huge setback for the World Cup winner, having been handed a four-year ban in February 2024, only for it to be successfully appealed and reduced to 18 months.

‌



Last season, he made six appearances for Monaco and was also in the squad for their recent 3-2 pre-season friendly victory over Liverpool. Now it's being reported the deal may be cancelled.

‌



FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

The Athletic understands both club and player are in talks about having his contract mutually terminated. Last summer, he put pen to paper on a two-year deal, before going on to make his first football appearance for 26 months the following November.

Man Utd have clear transfer priority after Myles Lewis-Skelly offer READ MORE :

Man Utd ready to open talks over £30m transfer in perfect response to double blow READ MORE :

In total, Pogba has featured just six times for Monaco, with all of those performances coming in Ligue 1 last season. He was also present at Anfield for his side's 3-2 victory over Liverpool on Sunday.

‌



However, he has been absent throughout Monaco's pre-season due to fitness concerns, and with contract termination talks ongoing, his future at the club looks increasingly uncertain, reports the Manchester Evening News. Last month, Monaco CEO Thiago Scuro cast doubt over Pogba's future, suggesting he could depart this summer.

View 3 Images Pogba mase his first appearance in over two years last season (Image: Eurasia Sport Images, Getty Images)

"Maybe he'll leave, yes, maybe he'll stay here, yes," Scuro told a news conference. "That's [Pogba's future] a very complicated subject because we have a lot of respect for Paul. For the person first of all.

‌



"When he first arrived here he was very positive, he worked, he helped the young players. But the truth is that the project didn't go well last season. When we started this project during the summer, the expectations that we had were different to what happened.

"I think now, we must be fair to him, look at his preparation every week, to see how he has progressed, his physical level, his technical level. And after, that will be a decision for the coach. If the coach decides to give him game time or not. That depends completely on performances. We have the summer to see what Paul's level will be.

View 3 Images Pogba's future has been plunged into more uncertainty (Image: NurPhoto, NurPhoto via Getty Images)

‌



"With Paul, the relationship has always been open, transparent. If, at a certain time, the player's objectives and the club's are different, we have to talk and find a solution. Performance will give all the answers we need."

Pogba, who rose through the academy at United, returned to Old Trafford for £89.3million in 2016 following a stint at Juventus. He subsequently became a key player for Jose Mourinho and Ole Gunnar Solskjaer throughout his six-year second spell with the Reds, racking up more than 200 appearances along the way.

However, Pogba would eventually depart United for a second time in 2022 when his contract ran out, subsequently rejoining Juventus.

Sports.title: Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle offers bleak reality check - 'This is a vacuum'
Sports.content:
Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle offers bleak reality check - 'This is a vacuum'

Newcastle have undergone a major overhaul this summer, with Matthias Jaissle taking over from Eddie Howe as manager and a series of key players leaving in the transfer window

View 3 Images Matthias Jaissle offered a heavy does of realism (Image: Serena Taylor/Newcastle United via Getty Images)

Newcastle manager Matthias Jaissle has tempered expectations around his side this season in his first press conference after taking over from Eddie Howe.

‌



Jaissle has inherited into a tricky situation on Tyneside following a succession of high-profile exits. Howe walked away after nearly five years in the hot seat, while Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimaraes were sold and Kieran Trippier also departed.

‌



Newcastle banked nearly £250million from those transfers, but have opted to sign young unproven players with potential as replacements. Ewen Jaouen, Bazoumana Toure, Sean Steur, Aladji Bamba and Lukas Hornicek have arrived to work under Jaissle.

‌



The 38-year-old German was hired from Al-Ahli and is under no illusions over the task facing him. "We are in that transition phase," he said. "The players who have left were great characters, great players, experienced players. This is now a vacuum.

Tottenham hold the key to Arsenal transfer after Mikel Arteta changes target READ MORE :

"We have to adjust something in the squad by signing these profile of players, or other players need to step up and fill these positions and these leadership roles.

"We are aware of what we need and the squad that we want. Internally, everyone is aware of that, and we are working on the solutions."

‌



Newcastle saw a move for Marseille midfielder Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg fall through recently and remain on the lookout for experience in the transfer window.

The Magpies finished a disappointing 12th in the Premier League last season under Howe and Jaissle has refused to state their ambitions this season. "This will not happen overnight, especially when you now have such a big transition phase," he said.

View 3 Images Newcastle captain Bruno Guimaraes left for Arsenal (Image: David Price/Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

‌



"You need to have a clear goal of where we want to go to. Then, if you have that synergy with the fans, the players and the staff to go there, then I’m pretty sure it will be a successful story. But we need time now. We can only do our best day by day, breaking it down with the goal long ahead.

"We are ambitious. But it makes no sense to promise you anything, because I don’t know how things look in half a year or one year. What we can control, we will control.

"Cutting the tasks down on a daily basis, doing the best job, and then we go in the right direction - and that is going to be successful."

‌



View 3 Images Matthias Jaissle has a rebuilding job on his hands (Image: Serena Taylor/Newcastle United via Getty Images)

Jaissle will be a contrast to the reserved Howe on the touchline, with his animated style likely to come to the fore. "I will not change my style because that's my personality," he said.

"On the touchline, I am emotional, but I need to respect the box [technical area] a bit more. I'm a bit scared. I hope in the beginning the referees can maybe close their eyes here and there a little. I need to learn that.

Article continues below

"I had a long touchline in Saudi Arabia, so I think the GPS would be quite high if I had worn it!"

Sports.title: Tottenham hold the key to Arsenal transfer after Mikel Arteta changes target
Sports.content:
Tottenham hold the key to Arsenal transfer after Mikel Arteta changes target

Arsenal are desperate to sign an experienced defender in the summer transfer window to cover for William Saliba, but have found themselves reliant on Tottenham for help

View 3 Images Mikel Arteta wants defensive reinforcements (Image: Stuart MacFarlane/Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

Arsenal could find themselves frustrated in the transfer market once again after it emerged that they could need a favour from Tottenham to land their latest target.

‌



Mikel Arteta is keen to bring in an experienced defender this summer, to help provide cover for William Saliba, who will miss the start of the season due to a back injury picked up at the World Cup. They have identified Aston Villa's Ezri Konsa as an option, but his £60million valuation and competition from Liverpool complicates things.

‌



The Gunners have therefore turned their attention to Barcelona defender Jules Kounde, according to reports in Spain. The France international is capable of playing at right-back or centre-back, so would offer tactical flexibility to Arteta.

‌



Sport says Arsenal are monitoring Kounde, who still has four years left on his Barca contract so wouldn't come cheap. It is said that the process has 'stalled' currently, partly due to Kounde's reluctance to leave the Catalan club.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Tottenham could hand Arsenal major transfer boost after opening Folarin Balogun talks READ MORE :

However, Barca reportedly would consider a 'multi-million euro' sale because they need funds to revamp their backline. Hansi Flick's side, who have just loaned out Ronald Araujo to Liverpool, are said to be sounding out possible arrivals should Kounde leave.

‌



Their top target in that eventuality is Tottenham right-back Pedro Porro, whose stock is extremely high after helping Spain win the World Cup. But this is where Arsenal's chances of landing Kounde get even more remote.

Porro recently signed a new contract with Spurs until June 2031 and is a key player for manager Roberto De Zerbi, who has no intention of letting him go. It remains to be seen whether the 26-year-old could have his head turned by Barcelona if they step up their pursuit.

View 3 Images Jules Kounde is a target for Arsenal (Image: Jose Breton/Getty Images)

‌



"Pedro is a very important player for us, who has consistently shown his ability to influence matches in both defensive and attacking situations," De Zerbi said after Porro signed a new deal in June.

"As well as his technical quality, I also love his mentality. Every day he wants to work, to learn and to improve, and these are the characteristics that help players reach the highest level."

Arsenal have already been frustrated in their failure to land Vinicius Junior, who used their interest to negotiate a new contract with Real Madrid. The Gunners have therefore been forced to look for alternatives in attack, with Atletico Madrid striker Julian Alvarez the dream signing.

‌



View 3 Images Pedro Porro's stock is very high after the World Cup (Image: John Todd/Getty Images)

Asked if fans could expect further signings this summer following the £75m capture of Bruno Guimaraes, Arteta replied: "Well that's what we're trying to do. If we have the right player in the market to make us much better, we are very looking forward to that."

Arsenal's defence has been leaky in pre-season, but Arteta has insisted that hasn't increased their desire to sign a defender. "I wouldn't go there just to put it isolated there," Arteta said after losing to Borussia Dortmund

Article continues below

"We conceded some poor goals the other day, some poor goals today. In the way we competed, especially. But that's a very collective responsibility. So we need to improve with the players that we have. And we want to improve for sure."

Sports.title: Man Utd urged to complete 'no brainer' seventh summer signing 'they can't say no to'
Sports.content:
Man Utd urged to complete 'no brainer' seventh summer signing 'they can't say no to'

Michael Carrick has been told that landing one particular midfielder this summer is paramount to Manchester United's success

View 2 Images Manchester United have been urged to sign the Premier League star (Image: (Image Photo Agency/Getty Images))

Manchester United have been urged to pursue the signing of Fulham star Sander Berge because of his similarities to Rodri. While a move for the Manchester City talisman is borderline impossible, especially as he nears a transfer to Barcelona, acquiring the Norway international is the next best thing, according to United icon Paul Parker.

‌



Michael Carrick, 45, has already welcomed Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos in his plan to overhaul United's midfield. United have also brought in Karl Darlow, Tynan Thompson, Kit Margetson and Cristian Orozco.

‌



A possible deal to sign a third midfielder has not been ruled out, with Parker stating it makes sense to go for Berge, who is set to enter his third season with the Cottagers.

‌



Not shy to throw glowing praise on the 28-year-old, the former England full-back claimed Berge's potential impact on United's midfield could be as influential as the role Rodri has had at the Etihad Stadium.

Speaking to PariuriX.com, Parker said: "I have seen that Sander Berge has been mentioned. I like him a lot. He is very steady and plays in a similar way to Rodri, even though he is still far from his level.

"Sander Berge is a very positive player. Very rarely gives the ball away and he is excellent at controlling the midfield. He is a big guy and everything about him looks great. I totally get why the club might be looking at him.

‌



Jose Mourinho admits his family have a better time when he's not around READ MORE :

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

"He is always playing games as well. He is never injured, which I really like because it adds some continuity to the team." Berge has yet to make the giant step in his footballing career, having begun his journey in England with Sheffield United before moving to Burnley and now finding himself at Fulham.

However, Parker has noted the midfielder's career choices as "positive", praising the incremental steps he's taken rather than moving to a bigger club too early. He explained: "He was excellent during the World Cup as well but I am not surprised because he always plays very well.

Sports.title: Man Utd have made six signings, let 14 players leave and could still secure seven transfers
Sports.content:
Man Utd have made six signings, let 14 players leave and could still secure seven transfers

Manchester United have continued their high level of activity in the summer transfer window

View 9 Images Michael Carrick is making moves in the transfer window (Image: Michael Campanella/Getty Images)

Michael Carrick has been busy building his Manchester United squad for the upcoming 2026/27 season, with a number of transfers heading in and out of Old Trafford. The new club confirmed his permanent stay as manager towards the end of last season, following a successful stint in temporary charge since January.

‌



A number of stars have returned for pre-season training already, including out-of-favour winger Marcus Rashford. The 28-year-old is said to be "excited" to work under the ex-United captain next season, with The Athletic reporting that the academy graduate is looking forward to the upcoming campaign.

‌



The likes of Casemiro and Jadon Sancho have exited the building in Manchester following the expiry of their contracts, with 12 more also no longer at Old Trafford. But with the Premier League season beginning on August 22 against Hull City, Carrick will be keen to bring more stars in quickly.

‌



Here, Mirror Football has detailed the current state of play at Old Trafford right now.

Who have Man Utd signed so far?

Andrey Santos was the first signing of the Carrick era, joining from Chelsea for a £50 million fee. The midfielder has been a constant presence in United's pre-season fixtures and is confident he can replace Casemiro as the No. 6 this season.

‌



Speaking after the 1-1 draw with Paris Saint-Germain, Santos said: "I prefer playing deep like a number six. I try help my teammates without the ball and with the ball I love breaking the lines. For me Casemiro is a legend. Now he's gone and I'm here. I feel that I can do like Casemiro did last season."

View 9 Images Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans have joined United this summer (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Goalkeeper Karl Darlow was next to join the squad, leaving Leeds on a free transfer and heading to Old Trafford. Aston Villa's Youri Tielemans was the second midfielder to hop on the Carrick train, with United exercising the £35m release clause to sign the 29-year-old.

‌



Youth signings Tynan Thompson and Kit Margetson also joined from Tottenham and Swansea City, respectively. United most recently secured Cristian Orozco from Fortaleza CEIF, with the 18-year-old midfielder joining the United academy to gain experience in England.

Who has left Man Utd?

View 9 Images Sancho and Casemiro's salaries are now off the wage bill (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

A whopping 14 players have left United this summer, including a few big names on the wage bill. Casemiro joined Inter Miami on a free transfer, taking £350,000 off the weekly salary output.

‌



Jadon Sancho, Tyrell Malacia and Malachi Sharpe have all left upon the expiry of their contracts and are without a club for the time being. Radek Vitek recently joined Middlesbrough, with reports claiming that an initial fee of £7m had been agreed, which could double if performance bonuses are met.

In terms of loans, Solomon Honor has moved to Southport, Sekou Kone has arrived at Lausanne-Sport and Andre Onana returned to Trabzonspor for a second temporary spell. Altay Bayindir joined Celta Vigo on loan earlier this week and Elyh Harrison headed north to spend the season at Greenock Morton.

Sonny Aljofree has moved to Rotherham United on a free transfer, with James Bailey heading to Stockport County in a similar deal. Tyler Fredricson has ended his eight-year association with United by joining Lausanne-Sport on a permanent deal in Switzerland.

‌



View 9 Images Rasmus Hojlund has left Manchester for Napoli (Image: Ciro De Luca/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

Finally, Rasmus Hojlund joined Napoli following a successful loan in Italy. The Serie A side had a £38m obligation-to-buy clause, provided they qualified for the Champions League.

This was achieved after they finished second in the 2025/26 campaign, and Hojlund confirmed his move by scoring against Pisa to secure the European spot. Writing on Instagram in May, the Denmark international said: "This goal felt symbolic because it means two things. We now secured Champions League with Napoli, which means because of my contract I’m now officially a Napoli player and I’m saying goodbye to Manchester United.

‌



"My childhood dream came true by playing at Old Trafford in a red jersey. So the goal today symbolises a new confident start, in which I will give everything for the time ahead to Napoli, and a thank you to all the fans, players and staff of Manchester United who made the dream I had as a kid come true. It’s time for new dreams, so let’s chase them."

Seven transfers that can still be done

View 9 Images United are keen to bring Louis Page to Old Trafford (Image: Plumb Images/Leicester City FC via Getty Images)

‌



More transfers could still be achieved at United, with potentially three more incoming and four heading out the exit door. The Red Devils are currently working on a deal to bring Louis Page to the club.

The Leicester City midfielder has become an impressive talent despite his club's relegation to League One. The 18-year-old was named EFL Apprentice of the Year and has already made 21 senior appearances so far.

BBC Sport reports that talks are ongoing, with Aston Villa and Arsenal also interested, but United are the frontrunners in the transfer conversation. The club are also looking at fullbacks to bolster their defensive department with Jorge Salinas emerging as a target.

‌



Previous reports have claimed that the left-back is regarded as a huge talent and could provide United with a long-term plan to replace Luke Shaw. Racing Santander sporting director Chema Aragon has made it clear that clubs will have to reach their £13.7m release clause if they plan to sign the defender, adding: "There is nothing we can do if a big star appears."

9 View 9 Images Jorge Salinas has been linked (Image: Juan Manuel Serrano Arce/Getty Images) 9 View 9 Images Lewis Hall is still a huge target for Carrick (Image: Ed Sykes/Getty Images)

‌



Lewis Hall remains the primary target for United, but Newcastle are adamant the 21-year-old is not for sale. The transfers of Sandro Tonali, Anthony Gordon and Bruno Guimaraes have prompted the Magpies to close ranks and try to keep their remaining key stars at St James' Park this summer.

Myles Lewis-Skelly could be one alternative who can provide proven Premier League experience in place of Hall, with United being offered the opportunity to sign the 19-year-old this week. Following the arrival of Bruno Guimaraes, the Gunners have opened up to the prospect of selling the young star this summer.

Lewis-Skelly can operate as a full-back as well as a midfielder and could be a versatile addition to Carrick's squad. One more midfielder is expected to arrive, with Manu Kone also having been strongly linked with a move to Old Trafford during this window.

‌



Reports suggest that the Roma star has emerged as a midfield target, and Corriere dello Sport claims that personal terms have been agreed. However, the Serie A side will reportedly demand up to £51m (€60m) for his services.

9 View 9 Images Myles Lewis-Skelly has emerged as a shock transfer opportunity (Image: Marc Atkins/Getty Images) 9 View 9 Images Lamine Camara has been linked with United (Image: Simon Stacpoole/Offside/Offside via Getty Images)

‌



Lamine Camara has also been linked with United as a possible alternative, with The Standard reporting that he will cost at least £42.7m (€50m). With Page looking likely to be an academy addition, another midfielder and a left-back could wrap up United's summer incoming business.

But with this amount potentially coming in, Carrick will look to offload some stars this summer. Toby Collyer has interest from a number of Championship sides with The Athletic reporting that a loan or permanent move is possible.

Harry Amass is also a subject of transfer interest despite featuring heavily during United's pre-season tour of Europe. It is reported that the club are open to a transfer if the left-back's £6m fee is met, but a loan could also be on the cards.

Article continues below

Joshua Zirkzee has been continuously connected to Juventus in recent months. The Serie A side are considering a loan with obligation to buy, as per The Athletic, with other clubs said to be interested in the striker. Ethan Wheatley is being monitored by Everton currently to bolster their under-21 set-up.

Sports.title: Jodar on course for tennis history as Rybakina fights past Osaka
Sports.content:
Spanish teenager Rafael Jodar is on course to break the record for the fastest rise into the top 10 of men's tennis after beating Arthur Filis in the quarter-finals of the Canadian Open.

Jodar came out on top in a rain-affected contest on Tuesday to win 7-6 (7-5) 6-3 to ensure he will move up to at least 11th in the ATP rankings, having started the year in 165th.

The 19-year-old will face American Brandon Nakashima in the semi-finals on Wednesday night, live on Sky Sports Tennis, where victory could see him smash Boris Becker's current record of 210 days to go from breaking the top 100 to being in the top 10. Jodar would do it in just 140 days.

However, Jodar also requires defending Canadian Open champion Ben Shelton to lose to Learner Tien in the other semi-final.

Shelton, a two-time Grand Slam semi-finalist, swept out Jakub Mensík in straight sets 6-3 6-1 in 72 minutes and is yet to drop a set in this tournament.

Image: Ben Shelton is the defending Canadian Open champion (Christinne Muschi/The Canadian Press via AP)

Should Jodar and Shelton meet in Thursday's final, a win for Jodar would also see him move into the top 10 and make history.

"I played a very high level against a tough player like Arthur," said Jodar after beating Filis.

"I had to give my best to win this match. It worked perfectly, staying calm in those important moments of the match, those pressure moments."

Image: Rafael Jodar (left) reached the quarter-finals at the French Open earlier this year (Christinne Muschi/The Canadian Press via AP)

Rybakina battles back to beat Osaka

Elena Rybakina rallied back after losing the opening set to defeat 11th-seed Naomi Osaka 4-6 7-6 (7-5) 6-4 and advance to the semi-finals of the WTA Canadian Open in Toronto.

Osaka came flying out of the blocks by breaking in the opening game which was enough to win the first set, before both players twice exchanged breaks in the second which Rybakina won on a tie-break.

The Kazakh made the decisive break in the seventh game of the last set and went on to win arguably the match of the tournament.

Image: Elena Rybakina would be just four ranking points behind Aryna Sabalenka if she wins the Montreal title (Julian Avram/Icon Sportswire/AP)

"Super happy. It was a very difficult match. In the first set [I made] a few mistakes, a poor start," said Rybakina, who could overtake Aryna Sabalenka as world No 1 later this month.

"It was a really tough one but I'm glad I could turn it around, I don't yet know how, but I think my serve helped me a little bit."

Rybakina will play Coco Gauff in the semi-finals after the American received a walkover in her quarter-final when her opponent Belinda Bencic withdrew due to a hip injury.

The other semi-final sees Iga Swiatek take on Elina Svitolina for a place in Thursday's final.
