However, in an interview with Marca last year, the Portuguese admitted he hadn't yet married Georgina because he hadn't felt the 'click'.

He said: 'I always tell her, "when we get that click". Like everything with our life, and she knows what I'm talking about.

'It could be in a year or it could be in six months or it could be in a month. I'm 1000 per cent sure that it'll happen.'

In August, the footballer finally popped the question with a giant diamond ring.

Fans speculated the pair got engaged the month before after the model shared pictures of a bridal-themed dinner, complete with 'C heart G' pillows, a six-piece band and stunning white flower arrangements.

She also wore a giant sparkler on her wedding ring finger, hinting at the pair's secret engagement.

Georgina gleefully shared the news on Instagram with a photo of her glitzy engagement ring. 'Yes I do. In this and in all my lives,' she wrote in a heartfelt caption.

Cristiano then revealed that two of his children inspired him to give Georgina a 'not-so romantic' and off-the-cuff proposal.

He revealed that he didn't plan to propose to the 'woman of his life' the night they got engaged, but it felt like the 'right time'.

'It was like 1am. My daughters were in bed sleeping,' the 41-year-old told Piers Morgan in part one of their new interview.

He said: 'One of my friends gave me the ring to offer Gio (Georgina) and as I was giving her the ring, my two kids come in and say "Daddy, you're going to give the ring to mum and you're going to ask her to get married."

'I said, "Wow, this is the right moment to say yes." It was the time. I knew that I was going to do it one day but I hadn't planned to do it then.

Cristiano met Georgina in 2016 after he saw her in the Gucci store where she was working

'Because my daughters said that and my friends were filming, it was what I wanted and I offered (the ring). I didn't (get on one knee) because I wasn't prepared but it was a beautiful moment. I made a speech.

'It was simple, I'm not a very romantic guy. Well, I am, but I'm not very romantic, not the kind of guy who brings flowers every week to the home. But I'm romantic in my way. It was beautiful and I knew that it's the woman of my life so I did that and I hope that I did it well.'

Asked about when they plan to tie the knot, the footballer joked: 'Not yet. We plan to do it after the World Cup with the trophy! But she is not the person that likes big parties. She doesn't like it. She likes private things. So I will respect these decisions.

'One thing that I love, she didn't care about the ring. She asked me if I was honest and I said, "I want you and I want to marry you." I didn't cry but I had tears on my eyes.'

Experts estimated that Cristiano splashed out an astonishing £1.5million on Georgina's engagement ring.

Sports.title: These are the key clues Matthias Jaissle gave away at Newcastle unveiling - from the signings he wants to how he will turn this club around, writes CRAIG HOPE
Sports.content:
These are the key clues Matthias Jaissle gave away at Newcastle unveiling - from the signings he wants to how he will turn this club around, writes CRAIG HOPE

Unlock more from Craig Hope inside the Newcastle camp with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight, analysis and more

There was no mass of fans on the St James’ Park steps and very little fanfare inside Matthias Jaissle’s Newcastle United unveiling.

For a club who want to be among the world's best by 2030, this was an understated arrival for a head coach whose contract takes us through to that date. He is, by that logic, the man the Newcastle hierarchy believe can lead them to the top.

Not that there was any talk of Champions League and Premier League titles here, or questions about signing Kylian Mbappe, as there was at the outset of the Saudi project nearly five years ago. Veteran midfielder Pierre Emile-Hojbjerg, 31, has been the No1 target in recent days.

Rather, this was something of a reality check, and that is no reflection on Jaissle. The German spoke with enthusiasm and intelligence, and he did so alone. There was no sign of chairman Yasir Al-Rumayyan or hierarchy on stage with the 38-year-old. No global media, either. This is where Newcastle are at right now, and Jaissle appears smart enough to know what he is walking into – a club where the best players and manager have not long walked out.

His demeanour was one of excitement, composure and, a word he sought to stress more than once, optimism. There is a believable authority about him. But beneath the positivity was a more subtle message. He needs new players. And he needs time.

Sources have suggested Jaissle is already well aware of what the squad he has inherited lacks – leadership and depth of quality in key areas. You took note when he was asked about the departures of senior players and responded by referencing a leadership ‘vacuum’. He is right, too.

There was no mass of fans on the St James’ Park steps and very little fanfare inside Matthias Jaissle’s Newcastle United unveiling

Sources have suggested Jaissle is already well aware of what the squad he has inherited lacks – leadership and depth of quality in key areas

So, with Bruno Guimaraes now in north London, does he have a new captain yet? ‘No,’ came the reply. And that was that.

His answer when asked what remit the board had given him for this season was equally revealing, given Eddie Howe and the club made no secret of their expectation of European qualification last term, which ended in 12th place in the Premier League.

‘(The remit) is that we are ambitious, but this will not happen overnight, especially when you have such a big transition phase now,’ he said. ‘It makes no sense to promise you anything, because I don’t know how things look in half a year or one year. What we can control, we will control. Cutting the tasks down on a daily basis, doing the best job, and then we go in the right direction - and that is going to be successful.’

Transition was another word he used repeatedly. In fact, the Newcastle 2.0 that chief executive David Hopkinson has spoken about post-Howe feels, at this moment, more like Newcastle 1.5. Less than two weeks out from the visit of Liverpool in the Premier League opener, Jaissle has no fit full backs, while the experienced midfielder he craves appears no closer to arriving.

‘We are aware of what we need and the squad that we want,’ he said. ‘Internally, everyone is aware of that, and we are working on the solutions.’

There are talks over a deal for Benfica right back Amar Dedic, but he is another who has never played in England. It is not hard to understand why 97-cap Denmark midfielder Hojbjerg, with more than 250 Premier League appearances at Southampton and Tottenham, was seen by Jaissle as the kind of foundation around which a younger team could be rebuilt. The Marseille midfielder, however, has opted against the move. The optics of Newcastle 1.5 are not the easiest sell.

Because when the target of ‘consolidation’ was put to the manager of this Saudi-owned club at his first press conference – and it did not sound ridiculous or provoke a challenge – it told you plenty about the task in front of him. For that, he deserves patience.

‘It's a big challenge,’ he said. ‘It always is when there's a transition period, but it's not the time to complain. It doesn't make sense to see the negative. We want to see the chance in the situation.’

There are talks over a deal for Benfica right back Amar Dedic (left), but he is another who has never played in England

It is not hard to understand why Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg (right) was seen by Jaissle as the kind of foundation around which a younger team could be rebuilt

You suspect Jaissle's demonstrative touchline presence will endear him to Newcastle supporters, if not those of the opposition

There is another challenge for Jaissle – keeping himself out of the stands. Although you suspect a demonstrative touchline presence will endear him to Newcastle supporters, if not those of the opposition.

At times in Valencia during his first game on Saturday night, it looked like he was making overlapping runs beyond right winger Anthony Elanga. Indeed, he has already asked club staff how many bookings a manager is allowed before they serve a touchline ban, and he returned a hesitant laugh when informed it was just three.

‘I will not change my style because that's my personality,’ said the former Al Hilal boss. ‘On the touchline, I am emotional. But I need to respect the technical box a bit more. I had a long line in Saudi Arabia, so I think my GPS would be quite high! I'm a bit scared. I hope in the beginning the referees can maybe close their eyes here and there a little!’

There were other flashes of levity, too, including mention of the song which the Toon Army bestowed on him in Spain – ‘Jaissle, I can boogie’ to the tune of Baccara’s Yes Sir, I Can Boogie. ‘I heard it once and I was smiling,’ he said. ‘The guys around me, all the staff members, said they're really looking forward to sitting after a match in the bar and listening to the song. So let's see about that.’

To sit in the bar and be serenaded will need wins. To get those wins, at least on a consistent enough basis to make a success of his debut season, will need more players of greater experience and quality. He knows that. Maybe it is, then, that a low-key introduction was what was necessary. There is no need for Jaissle to boogie just yet. First, he needs a team to dance with.

Sports.title: GORDON MILNE interview: Coventry's golden age and all the 'daft' schemes of Jimmy Hill, growing up with Bill Shankly, learning from Tom Finney, Japan with Gary Lineker... and how he nearly replaced Shankly as Liverpool manager
Sports.content:
GORDON MILNE interview: Coventry's golden age and all the 'daft' schemes of Jimmy Hill, growing up with Bill Shankly, learning from Tom Finney, Japan with Gary Lineker... and how he nearly replaced Shankly as Liverpool manager

Unlock more of the best of our journalism with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight and the writers you love every day

Coventry City were the epitome of fresh thinking and pioneering change when they last broke the surface at the top of English football.

They had been powered to promotion in 1967 with sky blue trains and buses for fans and their players slid behind the wheels of pristine sky blue Rover cars and drove them into Europe on summer tours to blend the city's industrial heritage and fanbase with its flourishing football team. They went on at the vanguard when it came to shirt sponsorship and creative kit designs, all-seater stadiums and electric scoreboards.

And their gravity-defying refusal to kowtow to football's old-world order and simply disappear again prompted jokes that if the Titanic had been painted sky blue it would never have gone down. Coventry remained afloat in the top flight for 34 years and Gordon Milne, the manager for nine of them from 1972, traces all of that back to the influence of Jimmy Hill.

'There was a culture there and it was created by Jimmy,' says Milne, 89 years old and delighted to see Coventry back in the Premier League after 25 years of exile.

'He was a clever guy, intelligent enough to see where football was going. A humble guy, which surprises some people. A lot of people didn't like Jimmy. He'd tell me when he was on Match of the Day how he received thousands of letters telling him to eff off. He used to say his unpopularity kept him in the job.

'At Coventry, he put himself about, went into the factories and connected with people. He loved Coventry and he loved football.'

When Coventry were last promoted to the top flight in 1967 they stayed afloat for 34 years, with nine of them under the management of Gordon Milne

Milne attributes a lot of the success to Jimmy Hill, who led the club from the third tier to the top flight before resigning on the eve of the new season to take a job in television

Hill had been manager of Coventry for six years from 1961. The club was in the third tier when he arrived, and he led them to two promotions before a shock announcement on the eve of their debut season in the old Division One that he intended to quit for a job as head of sport at London Weekend Television.

He certainly knew the future of football would be tied closely to television. When Hill returned in 1975 as managing director and later chairman, Milne was manager and Ron Wylie was his assistant.

'People thought we wouldn't last five minutes once Jimmy was back,' he says. 'We were scratching about near the wrong end of the table with all the journalists writing us off for relegation. Then Jimmy says he wants to meet for a working breakfast. We'd never heard of a working breakfast. Ron, a Glaswegian, says, "Well, that's it, we're on our way".

'It was in a period when Jimmy had investments in developing football in Saudi Arabia and he said, "I want you to help me find a coach". We got talking and the conversation moved onto the salary, which was more than a hundred grand a year and probably about three or four times what I was earning.

'I just remember Ron going: "How much!" Then he said: "We'll do it." And Jimmy laughed and said: "Oh no, no, no… you two are going nowhere." And he knew what he was saying. He knew there had been speculation. That meant a lot to us.'

Bill McGarry, former Ipswich Town and Wolverhampton Wanderers boss, got the lucrative job in charge of Saudi Arabia.

Milne thrived alongside Hill's energy and fearless ambition, unearthing gems in the transfer market, blooding young players alongside carefully selected veterans. In the distinctive Admiral kit, Coventry came seventh in 1977-78. The brown away kit, now portrayed as a cult classic, was rarely worn.

'We hardly won in it,' says Milne. 'The fans were saying it was jinxed but again Admiral came on the scene and wanted to do something different and we were up for it. I only wish I'd kept some of those shirts.'

Milne poses at the launch of the now cult classic brown Admiral kit of the late 1970s

Alongside assistant Ron Wylie (bottom row, fourth from left) with the Coventry squad at the start of the 1975-76 season

Pictured here with Sir Bobby Charlton (left) and Bobby Moore (right), Milne was part of the provisional England 1966 World Cup squad but did not make Sir Alf Ramsey's final cut

Coventry were ahead of their time, and the team was free-scoring, featuring favourites from the era such as winger Tommy Hutchison, a former team-mate of Milne's at Blackpool, and the duo of Mick Ferguson and Ian Wallace up front.

'I always thought if you could score 60 goals you wouldn't be relegated,' says Milne, whose team made a serious effort to beat Nottingham Forest to sign Trevor Francis from Birmingham in Britain's first million-pound transfer in 1979.

'We were very close to signing Trevor. I knew him from the days working with England Under 18s and one of my best pals was Jim Smith, who was manager at Birmingham and absolutely loved Jimmy Hill, so we were in and ready to pay a million for him. It didn't quite work out and going to Forest was the right decision for Trevor, but Jimmy's thinking was, "I'll get Trevor".'

In his study, a shimmering trove of memorabilia, Milne rummages through desk drawers and piles of photographs as he reminisces, pulls books from the shelves and flips through the pages to confirm his recall.

He has a wealth of knowledge accrued from a stellar career which began playing at Preston alongside Tom Finney.

'The best player I've ever seen,' says Milne. 'Outside right, outside left, centre forward, two great feet. He had the art of moving the ball in a flash and shielding it with his body. He'd done it before you knew he was doing it.

'Strong, good in the air. Played through injury. I always picture him on the old treatment room with its immaculate wooden floors, and he'd be on the table, legs black and blue, bruises everywhere and the gaffer would say, "What about tomorrow Tom?" and he'd say, "I'll be OK". Top guy.'

Milne's father Jimmy played for Preston in the pre-war years with Bill Shankly. Both Scottish, their families lived in the same street. As a boy, if Milne Jr ever went outside to kick a ball against the wall, he found Shankly was soon out there kicking it with him.

Bill Shankly (centre) and Bob Paisley (furthest left) attend to Milne (second right) and his Liverpool team-mates on the treatment table

Shankly directs the tactics board in 1963 before an FA Cup quarter-final against West Ham

So perhaps it was no surprise then that Shankly made him one of his first signings as Liverpool boss, in 1960. Two years later, they were drawn in the FA Cup fifth round to play against Preston, where Milne's father had returned as manager.

After two goalless draws, Peter Thompson scored the winner for Preston in a second replay. A year later, Shankly signed Thompson from North End as well. In 1964 his team won the title, a year later the FA Cup and a year later another title. Liverpool would never be the same again.

'What Shanks did at Liverpool was similar to what Jimmy did at Coventry,' says Milne. 'They were both genuine. Jimmy might throw some daft ideas around but he didn't bulls***. They believed in him in Coventry, in the way they believed in Shanks in Liverpool.

'He connected with the people and talked about them. We were doing it for them. Shanks always used to say, "Listen to them". At quarter to three, he would open the dressing room door and say, "The doors have been closed since quarter past two, we can't get another body in the place, how can you let them down? You can't let them down".

'That would be his team talk and when the music scene got going and The Beatles and Gerry and the Pacemakers came on the scene, he built on that. Liverpool was the place to be.'

Milne was considered as a replacement when Shankly quit in 1974. In his second season at Coventry, before the teams met at Highfield Road, he was in conversation with Shankly's assistant Bob Paisley, a man of few words who nodded towards the Liverpool team and said: 'This is a job for you, son.'

Paisley's words made more sense when Shankly quit at the end of the season and Milne was invited to meet Liverpool chairman John Smith and secretary Peter Robinson at a hotel in Manchester.

'What I should've said, that I never said, was that I'd love the job and would've walked up the M6 for it, and that if I got it, I'd want Bob as my right-hand man,' says Milne. 'Bob could read a game. He was brilliant. Perfect for Shanks. They were the perfect combination and Shanks listened to him. He'd pretend he didn't, but he did.

Winning the FA Cup at Wembley in 1965 (Milne pictured centre in tracksuit)

Milne (bottom row, third from left) with the 1966-67 Liverpool team, captained by Ron Yeats, and their First Division and Charity Shield titles

'The worry for Bob was being the No1 man. He didn't want the publicity. Bob took it, but he didn't want it.'

Milne's book, published by Pitch in 2023, was titled Shankly, My Dad and Me. He had sought Shankly's advice when he was offered the Coventry job.

Milne, then in charge of non-League Wigan, was interviewed by Coventry chairman Derrick Robbins on the backseat of his Rolls-Royce. Robbins wanted to recreate Joe Mercer's success with Malcolm Allison at Manchester City by bringing in Mercer as general manager and Milne as manager, in what today we would recognise as the roles of director of football and head coach.

Shankly summoned Milne to Blackpool, where he was on his summer holiday.

The Liverpool boss, wearing pyjamas and with his face smothered in Vaseline, answered the door to his hotel room and invited Milne to step inside before asking only one question: 'Do they want Milne or do they want Mercer?'

Milne explained that Coventry wanted both. 'Aye, but do they want Milne or do they want Mercer?' repeated Shankly.

Milne said he believed they wanted Milne. 'Take it then,' advised Shankly, then asked him to leave because his wife Nessie was sleeping next door.

Milne spent a decade at Highfield Road, the final year as director of football before leaving in 1982 for Leicester, where he won promotion and unearthed another prolific strike partnership in Alan Smith and Gary Lineker in his ongoing quest for 60 goals a season.

Milne and Coventry general manager Joe Mercer greet the team ahead of the 1972-73 season

At his unveiling as Besiktas director of football in 2005, after a highly successful period as manager when he led the club to three consecutive titles from 1990 to 1992

When Coventry won the FA Cup in 1987, the only major trophy of their 143-year existence, he was moving to Istanbul, where he guided Besiktas to a hat-trick of Turkish titles. They did not lose as they won the third and Milne is a legend there.

Lineker lured him to Nagoya Grampus Eight in Japan for a year before a return to Turkish football and a spell as Newcastle's director of football with Sir Bobby Robson.

Coventry though has always been close to his heart and he is proud of his part in the legacy. 'Nine years and we didn't get relegated,' he says. 'You couldn't say that's the objective at the start of every season but over those nine seasons, look at who went down. Some big ones went.'

Among them Manchester United, Chelsea twice and Tottenham. And, like many others, Milne was thrilled when Frank Lampard led the Sky Blues once more into the Premier League.

'Frank has done a great job,' says Milne. 'He has done it all as a player, knows his football and has strong contacts. It looks like they want to play for him and that's important. And he has connected with the fans. It's great to see them back.'

Now to see if they can defy gravity all over again.

Sports.title: Britain's new golden girl: Cambridge English Grad-turned sprinter Amy Hunt who went to Margaret Thatcher's old school wins 100m at European Athletics Championships
Sports.content:
See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

She became the fastest woman in Europe on Monday night, when she won a gold medal for sprinting 100m in 11 seconds.

Yet that's not the only honour Amy Hunt, 24, has earned - with a degree in English Literature from the University of Cambridge under her belt too.

And although she is a fellow old girl of the same grammar school as fellow high-achiever Margaret Thatcher, she has also retained the ability to very much let her hair down.

For despite reaching the pinnacles of success on the track and the classroom, her social media accounts are full of pictures of her enjoying more than the odd glass of wine.

Miss Hunt said after winning the women's 100m final at the European Athletics Championships in Birmingham on Monday: 'I want it all, and I think I'm someone who doesn't shy away from what she knows she can do.

'I knew I could come away with a gold coming into the day.

'I had such a big premonition, and I just love my job. This is what makes it the best.

'My first gold. I think it was definitely time for an upgrade.'

Miss Hunt, who evidently enjoys a night out, poses while watching a Taylor Swift concert

She then studied at Corpus Christi college, Cambridge - financing her studies with earnings from track events and sponsors

Glasses of wine are a regular fixture on Miss Hunt's social media feeds

She also finds the time between training sessions to carefully curate her warbrobe

Miss Hunt poses with a bottle of wine during her Cambridge years

It was Miss Hunt's first gold after winning the women's 100m final at the European Athletics Championships in Birmingham

Miss Hunt, 5ft10ins, had previously won English Schools races at the Birmingham track, but her gold is her first major victory. It makes her a big hope for 2028 Olympics in Los Angeles. She is actually considered better at 200m.

Raised in Newark, she attended Mrs Thatcher's grammar, Kesteven and Grantham Girls' School, like the former Premier studying chemistry at A Level. She played cello too.

Miss Hunt then studied at Corpus Christi college, Cambridge - financing her studies with earnings from track events and sponsors.

Upon graduating two years ago she joked: 'I just got one degree hotter.'

She had herself into student social events too, posing in a party dress and with a bottle of wine for one picture.

Miss Hunt has also repeatedly posed with glasses of wine and other drinks in sun-baked squares and in a bikini in an infinity pool.

She currently lives and trains a 20-minute train ride from Venice - and is feasting her eyes on Italian art.

The Renaissance woman said last year her current motto is 'Medals before men', but was not down about it, adding: 'My two little legs have left me living the life of my dreams.'

Sports.title: Paul Pogba 'set to have Monaco contract ripped up after suffering injury' in latest blow to troubled ex-Man United star
Sports.content:
Paul Pogba's Monaco contract is 'set to be terminated' after the 33-year-old suffered a fresh injury.

The French World Cup winner and former Manchester United star had been trying to revive his career following a doping ban.

But his time at Monaco in Ligue 1 has been disastrous and pre-season this summer was seen by the club as crucial in determining whether he could contribute.

He played 45 minutes in one game before a recurrence of a knee injury last season kept him out of four matches.

And now he has collapsed in severe pain in his leg during a training session, accelerating Monaco's decision to terminate his contract, according to L'Equipe and Nicemartin.com.

Pogba only returned to training last week but sustained the thigh injury in a small-sided game and was scheduled for an MRI this week.

Paul Pogba is set to have his contract at Monaco terminated after suffering an injury

The club will now try and reach an agreement with Pogba and his representatives over paying out his deal, which expires next summer.

Daily Mail Sport understands he was offered to MLS clubs in America on Tuesday.

Pogba - who earned £290,000-per-week in his second spell at Man United - is reportedly earning below £44,000-per-week at Monaco.

Pogba was allowed back into football in March 2025 after his doping ban was reduced on appeal.

He had already left Juventus after having that contract terminated by mutual consent in December 2024.

Monaco was his route back into the game but he only managed to play in six matches last term due to persistent injury problems.

It remains to be seen whether Pogba will try to find a new club or decide the time is right to hang up his boots.

Pogba was emotional when he signed for Monaco last summer, describing his comeback as a second chance after what he called 'a time of darkness'.

The midfielder told Daily Mail Sport in 2024 that he discovered news of his reduced ban while preparing for a film premiere, adding: 'We went through hell. A time of darkness. But this is my second chance, I have to use it.'

Sports.title: Arsenal news: Door opens to £20m transfer as wonderkid agreement reached
Sports.content:
Arsenal news: Door opens to £20m transfer as wonderkid agreement reached

Premier League holders Arsenal have had a busy summer as they gear up to defend their title with some new faces in the squad

View 2 Images Mikel Arteta's Arsenal squad is continuing to take shape (Image: Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

After making Bruno Guimaraes their fourth senior summer signing, Arsenal are preparing to get further business done. The Brazilian midfielder followed Illan Meslier and Christos Tzolis to North London, while Piero Hincapie has joined permanently after a successful loan.

‌



There have also been exits to the tune of around £40million. Karl Hein, Jakub Kiwior, Leandro Trossard and Christian Norgaard have all departed, while further departures could also follow.

‌



Mikel Arteta oversaw a 3-2 defeat to Borussia Dortmund in the Emirates Cup over the weekend and will want a response against Como on Wednesday. After that comes the Community Shield against Manchester City, with new arrival Guimaraes champing at the bit to get his first action in an Arsenal shirt.

‌



There's news on some ins and outs this week as the start of the new season draws ever closer. Here are our latest headlines from around the Emirates Stadium.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Chelsea and Man Utd offered Myles Lewis-Skelly as Arsenal open to shock sale despite new deal READ MORE :

Arsenal set to receive millions back from Newcastle days after Bruno Guimaraes transfer READ MORE :

Door open for Jesus move

One player who could end up leaving Arsenal this summer is Gabriel Jesus. The Brazilian forward is of interest to Napoli and it looks as though space is opening up in the Serie A side's squad.

‌



That's because, according to Sky Italy, Fenerbahce have reached an agreement with Napoli over a move for Romelu Lukaku. The Belgian international is set to move in a cut-price deal worth around £5.12m plus add-ons.

View 2 Images Gabriel Jesus continues to be linked with Napoli (Image: Offside via Getty Images)

Get Arsenal's new 2026/27 home kit This article contains affiliate links, we will receive a commission on any sales we generate from it. Learn more £85 Fanatics Buy Now on Fanatics Product Description Arsenal have launched their new home kit for the 2026/27 season, said to incorporate classic Arsenal design features that tie into the club's heritage.

‌



That money could go towards a move for Jesus, who Arsenal are understood to value at around £20m. Napoli are believed to need one more sale before turning their attention to incomings but the door is now ajar at the very least.

Wonderkid Bernard joins

Mylo Bernard has joined Arsenal after coming through the ranks at Crystal Palace. According to The Athletic, the Gunners will pay Palace training compensation for the 16-year-old after his schoolboy registration at Selhurst Park expired.

Bernard, a striker, has four goals in eight appearances for England's Under-16 side. He also scored six times in 13 outings in last season's Under-18 Premier League and played in a 2-2 draw with Arsenal in May.

Article continues below

The teenager becomes the second promising youngster to join in the close-season. Elijah Upson, son of former Arsenal and England centre-back Matt, arrived in July after leaving Tottenham's academy.

Sports.title: James McHugh's wife dies after Irish sporting icon killed in road collision
Sports.content:
James McHugh's wife dies after Irish sporting icon killed in road collision

James McHugh, 62, was killed in a road traffic collision in Cavan on Monday, and his wife Noreen, who was a passenger in the car, died from her injuries on Tuesday

View Image James McHugh (Image: @Inpho)

The wife of Gaelic football star and Donegal All-Ireland winner James McHugh, who tragically lost his life in a road traffic collision on Monday, has also passed away.

‌



Noreen, who was in her 60s, was airlifted to Beaumont Hospital in Dublin with life-threatening injuries following the crash in Cavan on Monday. Devastatingly, she succumbed to her injuries the following day.

‌



The collision occurred on the N3 at Drummallaght, between Virginia and Cavan, shortly before 2pm on Monday.

‌



James, 62, who was a key member of the Donegal side that claimed the All-Ireland title in 1992, was driving a car that collided with a van. He was pronounced dead at the scene, with his body subsequently taken to Cavan General Hospital.

McHugh first pulled on the Donegal jersey in 1990 against Cavan, the same year the county claimed the Ulster title following victory over Armagh. Two years on, he was part of the historic Donegal squad that lifted the All-Ireland in 1992, alongside his brother Martin, reports the Irish Mirror.

The talented forward was also honoured with an All-Star that same year. At club level, he enjoyed considerable success with Cill Chartha, winning the championship in 1985, 1989 and 1993.

‌



In a statement released on Tuesday evening, Gardaí said: "Gardaí in Bailieborough investigating the fatal road traffic collision that occurred on the N3 at Drummallaght, between Virginia and Cavan, Co. Cavan, shortly before 2pm on Monday 10th August 2026 have confirmed a second person has passed away.

"The collision involved a car and a van.

"The male driver of the car, aged in his 60s, was fatally injured in the collision. His female passenger, also aged in her 60s, was seriously injured and was airlifted to Beaumont Hospital for treatment but passed away this evening Tuesday 11th August, 2026.

Article continues below

"Gardaí continue to appeal to anyone who may have witnessed this collision or who was travelling on the N3 between Virginia and Cavan, particularly between 1pm and 2pm to come forward.

"Gardaí are appealing to any motorists who may have dashcam or other camera footage of the area during this time to make this footage available to investigating Gardaí.

"Anyone with information is asked to contact Bailieboro Garda Station on 042 969 4570, the Garda Confidential Line on 1800 666 111, or any Garda station."

Sports.title: Freddie Flintoff's son Rocky, 18, smashes first career century off just 65 balls
Sports.content:
Freddie Flintoff's son Rocky, 18, smashes first career century off just 65 balls

Rocky Flintoff notched up his first career hundred in brutal fashion as Lancashire hammered Somerset in the One Day Cup

View 2 Images Rocky Flintoff scored his first career century (Image: Getty Images)

Freddie Flintoff's 18-year-old son Rocky proved himself a chip off the old block as he bludgeoned a brutal first career century.

‌



Flintoff Jr was in action for Lancashire in the Metro Bank One Day Cup and helped his side seal a place in the knockout stage with an astonishing display of hitting.

‌



Batting first against Somerset, Lancashire had been reduced to 138-3 when Flintoff entered the fray in the 23rd over.

‌



He shared a stand of 214 with Keaton Jennings, who finished with 156 off 127 balls.

Andrew Flintoff releases statement after shock England departure and confirms next job READ MORE :

Flintoff's hundred came off just 65 balls and he scored a total of 123 runs from 76 deliveries before being caught by Archie Vaughan, son of Freddie's former England captain Michael.

Lancashire scored a mammoth 443-6, bowling Somerset out for 269 in reply to set up a home knockout clash against Ben Stokes' Durham.

‌



It comes just three days after Freddie confirmed he was standing down as head coach of England Lions. He will coach Sydney Thunder in Australia's Big Bash League this winter.

Posting on Instagram, Flintoff said; "Unfortunately, I’ve made the decision to step away from my role with the Lions. Not only have I enjoyed my time having the opportunity to work with the best young cricketers in the country, but have taken great pride in seeing them develop.

View 2 Images Rocky proved himself a chip off the old block (Image: Getty Images)

Article continues below

"I’d like to thank the coaches and staff for all their passion, tireless work and support they give everyday.

"In particular Ed Barney who I’ve loved working with and was so lucky to have as a performance director, and obviously Rob [Key] for trusting me with one of the most Important roles in English cricket.

"I can’t wait to get started with the Thunder later in the year and see where coaching takes me. Good luck to whoever takes over you have some big pants to fill."

Sports.title: Liverpool get 'multiple calls' over taking star who Andoni Iraola is banned from playing
Sports.content:
Liverpool get 'multiple calls' over taking star who Andoni Iraola is banned from playing

The Liverpool young centre-back has enjoyed an impressive Liverpool pre-season so far before leaving out on loan for the new season

View 2 Images Liverpool youngster Ifeanyi Ndukwe is not short of suitors (Image: (Photo by Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty Images))

Liverpool youngster Ifeanyi Ndukwe is not short of suitors and he reportedly already favour a move to Portugal. The 18‑year‑old, who joined from Austria Vienna in a £2.5million deal, is expected to be loaned out for the upcoming season.

‌



Ndukwe impressed for the first team during pre‑season friendlies, but must now head out on loan due to work‑permit complications. Liverpool require a Governing Body Endorsement (GBE) from the FA to secure a work visa from the Home Office, yet the defender does not currently qualify, with players needing 15 points across several criteria.

‌



Having made just one senior appearance for Austria Vienna last season and being signed largely on the back of his standout performances at the Under‑17 World Cup in Qatar, he has not yet accumulated enough points to meet the senior international threshold.

‌



Liverpool sign Ronald Araujo as club legend reaches out and Andoni Iraola gets his wish READ MORE :

At the time, his agent Georg Lederer confirmed the plan had changed after the defender failed to qualify for a visa.

"The fact is that in the 2025/26 Premier League season, clubs had two exception spots where they didn't have to reach this points target," he explained to ORF, as quoted by Sky Sports Austria. "In the new season, this extra rule will be reduced by one spot. A loan club will now be found where Ifeanyi can gain playing experience at a very high level."

According to The Mail, clubs in Portugal, Germany, Spain, Denmark and France have all enquired about taking Ndukwe on loan, but there is a growing sense that Portugal may be his preferred destination.

‌



"I can't say which clubs we are in dialogue with, but I can confirm that we are in dialogue with Danish clubs about Ifeanyi Ndukwe," Lederer added. "The only thing I can say is that we are not talking about the top clubs in Denmark.

View 2 Images Liverpool youngster Ifeanyi Ndukwe in action during pre-season (Image: (Photo by Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty Images))

"We are also talking to several foreign clubs, but right now we need to decide, in collaboration with Liverpool, where Ifeanyi will fit best. We are looking at several different parameters. First and foremost, it is about Ifeanyi getting a lot of playing time, and then Liverpool are also looking at what type of football clubs play, as they want him in a high-pressing defence, so it is a bit like what you see in Liverpool.

‌



"Since Ifeanyi has just arrived at Liverpool, it is of course a loan agreement without an option to buy, but for now I can't say much more."

Liverpool paid around £2.6m for the teenager in January ahead of his planned move this summer, following his 18th birthday in March. Since then, he has caught the eye in defence during pre‑season outings against Sunderland, Wrexham, Leeds United and Monaco.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Virgil van Dijk, who partnered a player 17 years younger than him in Sunday's 3-2 defeat to Monaco, was left impressed by the youngster.

"Obviously I saw the games in pre-season in America," Van Dijk said. "He's a big talent, big guy and he wants to learn and I had a brief conversation with him, especially in the last couple of days. For him it is just progressing.

"I know he has to go on loan I think so let’s see where he ends up. Yeah [it's a shame he has to move on loan].

Article continues below

"I don’t know exactly what the rules are but the matter of fact is that he has to go on loan and wherever he goes, he needs to learn, get better and be ready when he comes back to hopefully stay there."

Sports.title: Martin Zubimendi dilemma shows Mikel Arteta and Arsenal face new transfer problem
Sports.content:
Martin Zubimendi dilemma shows Mikel Arteta and Arsenal face new transfer problem

Martin Zubimendi is being linked with the Arsenal exit door after only one year and the signing of Bruno Guimaraes suggests the Spaniard will be shunted down the pecking order

View 4 Images Arsenal signing of Bruno Guimaraes could have a knock on affect on the squad (Image: (Photo by David Price/Arsenal FC via Getty Images))

When someone of Bruno Guimaraes' calibre arrives at Arsenal, amid all the fanfare, there will be someone wondering if their time is up.

‌



The Brazilian has just moved to the Emirates for £75million after making it known that the Gunners were the club for him. This is a player who could play for any team in Europe and he will inevitably make Arsenal better.

‌



But following his arrival, that leaves one player having to go out and as part of the fallout reports have emerged that Arsenal have named their price on Martin Zubimendi. That generally only happens for players who could be on the move.

‌



You don't see any prices being quoted for Declan Rice, because he's one of Arsenal's untouchables, if they ever did make such a list. Zubimendi less so and after only a year at Arsenal the Spaniard could be set for a new role, and one he may not enjoy, if he stays.

It's a huge change for a player who, it was well documented, Mikel Arteta had eyed for several years before eventually luring him to London. This was a player who dominated England in the Euro 2024 final, making replacing Rodri look a simple task.

Arsenal get significant Julian Alvarez transfer update after Atletico Madrid meeting READ MORE :

But elite clubs only go looking for players in areas where they think they can improve. You hear no noise around Arsenal landing a top class centre-half, because in William Saliba and Gabriel, they have what they need. You hear no noise around Manchester City signing a top tier No.9, because they have Erling Haaland.

‌



Arsenal's pursuit of Guimaraes showed that they feel they can upgrade in that position. Rice is their talisman but alongside him there's been plenty of contenders. Mikel Merino is one, albeit very versatile, Zubimendi another. Myles Lewis-Skelly may have ambitions to play in that role.

If Zubimendi is to shift from a player who was guaranteed to start to one who isn't, then perhaps the warning signs were there. This is a player who started 34 of 38 games last season - but was benched for three of the final four.

View 4 Images Martin Zubimendi increasingly found himself on the bench towards the end of the season

‌



The Spaniard's minutes were cut and he endured the embarrassment of being subbed on, and then off, by Arteta. That came in the vital win over West Ham with Zubimendi coming on in the 28th minute for the injured Ben White. But his afternoon lasted less than 40 minutes and he was hauled off in the 67th minute for Kai Havertz.

"It is never easy to do that to a player, especially someone with Martin’s quality," Arteta admitted after the game.

Weeks later and Lewis-Skelly, who had been snubbed for much of the season, was picked to play in the Champions League final against PSG. Zubimendi started on the bench, and that's where he would remain for the evening.

‌



Managers can talk all they want about the value and the importance of a player, but what really tells is whether they call upon them come crunch time. With the title in the balance and a European Cup on the line, Zubimendi found himself overlooked.

View 4 Images The Spaniard did claim the Premier League title in his first campaign with Arsenal

When Zubimendi signed from Real Sociedad the club's sporting director, Andrea Berta, claimed: "Martin was a key target for us and we all know that he is a perfect fit for our squad with the high quality he has."

‌



That fit does not look so perfect now following Arsenal's pursuit of Guimaraes. Arteta has a squad that is the envy of most of Europe, but he'll find that having so many options creates as many problems as solutions it solves.

Arsenal have effectively played with two holding midfielders and a 10, previously Martin Odegaard. The Norwegian too is a man under pressure for his spot. Going on the fact that Rice is the pillar and Guimaraes, the second most expensive player in Arsenal history, will start - where does that leave Zubimendi?

View 4 Images Mikel Arteta has some difficult decisions regarding the make-up of his midfield

‌



A possibility exists that Arsenal play with more of a flat three in midfield. But where does that leave Odegaard. Or Eberechi Eze, who played centrally last season, or Kai Havertz or eventually Max Dowman?

Arsenal were pipped on penalties by PSG last season as their European Cup dreams were ended in heartbreaking fashion. On that night in Budapest, for all their battling spirit and defensive quality, it was clear that the Gunners had levels to go in the final third to match PSG.

This summer has been about closing that gap. Guimaraes is the type of player who helps them play through the lines. Their pursuit of Vinicius Junior was well publicised.

‌



Arsenal are firmly back among Europe's elite, capping an impressive rise under Arteta's leadership, but if there's one conundrum they're yet to face during the assembly of their stunning squad, it is who to back. In recent years no major player has wanted out, but with so many top class operators now available some will inevitably end up being cannon fodder in the club's grand plan.

Zubimendi may be one of the early lessons.

Sports.title: Bow Echo retired after setback as trainer George Boughey hails 'exceptional racehorse'
Sports.content:
Bow Echo retired after setback as trainer George Boughey hails 'exceptional racehorse'

The unbeaten Group One winner was entered for Sunday's Aga Khan Studs Prix Jacques Le Marois in Deauville but Boughey has been forced to call time on his colt's brilliant career

View 3 Images Bow Echo and Billy Loughnane starred on the track (Image: John Walton/PA Wire)

Unbeaten star of the Flat season Bow Echo has been retired due to injury, trainer George Boughey has announced.

‌



The miler took the 2,000 Guineas, St James's Palace Stakes and Sussex Stakes in a stellar campaign as a three-year-old.

‌



Bow Echo had been entered in Sunday's Aga Khan Studs Prix Jacques Le Marois at Deauville, which would have been his seventh racecourse outing.

‌



But an issue has led to Boughey reluctantly calling time on his stable star's career, which he shared with jockeys' championship leader Billy Loughnane.

In a statement, Boughey said, “It is with great disappointment that we have to announce that Bow Echo has had a setback and will be retired from racing.

“It has been the honour of a lifetime to train a horse like Bow Echo, He has given us some extraordinary days and taken everyone involved on a journey we will never forget. To retire unbeaten, having won the 2,000 Guineas, St James's Palace Stakes and Sussex Stakes says everything about what an exceptional racehorse he has been.”

‌



View 3 Images Billy Loughnane riding Bow Echo (R, yellow) to beat Ryan Moore (L, purple and white) at Royal Ascot (Image: Alan Crowhurst/Getty Images for Ascot Racecourse)

Loughnane added: "Bow Echo has been the most unbelievable racehorse and has given me days in the saddle that I could only ever have dreamed of.

"To ride a horse like him at this stage of my career, and to win the 2000 Guineas, St James’s Palace Stakes and Sussex Stakes together, is something incredibly special.

‌



“I can’t thank George and the whole team enough. George has trained him to perfection throughout his career and I feel incredibly lucky to have been Bow Echo's jockey in all six of his starts. “Of course it’s disappointing that we won’t see him on the racecourse again, but he retires unbeaten having done everything that was asked of him. It has been a privilege to ride him and he’ll always mean a huge amount to me.”

Bow Echo's career began almost a year ago to the day with an easy victory in a one mile maiden at Newbury.

He then won a Listed race at Haydock before finishing his two-year-old campaign with a Group Two success in the Royal Lodge Stakes at Newmarket.

‌



The son of Night Of Thunder began this season with a terrific performance in the 2,000 Guineas at Newmarket in May where he beat Gstaad.

He beat Gstaad again in a thrilling duel in the St James's Palace Stakes at Royal Ascot in June.

View 3 Images Bow Echo swoops to beat Gstaad in the Sussex Stakes (Image: Getty Images)

‌



And in what turned out to be his swansong, Loughnane conjured a devastating late burst from Bow Echo to win a dramatic renewal of the Sussex Stakes at Glorious Goodwood on July 29.

Gstaad was second three times to him this season and their rivalry lit up the sport.

In the aftermath of the shock news, Aidan O'Brien's horse was made the 5-2 (from 4-1) favourite with Coral for the Queen Elizabeth II Stakes.

Article continues below

Spokesman David Stevens said: "It's extremely disappointing for connections and indeed racing fans that Bow Echo's racing career has ended prematurely, as his rivalry with Gstaad in particular has been an ongoing highlight of this Flat season.

"In his absence, the horse beaten three times by George Boughey's charge this season is now clear favourite for the Queen Elizabeth II Stakes on Champions day."

Sports.title: Amy Hunt hails 'coming of age' moment as she turns silver into gold at European Championships
Sports.content:
Amy Hunt hails 'coming of age' moment as she turns silver into gold at European Championships

Amy Hunt hailed a “coming of age” moment after storming to European 100m gold in Birmingham for the first major individual title of her career.

View 2 Images Novuna GB & NI Team athlete Amy Hunt celebrates her victory in the Women’s 100m at the European Athletics Championships Birmingham 2026.

Amy Hunt hailed a ‘coming of age’ triumph after scorching to European 100m gold in Birmingham.

‌



The 24-year-old landed her first major individual success by coming home in 11.00s, two-hundredths of a second clear of Ewa Swoboda, to upgrade the silver she won at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow 13 days ago.

‌



It is the start of what she hopes will be a historic week as she targets gold on four fronts, with the 200m - in which she won World Championship silver last year - and a pair of relays to come.

‌



“I thought it was time to upgrade and I think this was definitely a coming of age night for me,” she said. “Now I am kind of fully established. I have two 100m medals in the last two weeks and one more sub-11 to boot, so I’m very happy.

“I want to be the best. I don't shy away from that. I train incredibly hard, and I back myself so incredibly hard. I'm not saying that I'm the best right now, but that's something I aspire to be.”

View 2 Images Gold medalist, Amy Hunt of Team Great Britain (Image: 2026 British Athletics)

‌



Hunt set the tone in the semi-finals, clocking 10.99s to ease into the showpiece. Reigning champion Dina Asher-Smith also made it through but could only manage fifth in the final on this occasion in the latest sign of a shift in the balance of power within British sprinting.

“The stage of a final doesn’t intimidate me and I just knew I had to stay calm and not overthink myself into the goal,” Hunt said. “That was why the Commonwealths really came in handy for me. That’s why I really wanted to do it, to have that experience of being in front of a home crowd, having that medal expectation, because I've never had that before.”

Hunt credited the unlikely trio of Megan Thee Stallion, High School Musical and Mamma Mia as key to keeping her calm in the build-up, along with keeping her brain active on Wordle. As in the Commonwealth Games final in Glasgow, her start left her with catching up to do but she never had cause to press the panic button.

‌



“One of my biggest skills in terms of championships is I know I'm so strong in the end and I always have that kind of extra magic in the last 40," she said. “It can definitely rescue me in situations that I've got myself into but I kind of know the distance I can be away from the girls in order to be able to come back.

“I did leave it a little bit last minute this time but in championships, it's all about crossing the line first. When I look back at this race in ten years, I'm not going to think about how far back I was after 30 metres.”

Hunt returns to action on Wednesday in her ‘favourite event’, the 200m. Her plans before that are refreshingly simple.

Article continues below

“Try and get as much sleep as possible and a big fat lie-in.”

After this, she has earned it.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."
