Sports.title: Lindblad vs Lawson: 2026 F1 team mates’ head-to-head scores at summer break | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Liam Lawson has finally begun what looks like being his first complete season with the same team and the stability appears to be paying off.

Having spent most of last season at Racing Bulls, Lawson has been a regular in the points. He has helped put the team fifth in the standings, on course for what would be its strongest championship finish in any of its guises.

But newcomer Arvid Lindblad has acquitted himself extremely well and goes into the summer break having tapped a strong vein of form. He’s scored in each of the last six grands prix and out-qualified Lawson in the last three – by decent margins, too.

So while Lawson’s numbers look good at the moment, he can’t be complacent about the growing threat on the other side of the Racing Bulls garage. Max Verstappen has all the reasons he needs to jump ship at the top team and if Lawson has a realistic chance of returning he needs to ensure he is the obvious choice. That won’t be the case as long as Lindblad keeps out-qualifying him.

As is often the case at Red Bull’s junior team, there is also pressure from below. Red Bull’s Nikola Tsolov leading the Formula 2 standings in his rookie campaign and the team will surely already be thinking about when he will be ready for a shot at F1.

Sports.title: Video: Honda explain Zandvoort ‘spec 2’ power unit changes | Brief
Sports.content:
Honda will introduce a ‘spec 2’ version of its RA626H power unit at the Dutch Grand Prix. The Japanese manufacturer is racing to catch up with its rivals after experiencing serious problems with vibration and insufficient power at the start of the sesason.

General trackside manager Shintaro Orihara said the new specification had hit their internal targets. “We focused to improve engine performance to make combustion faster,” he explained in a video released by Honda.

Sports.title: Verstappen vs Hadjar: 2026 F1 team mates’ head-to-head scores at summer break | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Isack Hadjar began his first full season at Red Bull knowing that the last driver in the same position as him lasted just two rounds before being booted out.

That must have been a daunting prospect to contemplate, though it bears pointing out that the senior race team management has changed significantly at Red Bull since Liam Lawson was shown the door after his pair of starts for the team last year.

The more experienced Yuki Tsunoda took Lawson’s place and became the latest in a series of drivers whose reputations took a brutal battering from occupying the garage adjacent to Max Verstappen’s. Tsunoda mustered just 7.2% of Red Bull’s points while alongside Verstappen.

This is the context in which to assess Hadjar’s performance this year. His 8-2 deficit in qualifying is nothing to brag about but he has been much closer to Verstappen over a single flying lap than his predecessors.

Hadjar has done vastly better at collecting points, too, claiming 38% of Red Bull’s score so far. True, compared to Tsunoda he’s had the benefit of a wider field spread between Red Bull and the midfield, but even so he’s already taken more than twice as many points as Tsunoda managed over his 22-race stint at the team last year.

He has achieved this alongside a formidable talent in a car which both drivers have termed “undriveable” on occasions. While the high level Verstappen operates at is so familiar it can almost be taken for granted (his superb second place in Hungary, for example), Hadjar has done a more than respectable job alongside him so far.

Sports.title: Featured Comment: Has F1 failed to promote quality racing? | Brief
Sports.content:
Those in charge of Formula 1 have allowed its new rules to turn racing into a ‘battle of the bots’, says @RedPill:

I felt there was going to be some trust and proper direction within FIA and Liberty Media who owns the rights to F1 to make sure the quality of (human) racing was going to remain high quality. Boy, we were wrong. The whole debacle and agreed verbiage in contacts allowed the power unit manufacturers and investors to pretty much be the ones to dictate what was going to be allowed in F1, while retaining huge powers in the wording to prevent changes.

Fans, drivers, teams, FIA and Liberty Media are now stuck with it. I hate how the drivers are more passengers in their own cars while racing. Yes, there’s too much going in the cars, that the drivers can’t possibly manage everything and race in full anger, but this is no secret or anything new. The powers that be needed to craft specifications that used the latest tech, but still retain the drivers’ ability to fully race the car, the way a race car driver is suppose to race. That is why we watch the races.

We come and watch these F1 races because there’s humans in control of brilliant machinery, racing them to the ninth degree, but there’s a limit. If I wanted to watch automated machinery duke it out and see battle of bots I would instead go to robot contests, not F1.

Red Pill (@RedPill)

Sports.title: Teofimo Sr. Dismisses Shakur Stevenson’s Vacant-Belt Championships
Sports.content:
“This fight is about Teofimo Lopez trying to get the world title again, become a real three-division world champion. No vacant belts,” Lopez Sr. said to Fighthype. “Shakur got like two vacant belts, right? So, to me, he’s not a real three-division world champion. My son is going to do it the right way. We’re going to go straight to the champion. No vacant belt.”

Stevenson has actually won world titles across four divisions. His first came against Joet Gonzalez for the vacant WBO featherweight belt in 2019. He then stopped reigning WBO junior lightweight champion Jamel Herring in 2021 before defeating Edwin De Los Santos for the vacant WBC lightweight title in November 2023.

The fourth belt is difficult for Lopez Sr. to dismiss under his own standard. Shakur took the WBO light welterweight title from Teofimo in January, giving him two divisional championships won by defeating reigning titleholders.

Lopez Sr. also criticized Shakur’s fighting style and questioned how much further Stevenson can climb through the weight classes.

“I would love to fight him again. Let’s hope that we can get him before we move up too high,” Lopez Sr. said. “I don’t think Shakur can go up in the weight divisions. He’s too chinny. He doesn’t like to get hit. He’s a boring fighter.”

He believes Teofimo fought the wrong fight against Shakur. In his view, Teofimo should have boxed from the back foot instead of following the southpaw to his right all night.

Sports.title: Liam Paro Answers Devin Haney’s IBF Call
Sports.content:
“Have the WBO.. I want the IBF,” Devin said on X.

Haney seems to have signaled his preferred opponent without directly naming him. The choice makes sense. Paro brings a large following in Australia and the potential for a PPV event built around two welterweight champions.

That separates Paro from Jack Catterall, another opponent who has been discussed for Haney. Catterall presents a difficult fight with his movement, defense, timing and awkward southpaw style.

Paro is a southpaw as well, but he’s much more willing to engage and turn fights into physical exchanges. Haney has generally performed well against aggressive fighters who come forward, giving him opportunities to box from range, counter, and tie up when they get inside.

Catterall offers a different challenge. He’s unlikely to chase Haney recklessly or provide the type of pressure that allows Haney to settle into his preferred rhythm. Taking that fight would mean accepting considerable stylistic difficulty without getting another world title in return.

Paro gives Haney the opportunity to unify the division while bringing an established Australian audience to the promotion. From Haney’s perspective, that combination makes the matchup easier to understand commercially.

Nothing has been finalized, but the exchange leaves little mystery about their interest. Both champions have publicly opened the door to putting the IBF and WBO titles together.

Sports.title: Archie Moore Silences Yvon Durelle in Montreal Rematch
Sports.content:
The rematch drew 11,555 spectators, generating a gate of $140,519 to set a Montreal boxing record. Former world heavyweight champion Jack Sharkey served as referee.

Moore, already well into his 40s, had held the light heavyweight crown since defeating Joey Maxim in December 1952. Durelle, 29, remained a leading contender after his ferocious effort in their initial meeting.

Rather than trading immediately with the heavy-handed challenger, Moore fought cautiously through the opening two rounds. His defense limited Durelle’s opportunities to land the kind of power shots that had caused so much trouble in their first fight.

Two judges had Moore in front after two rounds, while the third had the fight even.

Moore changed the fight completely in the third. A hard right hand dropped Durelle, who beat the count at seven and tried to fight back. The champion quickly closed in.

Three more knockdowns followed as Moore connected with rights and lefts. After the fourth knockdown of the round, Sharkey counted Durelle out at 2:52.

Moore had turned a rivalry born from one of the greatest scares of his championship reign into a decisive three-round knockout.

Durelle faced difficult circumstances before the fight. A boating accident left him with a back injury, and his hometown of Baie-Sainte-Anne suffered the tragic Escuminac Disaster in June, when 35 fishermen lost their lives.

Moore continued his remarkable run near the top of the sport. Durelle later challenged George Chuvalo for the Canadian heavyweight title in November 1959, losing by knockout in the 12th round.

The two rivals eventually became friends. Moore retained enormous respect for Durelle, remembering him as one of the hardest punchers and toughest opponents he faced.

Their first fight became the classic. On August 12, 1959, Moore made the rematch his answer.

Sports.title: Teofimo: Turki Alalshikh Pushed Benn, Ryan Garcia Wanted Me
Sports.content:
“Conor and Ryan are fighting because it’s a Turki thing. Turki pushed that fight,” Teofimo said to Fighthype. “It wasn’t something that Ryan wanted. Ryan wanted to fight me, but, you know, it’s a business at the same time.”

Ryan has since named Lopez among the opponents he wants to face after Benn, along with Rolando Romero and Shakur Stevenson. That shows the interest is there, although it doesn’t establish how close Garcia and Lopez were to actually fighting.

Teofimo has his own fight to win first. He challenges WBA welterweight champion Romero on August 22 in Las Vegas, attempting to capture a title in a third weight division.

Wins by Garcia and Lopez would leave both operating at 147 pounds with a marketable fight available between them. Teofimo would also own the WBA belt, giving Garcia another reason to pursue the matchup.

Garcia has mentioned Romero as a possible opponent as well, meaning Rolly could put himself in position for a rematch if he defeats Lopez.

Lopez believes money and promotional relationships are increasingly determining which fights get made.

“Everybody’s right now more on the money side,” Lopez said. “Everybody’s associated with somebody. Takeover is on his own with his own.”

Teofimo is coming off his January loss to Shakur Stevenson and will be making his welterweight debut against Romero. Rolly already owns a decision victory over Garcia, giving Teofimo a chance to strengthen his case for a Garcia fight with an impressive performance on August 22.

Sports.title: Raymond Muratalla Ready for 140, Targets Shakur Stevenson
Sports.content:
“I felt the effects of just like the weight cut. Didn’t feel my strongest. Everything wasn’t on point like it usually is,” said Muratalla to ProBox TV.

Moving up five pounds is what Muratalla wants next, although nothing has been finalized with Top Rank.

“That’s one thing I’m looking forward to. I’ve started to feel that in the ring. So I think it’s about that time to move up and feel a lot better and perform a lot better, too.”

Muratalla described making 135 as difficult and said it has “never been easy.” Competing at 140 should make the physical demands easier and allow him to perform closer to his best.

Stevenson is the major target. Muratalla has wanted the fight before, and moving into the light welterweight division would give him another opportunity to pursue it.

“I think it only makes sense now. Something we’ve been wanting and just never goes through. I think at this point, that’d be something that the fans would love to see.”

Muratalla believes his adaptability would give Stevenson a different test from his previous opponents.

“He’s never faced a fighter like me. I think it’s going to put out a good fight for the boxing fans. It’s definitely a fight that’s going to be competitive, a challenging fight and something that boxing needs.”

No decision has been announced regarding Muratalla’s IBF lightweight title, and he said there is no plan yet for his next fight. His preference, however, is clear: move to 140 and pursue the biggest fights available.

If Stevenson isn’t available, Muratalla wants the other champions in the division.

“Mostly champions. That’s all I really want. Whoever is champion, that’s what I’m going to be looking at and headed for.”

Sports.title: Ben Shalom Goes Nuclear On Zuffa Boxing
Sports.content:
“I’m disgusted by the organization. I can’t say anything more than being disgusted. They don’t care about boxing. They don’t care about British fighters. They don’t care about the sport. They care about profitability for their shareholders and ripping the sport from this country, changing it, packaging it up and excluding everyone else,” said Shalom to talkSPORT Boxing.

Shalom also challenged the British Boxing Board of Control to “get a backbone” and stand against Zuffa’s plans. He feels the UK government would support the regulator if it does.

He views Zuffa as more than another rival bidding for talent. Shalom maintains its attempt to create a separate boxing ecosystem threatens small-hall shows, independent operators, and the traditional pipeline through area, British, and world titles.

Simon Jordan questioned the timing of the outrage, arguing that the promoter’s voice grew louder only after talent contracted to BOXXER began appearing on other platforms.

Jordan also pointed out that British promoters eagerly welcomed Turki Alalshikh before Alalshikh became involved with Zuffa’s boxing operation.

Shalom insisted contractual disputes remain separate issues to handle through the courts. His larger concern involves the prospect of one entity gaining enough power to determine who receives title shots.

The rhetoric was extreme, but the power struggle underneath it is clear. Zuffa is competing with established promoters for fighters, influence, and control over how championship opportunities are distributed.

Sports.title: Klitschko Brothers Ruled Heavyweight Boxing Their Own Way
Sports.content:
Vitali Klitschko compiled a 45-2 record with 41 knockouts. His first defeat came against Chris Byrd in April 2000 when a shoulder injury forced him to quit after nine rounds despite leading on the scorecards.

Seven months later, Wladimir handled the problem his older brother couldn’t finish. He dropped Byrd twice and defeated him by a wide 12-round decision.

The roles were reversed after one of the biggest shocks of Wladimir’s career.

Corrie Sanders overwhelmed Wladimir in two rounds in March 2003, dropping him four times and taking his WBO heavyweight title. Thirteen months later, Vitali fought Sanders for the vacant WBC belt and stopped the South African in eight rounds.

Vitali’s most famous defeat was considerably different. He was leading Lennox Lewis 58-56 on all three scorecards after six rounds in their violent June 2003 fight when severe cuts around his left eye forced the stoppage. Lewis never fought again, leaving one of boxing’s biggest unanswered questions behind.

Vitali later became the WBC division’s dominant champion. His victories included Samuel Peter, Chris Arreola, Shannon Briggs, Tomasz Adamek and Derek Chisora. He finished his career in September 2012 by stopping Manuel Charr.

Wladimir’s reign was longer.

After early knockout defeats against Ross Puritty, Sanders and Lamon Brewster, he rebuilt his career under trainer Emanuel Steward. Wladimir stopped Byrd in their second fight in 2006 to win the IBF title and remained heavyweight champion for the next nine years.

He defeated Sultan Ibragimov, Ruslan Chagaev, David Haye, Alexander Povetkin, Kubrat Pulev and Bryant Jennings before Tyson Fury outpointed him in Düsseldorf in November 2015.

Wladimir returned for one final fight against Anthony Joshua at Wembley Stadium in April 2017. At 41, he dropped Joshua in the sixth round before being stopped in the 11th of a classic title fight. He retired with a 64-5 record and 53 knockouts.

Their styles and personalities were different. Vitali was the more awkward, aggressive fighter and possessed an exceptional chin. Wladimir became the more technically disciplined boxer under Steward, controlling opponents with his jab, right hand and clinching.

The question boxing never answered was which Klitschko was actually better.

They made sure it stayed that way.

Sports.title: Teofimo Sr. Wants Ryan Garcia vs. Conor Benn Winner After Rolly
Sports.content:
“Ryan Garcia, the winner, Conor Benn, Ryan Garcia, that’s what’s going straight right there,” Teofimo Sr. said to Fight Hub TV. “And then if Liam Paro is still around or whoever else it is, man, we’re just going to try to take over the weight division at 147, become undisputed again.”

The trainer made his interest in the Garcia-Benn winner clear earlier in the interview.

“That’s a good fight. And I think that we’ll take the winner out of that,” he said. “Especially, whoever wins, it’ll be a great fight. Either it’s Ryan, or it’s Conor Benn. And we’re ready to do it, man.”

That plan depends first on Teofimo beating Romero, which isn’t guaranteed after his one-sided loss to Shakur Stevenson in January. Moving to welterweight gives Lopez a chance to leave that performance behind while immediately fighting for another world title.

His father believes the additional seven pounds will make Teofimo faster and more effective rather than slowing him down.

“I think he should be able to do everything in less than two years, become undisputed,” Lopez Sr. said. “All these fighters are going to be slower than him, and he’s a really smart fighter in there.”

Senior also identified his son’s mental state as the biggest danger to those plans.

“All I know is this is the time where we got to be focused, and my son got to be in his best mental mind ever,” Lopez Sr said. “That’s the only thing that could mess up my son. Everything is mental with him.”

Teofimo has already named Devin Haney, Garcia and Liam Paro among the champions and contenders he wants at welterweight. His father’s version puts the Garcia-Benn winner at the front of the line after Romero.

If Lopez beats Rolly, Garcia and Benn will settle their own business three weeks later.

Ghana News.title: List of all 26 vacation judges nationwide and their courts
Ghana News.content:
There is a raging controversy following the petitions of lawyers Godfred Dame and Atta Akyea to the Chief Justice protesting the continuation of cases against their clients during the legal vacation.

Godfred Dame, the former Attorney-General, is defending the former CEO of the National Bufferskock Company, Hanan Abdul-Wahab Aludiba and his wife, Hajia Faiza Seidu Wuni.

Atta Akyea, on the other hand, is defending the former Director-General of the National Signals Bureau, Kwabena Adu-Boahene, and his wife, Mrs Angela Adjei-Boateng.

The two sets of accused are politically exposed persons, with the men holding offices in the erstwhile New Patriotic Party (NPP) administration. For this reason, the two petitions and the commentary they have occasioned have created the impression that the Chief Justice selected judges to sit on only the cases in which NPP members are the accused.

Following a post I made on Facebook, one of the accused persons sent me a private message expressing his concerns about the selective nature of the cases selected by the Chief Justice for the vacation court.

“The CJ has selected only 7 criminal cases to be heard during the vacation, leaving thousands of cases hanging. My issue is what seems to be selective,” the person said.

As I write this, there's a story on myjoyonline with the headline, "Why these 2 cases? – Atta Akyea questions Chief Justice’s expedited trial order." In this story, Atta Akyea creates the false impression that the vacation courts were mandated to sit only on the two high-profile cases involving the NPP administration members.

The fact that the current Chief Justice was appointed by the sitting president gives oxygen to the conspiracies, even if the lawyers and political commentators fall short of plainly saying what they have been insinuating.

The lawyers claim they want to rest, but the rest of us see the vehement opposition to the vacation courts as a delay tactic. They may be employing the tactics of North African football teams that are leading the scoreline in the dying embers of the game.

Put differently, they are trying to "Stephen Opunilise" the cases, praying for a favourable outcome of the 2028 election to enact their own version of Operation Create All Looters (OCAL), which the NDC executed at the dawn of the administration that is now spearheading its campaign promise, Operation Recover All Loots (ORAL).

As an investigative journalist who has uncovered major corruption scandals without seeing them resolved, I lean towards speedy trials. Legal vacations, which the experts have described as being vacations for judges—and not vacations for lawyers or cases—are an impediment to speedy trials.

I have no problem with the Chief Justice’s warrants for judges to sit during the legal vacation.

The reason for this write-up, however, is not to advance arguments superior to what the lawyers have already put out.

Mine is to put out facts to help correct the false and misleading information that has characterised this important discourse. These are the facts and my lay interpretation of those facts.

1. First, the impression is created that only a few cases have been selected for the vacation courts. That is false.

2. There are a total of 26 judges sitting nationwide during the vacation, according to the list available to Pledge Against Corruption. There are hundreds of cases involved, not just two or seven.

They are located in the Greater Accra, Eastern, Central, Northern, Western, Ashanti, Volta, and Upper East regions.

3. The warrants signed by the Chief Justice authorise the judges to sit on all substantive cases before their courts. The warrants are no case specific. So, if there are 20 cases in each court, then we are looking at 520 cases.

4. In addition to the cases pending in the courts of the vacation judges, they have also been assigned additional responsibilities for other courts to hear motions and other emergency processes. The judges of the additional courts whose emergency cases are overseen by the vacation judges are currently on legal vacation. When they return from vacation, and the judges currently sitting also go on vacation, they will assume responsibility for hearing motions and emergency matters from the courts of the judges who sat during the legal vacation.

5. This arrangement, which is not new, defeats the misleading information that vacation courts are only supposed to move motions. The vacation judges are authorised to hear substantive cases before their courts, but they cannot take over substantive cases pending in the courts of judges who have proceeded on legal vacation.

6. In a country where the justice system is extremely slow, we cannot afford to lose so much judicial time to legal vacation.

7. By the second week of October, the judges who are currently on vacation will have returned and settled, while those sitting during the legal vacations go on leave.

8. At the time the judges who will be proceeding for leave in October return, Christmas break and other end-of-year interruptions will be beckoning.

9. This means that if Kwabena Adu Boahene’s and Hanan Abdul-Wahab’s cases are not called during this legal vacation, when the judges hearing their cases are sitting, there won’t be any meaningful progress on the cases for the rest of the year. That will help the "Stephen Opunilisation" agenda but hurt Ghana's anti-corruption fight.

The political class has a game plan. And it works for them. If these two political cases had been absent, we probably would have heard no controversy over judges sitting during legal vacation.

Some independent lawyers, including the moribund Ghana Bar Association, have weighed heavily into the debate. A suit has reportedly been filed on the matter, and I suppose the litigant wants the case heard during the legal vacation. However it ends, one thing should be clear.

Our already slow justice system must not halt during legal vacations. Traditions must not become the law if it is detrimental to our judicial process. The judiciary must codify its practices and firmly plant its feet on legal grounds to ensure the sitting of vacation judges on substantive cases during legal vacations.

Let me end with facts that dispel the false narrative suggesting that the Chief Justice issued a warrant for the hearing of only two cases during the legal vacation.

Apart from the two Court of Appeal judges whose warrants are listed above, here is the full list of the other 24 judges sitting across the country during the legal vacation.

The first column is the additional courts they will be overseeing, courts whose motions and emergency processes they will hear. Their own courts are listed in the last column.

Ghana News.title: Government reaffirms commitment to empower Ghanaian youth on International Youth Day
Ghana News.content:
George Opare Addo

The Ministry of Youth Development and Empowerment has reaffirmed its commitment to creating opportunities for young Ghanaians to develop their skills, participate meaningfully in national development and thrive in the digital age.

The Ministry made the commitment as Ghana joins the global community to commemorate International Youth Day on August 12, 2026, under the global theme, “Different Contexts, Common Aspirations.”

Ghana is marking the occasion under the national theme, “Rebuilding Values, Inspiring Patriotism: Empowering the Youth in the Digital Age.”

In a statement issued by its Public Relations Unit, the Ministry said although young people grow up in different communities and face varying challenges, they share common aspirations for quality education, meaningful employment, innovation, dignity, inclusion and a better future.

It said the national theme complemented the global theme by highlighting the need to rebuild positive values, strengthen patriotism and equip young people with the digital skills and opportunities required to succeed in an increasingly technology-driven world.

The Ministry noted that young people across urban and rural communities, educational institutions, workplaces and entrepreneurial ecosystems continued to demonstrate resilience, creativity and determination.

Their contributions, it said, were evident in areas including business, technology, agriculture, the arts, sports, public service and community leadership.

According to the Ministry, young people should not be viewed merely as future leaders but as active agents of change who are already driving solutions to local and national challenges and contributing to Ghana's social and economic transformation.

Five Key Priorities

As part of its youth empowerment agenda, the Ministry said it remained committed to expanding opportunities for skills development and lifelong learning, supporting youth entrepreneurship and innovation, and promoting decent employment and economic inclusion.

It also listed strengthening youth participation in governance and civic engagement, as well as advancing mental health awareness and psychosocial support, among its priorities.

The Ministry further pledged to ensure that no young person was left behind regardless of location, gender, ability or socioeconomic background.

It said the global theme, “Different Contexts, Common Aspirations,” was also a call for greater collaboration among government institutions, the private sector, development partners, civil society organisations, educational institutions and communities.

Such collaboration, it said, was necessary to create an enabling environment in which every young person could thrive.

The Ministry also called on stakeholders to work together to rebuild values such as integrity, discipline, hard work and patriotism, while empowering young people to harness the opportunities of the digital age responsibly and productively.

As Ghana celebrates International Youth Day, the Ministry urged young people to pursue excellence, embrace innovation and continue making meaningful contributions to national development.

It said the differences in young people's experiences should enrich the nation, while their common aspirations should unite them towards building a prosperous, inclusive and resilient Ghana where every young person has the opportunity to realise their full potential.

The Ministry of Youth Development and Empowerment is responsible for coordinating and implementing policies aimed at promoting youth development and empowerment and ensuring that young people are equipped with the skills, opportunities and support required to contribute meaningfully to national development.

Ghana News.title: I thought I knew how to manage people- until I entered the workplace
Ghana News.content:
Jonathan Kofi Appiah

(The Hard Lessons That Gave Birth to the People Management Triangle)

I left the University of Ghana thinking I understood people. I was wrong.

As a student leader, I had learnt how to mobilise students, negotiate and rally people around a common cause. I thought those experiences had prepared me for the world of work.

Then I entered the workplace.

It was a completely different ball game.

Because of my student leadership responsibilities, I had little opportunity to undertake internships. Besides, internship opportunities were not easy to come by in those days. So, like many graduates, I entered the workplace armed mainly with classroom knowledge, enthusiasm and ambition.

It did not take long for me to discover that knowing how to do your job and knowing how to navigate the workplace are two different competencies.

I was good at my assigned tasks. No bragging; I could practically recite my job description in my sleep! But there was another job description nobody gave me:

How do I relate with colleagues? Who do I trust? How do I navigate organisational politics? How do I disagree without creating enemies? And perhaps most importantly, how do I manage my supervisor—or, better put, my boss?

These questions never appeared in my examinations, yet suddenly my career depended on finding the answers.

When helping my boss landed me in trouble

The workplace was already characterised by organisational politics. There were interests, alliances and relationships that a young employee could easily misunderstand.

I quickly realised that my experience in student politics did not automatically translate into workplace success. You may successfully rally students against an unpopular university decision, but try the same strategy against your boss on Monday morning and see what happens!

One experience particularly shaped my thinking.

My supervisor was going through family challenges that were affecting his work. Wanting to help, I fabricated a loose story to cover for him.

My intention was good. My judgement was not.

Instead of solving the problem, I landed in trouble. Thankfully, a fellow OLD TOM, who was a member of management, came to my rescue.

That experience taught me an important lesson: good intentions alone are not enough when managing your boss. You need judgement, boundaries, emotional intelligence, communication and the ability to manage upward without compromising yourself.

Then I became the boss

Years later, I was promoted to manager at a relatively young age.

Perhaps somewhere inside me I thought, “Finally, now it is my turn!”

I became heavily focused on targets, deadlines and results. Unfortunately, the more I focused on the work, the easier it became to push the people doing the work into the background.

Then another experience changed my perspective.

One day, I aggressively demanded a report from one of my talented employees without first listening to him.

Later, I discovered something that humbled me:

It was his birthday and I didn’t even know.

I nearly lost a talented employee before learning a powerful lesson:

Managing staff is not only about getting results. It is about building genuine human connections with the people who produce those results.

Employees are human beings before they are job titles. Sustainable performance requires accountability, but it also requires relationships.

And then I saw the triangle

Over more than 18 years of workplace experience, I began to see three relationships that repeatedly determined how effectively people worked together:

🔺 Managing Self; your emotions, attitude, discipline, integrity and personal growth.

🔺 Managing Staff; communication, accountability, trust, coaching, empathy and human connection.

🔺 Managing Boss; understanding expectations, building trust, communicating strategically and influencing upward.

That became the People Management Triangle.

The principle is simple: balance matters.

You can be technically brilliant but poor at managing yourself. You can impress your boss while destroying your team. You can have excellent relationships with colleagues but struggle to manage upward.

Like an equilateral triangle, sustainable workplace relationships require deliberate attention to all three sides.

This book was not born in the library

Let me emphasise this:

The People Management Triangle was not born in the library. It was born in the workplace.

If you are looking for fancy theories, complicated management jargon and concepts that sound impressive but are difficult to apply on Monday morning, this may not be the book for you.

This book was shaped by real workplace experience; mistakes, difficult conversations, bosses, employees, organisational politics, promotions, failures, successes and relationships accumulated over more than 18 years in the world of work.

Interestingly, the initial manuscript was approximately 372 pages.

But I asked myself:

Will the busy CEO have time to finish this?

Can the newly promoted supervisor quickly read it and start making a difference?

Can the new employee use it to adjust quickly and build balanced workplace relationships?

So I cut, simplified and refined the manuscript to almost half its original size.

Not because there was nothing more to say, but because busy people need practical wisdom they can actually find time to read.

Less unnecessary complexity. More workplace reality. More practical application.

Let’s make the workplace healthier

People Management Triangle: Managing Self, Staff and Boss Effectively is dedicated to leaders, supervisors, managers, business owners, professionals and students who desire to build healthier and more productive workplaces.

I hope the young graduate reads it before learning everything the hard way.

I hope the newly promoted supervisor reads it before discovering that being excellent at a job does not automatically make someone excellent at managing people.

I hope managers ask themselves:

“Have I become so focused on results that I have forgotten the people producing them?”

And I hope employees understand that managing your boss is not manipulation. It is about building a productive upward relationship while maintaining professionalism, integrity and respect.

My journey started as a young graduate who thought competence was enough.

After more than 18 years in the workplace, I know better.

Technical competence may get you through the door, but your ability to manage yourself, your staff and your boss can significantly determine how far you go—and the impact you make along the way.

The workplace taught me these lessons.

I simply gave them a name: The People Management Triangle.

People Management Triangle: Managing Self, Staff and Boss Effectively

Grab your copy. Read it. Apply it.

Bookings & Orders via WhatsApp: +233 24 670 8117

Together, let’s make the workplace a healthier place for all.

Jonathan Kofi Appiah is a seasoned aviation executive with over a decade of experience in leadership roles. He is the Team Lead at Heritage Necessity Consult (www.necessityconsult,com) and the author of People Management Triangle: Managing Self, Staff and Boss Effectively. Previously, he held key positions at an Airline in Ghana, including Head of Commercial, Senior Manager of Organisational Effectiveness and Business Development, and Deputy Head of Human Resources.

Ghana News.title: Upper West Police bust armed robbery syndicate after MoMo attacks; 6 arrested
Ghana News.content:
The Upper West Regional Police Command has busted an armed robbery syndicate operating in parts of the Wa West District and Wa Municipality.

In a statement signed by Francis Yiribaare, Deputy Commissioner of Police and Upper West Regional Police Commander, he said the six suspects have been arrested following months of intelligence-led and coordinated operations by the Police.

The arrests follow a series of robbery attacks in which victims were reportedly attacked and wounded with machetes before being forced to disclose their Mobile Money (MoMo) PINs.

The suspects allegedly used the PINs to transfer money from the victims’ accounts into MoMo accounts controlled by the robbers.

The six suspects are Amadu Moro, 35; Adama Yussif, 40; Nasiru Abdul Rahman, 52; Iddrissu Adama, 35; Korika Issaka, 20; and Zakaria Brigi, 21.

Nasiru Abdul Rahman sustained injuries during the operation and died upon arrival at the Upper West Regional Hospital.

His body has since been deposited at the hospital mortuary for preservation and autopsy.

Preliminary investigations have linked Adama Yussif, Amadu Moro and the deceased Nasiru Abdul Rahman to several robbery incidents in the region.

These include an attack at Kpenateng Junction on August 1, 2026, Kulkpara-Dapoha on June 19, Kpenateng Community on June 15 and May 23, and Piisi-Dapoha on March 27, 2026.

Police investigations have so far established that approximately GH¢22,070 in cash was allegedly taken from victims.

An additional GH¢3,274 was reportedly siphoned through the victims’ MoMo accounts.

The Police have also retrieved seven mobile phones from the suspects. The devices are being examined as part of the ongoing investigation.

Two other alleged members of the syndicate are currently at large.

They have been identified as Haruna, 30, who is alleged to serve as the gang’s armourer, and Amadu Mahamudu, 24, the son of the deceased suspect.

The Upper West Regional Police Command says it has intensified efforts to locate and arrest the two wanted suspects.

The Command is urging residents, particularly those in communities affected by the recent robbery incidents, to remain vigilant and promptly report suspicious persons, movements and activities to the Police.

It is also appealing to the public to provide credible information that could help investigators apprehend the two suspects and prevent further criminal activities.

Ghana News.title: BoG sells over $8bn through FX Programme as cedi faces fresh pressure
Ghana News.content:
The Bank of Ghana (BoG) has sold more than $8 billion into the foreign exchange market since January 2026 to improve liquidity, meet demand and support the stability of the cedi.

Data compiled by Joy Business from the Bank’s FX auction calendars and market communications show that the central bank sold about US$7.45 billion through its FX Intermediation Programme between January and July 2026.

The Bank also deployed about US$811 million through its FX Intervention Programme between January and June.

This takes the total market support to more than US$8.2 billion so far this year.

The figure could approach US$9.2 billion by the end of August if the Bank proceeds with plans to sell up to US$1 billion through its FX Intermediation Programme during the month.

The development comes as the cedi faces renewed pressure against the US dollar. The Bank of Ghana has put the cedi’s depreciation at 10.61% as of the end of July.

The FX Intermediation Programme is designed to improve liquidity and help reduce excessive volatility in the foreign exchange market when necessary.

It is particularly linked to activities under the Domestic Gold Purchase Programme.

Some market participants have argued that the cedi could have come under even greater pressure without the Bank’s interventions.

Data gathered by Joy Business from some commercial banks also indicate that demand for dollars from businesses has remained strong.

Some market participants have attributed the pressure to increased foreign exchange needs from energy sector players financing crude oil imports, finished petroleum products and payments to power producers.

Others have linked the pressure to limited dollar supply relative to demand from businesses.

Recent Bank of Ghana data indicate that Ghana’s international reserves have declined to a little over US$12 billion.

Despite the pressure, the central bank has maintained that businesses should not panic, describing the recent movements as temporary market pressures.

The Bank has also indicated that it remains capable of supporting the foreign exchange market when necessary and ensuring that critical imports are not disrupted.

Ghana News.title: Private citizen drags Chief Justice, Attorney General to Supreme Court over legal vacation
Ghana News.content:
A private citizen, Elorm Kwami Gorni, has sued Attorney General Dominic Ayine and Chief Justice Paul Baffoe-Bonnie at the Supreme Court over Ghana’s legal vacation arrangements.

Mr Gorni is challenging the constitutionality of the annual suspension of sittings at the Supreme Court and Court of Appeal from August 1 to September 30.

The suit, filed on July 28, 2026, invokes the Supreme Court’s original jurisdiction under Articles 2(1) and 130(1) of the 1992 Constitution.

Mr Gorni argues that the two-month suspension undermines citizens’ constitutional right to access justice within a reasonable time.

While High Courts continue to sit during the legal vacation through designated vacation courts, the plaintiff says the Supreme Court and Court of Appeal do not sit throughout the period.

He contends that this leaves litigants with pending matters before the two appellate courts waiting until the vacation ends.

According to him, the arrangement could delay appeals, constitutional cases, applications for stay of execution, interlocutory applications and judicial review proceedings.

Mr Gorni is asking the Supreme Court to declare Rule 61(b) of the Court of Appeal Rules, 1997 (C.I. 19), and Rule 82 of the Supreme Court Rules, 1996 (C.I. 16), unconstitutional to the extent that they permit the suspension of sittings during the legal vacation.

He argues that the rules and their implementation are inconsistent with Articles 19(1), 23, 33, 125 and 296 of the Constitution.

The plaintiff also contends that determining when courts sit is an administrative function and must meet the constitutional requirement of fairness and reasonableness.

He stresses that his challenge is not against judges taking annual leave or having periods of rest.

Rather, he wants the court to determine whether judicial leave can be organised without completely suspending the constitutional functions of the two appellate courts.

Among the reliefs being sought is an order directing the Chief Justice to consider alternative arrangements, including rotational sittings, vacation panels or staggered judicial leave.

Mr Gorni says such measures could allow the Supreme Court and Court of Appeal to continue hearing cases throughout the legal year while preserving judges’ entitlement to annual leave.

The case places Ghana’s longstanding legal vacation system before the Supreme Court and raises questions about its impact on access to justice and the timely determination of cases.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”
