World.title: Fake videos and false allegations target candidates in French 2027 presidential election
World.content:
France's presidential election is set for the spring of 2027, and it is already attracting instances of misinformation and alleged foreign interference that have since sparked criminal proceedings.

 

Researchers from the bot-tracking network AntiBot4Navalny have detected a campaign linked to Matryoshka, a covert influence and disinformation operation aligned with Russia.

At first, these posts focused on Gabriel Attal, the former prime minister of France who is running to succeed current president Emmanuel Macron.

Attal filed a criminal complaint with French authorities "alleging foreign interference originating from Russian networks", after fabricated videos impersonating French news outlets targeted him online.

Fake videos bearing the logos and visual identity of well-known French news outlets such as Le Figaro and Libération circulated online, attempting to smear Attal by linking him to political scandals.

Some attempted to throw Attal's health into question, with one false headline claiming he'd been hospitalised, and another claiming he had Parkinson's disease.

These false headlines claim Attal's health has deteriorated. Euronews

Somewhat paradoxically, various false posts even alleged that Attal had launched a campaign against "nonexistent" Russian disinformation to try and block social media platform X.

Others said that he had paid news outlets to spread disinformation about him, and that he had considered fabricating an assassination plot against himself to try and blame Russia.

News agency AFP, which reports having seen Attal's complaint, said that the former prime minister's lawyers said the fake content could undermine the integrity of the upcoming election.

They added that France's Secretariat-General for Defence and National Security (SGDSN) and Viginum, its foreign interference watchdog, had warned Attal about the disinformation campaign targeting him.

Attal's office did not respond to a request for comment at the time of publication.

A selection of false social media posts spreading disinformation about Attal. Euronews

Following the disinformation campaign against Attal, researchers noted that the Matryoshka network shifted its focus to Édouard Philippe, another former prime minister and a contender in the presidential election.

Posts against him follow a similar pattern to those against Attal, mimicking respected media outlets such as Le Monde and AFP to mix real-life circumstances with distorted claims.

For example, one of the posts falsely claims a politician admitted Phillippe orchestrated corruption in an investigation involving the association LH French Tech.

Philippe is currently under investigation over alleged financial wrongdoing, but there is no evidence that Stéphanie de Bazelaire, who is also implicated in the investigation, made these claims, despite what the post suggests.

The probe centres on a four-year agreement worth €2.154 million between the Le Havre metropolitan authority and LH French Tech to run the city's digital innovation hub while Philippe was mayor of Le Havre.

Financial prosecutors are investigating him for the alleged embezzlement of public funds, favouritism, illegal conflict of interest and financial misconduct by a public official.

He has consistently denied wrongdoing and says he is cooperating fully with the investigation.

Other posts claim that Philippe had apologised for referring to the inhabitants of France's former colonies as "scum", and that a company owned by his wife had supplied toxic components for the Moderna COVID-19 vaccine.

However, there is no credible evidence to support either claim, nor any record of the news outlets impersonated in the posts having published these reports.

It's not the first time the Matryoshka network has targeted elections. A parallel campaign using the same methods has also aimed at candidates in Germany's upcoming September state elections.

Here, the campaign has sought to exploit historical tensions between Germany's East and West,an effort researchers say seeks to aggravate existing grievances and ultimately deepen political polarisation.

World.title: Pyongyang tests another missile within one week and ahead of US-South Korean military drills
World.content:
North Korea conducted its second ballistic missile test in less than a week on Wednesday, South Korean media reports, in what is believed to be a protest against the upcoming military exercises between Seoul and Washington, which Pyongyang sees as a practice for an invasion.

 

A ballistic missile fired from the North’s eastern coastal Wonsan area around 6 a.m. flew more than 700 kilometres, South Korea’s Joint Chiefs of Staff said.

South Korea’s military condemned the test and warned it remains ready to repel any provocation by Pyongyang in cooperation with the United States. South Korea’s national security council called North Korean ballistic missile launches “acts of provocation” and urged the North to halt them immediately.

The Japanese Defense Ministry also reported detecting the launch, saying the weapon landed in waters outside its exclusive economic zone, between the Korean Peninsula and Japan.

Defense Minister Shinjiro Koizumi told reporters that Japan strongly protested the North Korean launch through their embassies in Beijing. “It’s a serious problem that affects the safety of the Japanese people,” he said.

A TV screen shows a file image of North Korea's missile launch during a news program at Seoul Railway Station in Seoul, South Korea, Wednesday, Aug. 12, 2026. (AP Photo/Ahn Yo Ahn Young-joon/Copyright 2026 The AP. All rights reserved.

The launches, within days of each other, were seen as part of North Korea’s extended run of weapons tests as the country has refused to return to talks with the US and South Korea for years.

It also came two days after South Korea and the United States announced they will kick off their annual large-scale military drills on 17 August to beef up readiness against North Korean threats.

North Korea has previously responded to the Ulchi Freedom Shield training and other major South Korea-U.S. military exercises with provocative weapons tests and harsh rhetoric, although experts believe Pyongyang often uses its rivals’ military training as a pretext to boost its own testing activities. The US and South Korea have repeatedly said their training is defensive in nature.

After last year’s Ulchi Freedom Shield training exercises began, North Korean leader Kim Jong Un said the drills showed the US and South Korea’s “will to ignite a war” and claimed they have grown more provocative than before, which has prompted North Korea to respond with “proactive and overwhelming” countermeasures.

Last week, on 6 August, South Korea, the US, and Japan detected the launch of a short-range ballistic missile from North Korea in what was the North’s first ballistic weapons testing activity since late June.

Pyongyang didn’t confirm the reported launch, though it usually releases details of weapons tests a day later.

World.title: France swelters in new heatwave as water restrictions tighten
World.content:
France is facing another spell of intense heat. On Wednesday, the heatwave is spreading across much of the country, with 78 departments placed on orange alert. In several regions, temperatures will climb above 35°C, while in some areas, such as Corsica, the mercury could exceed 40°C on Thursday.

 

This prolonged heat is making everyday life harder for residents. In Bordeaux, as elsewhere, some people have no choice but to keep their windows closed during the day and limit their movements to the coolest hours. Nights are also proving difficult, with temperatures struggling to drop, particularly in the west of the country.

In these conditions, the authorities recommend drinking water regularly, staying cool and paying particular attention to vulnerable people, such as older people and young children. A diet rich in fruit and vegetables and cool showers can also help people cope better with the high temperatures.

But the heatwave is not the only cause for concern. The lack of rainfall (source in French) is worsening the drought. Soils remain extremely dry and small rivers are in a particularly worrying state. Nearly 1,400 waterways are thought to have run dry, according to the OFB, the French Office for Biodiversity. (source in French) Restrictions on water use now affect a very large majority of the population in mainland France and in Corsica.

This succession of heatwaves, which are becoming more frequent and more intense in the context of global warming, highlights the growing difficulties France needs to prepare for. A return to more bearable temperatures is not expected before the weekend.

World.title: Golden homecoming for Alexandri sisters to Greece: life after Austria, medals in Paris
World.content:
There are sporting triumphs that show up on results sheets, and there are triumphs that carry an entire story with them. The two gold medals won by Anna Maria and Eirini Marina Alexandri at the European Championships in Paris, in the technical and free duet of artistic swimming, as well as the honours earned by Vasiliki Alexandri in the free and technical solo, undoubtedly belong to the second category.

 

Behind them lies a journey of fourteen years, a childhood spent far from Greece, major successes with Austria, and a deep desire that stayed alive all those years: to come back one day and compete again for their country.

Together with Anna Maria and Eirini Marina, their triplet sister Vasiliki wrote her own chapter in Paris, competing in the solo event, where she finished fifth in the technical and seventh in the free programme. Her route was even more demanding, as a serious knee injury and a bout of tonsillitis shortly before the championships limited her preparation, without shaking her belief in her abilities.

Starting from scratch abroad

For the three sisters, the Europeans were not just another big event; they were the first major chapter of a new life that began when they decided to return to Greece.

Their story had started much earlier, when at just 14 they found themselves in a foreign country, without speaking the language, far from their family environment and needing to juggle school with the ever-growing demands of elite sport.

"We didn't speak the language. We had to go to school to continue our studies there. It was very difficult because we left on our own," recalls Vasiliki, describing a period in which the three sisters had to grow up much faster than their age.

In that harsh reality, however, there was something that kept them together and gave them the strength to carry on: each other. "What saved us, I would say, was that we had one another; we were together," she says.

The Alexandri sisters are coming back to Greece after years in Austria. Alexandri sisters social media

Adaptation, of course, did not happen overnight. Vasiliki still remembers how hard it was to feel away from her sisters even when they were just in the next room. "I missed them terribly. It was very difficult [...] to be away from the girls," she explains, capturing the feelings of three children who had left Greece together.

In Austria, though, they learned to endure and to fight for what they wanted. Artistic swimming became the central axis of their daily life, while the wait for citizenship was yet another test. When they were finally able to compete, the major successes soon followed, with the three sisters claiming important international titles and establishing themselves at the top of European and world artistic swimming with Austria.

New life back in Greece

Despite the successes, Greece never left their thoughts. "I believe we always had a deep desire inside us to compete for Greece," says Eirini Marina, explaining that going back was not a snap decision but a wish that had been within them for years.

She is also open about the reasons they left Greece. "We left because of a lack of meritocracy, as we have stated in the past," she notes, adding that by the time the proposal to return arrived, things had changed. "Now things have completely changed. The leadership is new. [...] All these people believed in us, supported us, and I think that is what every athlete wants."

They also make special mention of the people who stood by them from the very first moment of their return to Greece, recognising the support they were given at this new beginning. The three sisters thank the president of the Hellenic Olympic Committee, Isidoros Kouvelos, the president of the Hellenic Swimming Federation, Kyriakos Giannopoulos, as well as team manager Despina Karampela.

The decision to return, even though it meant leaving behind a life they had built from scratch, was ultimately joint and immediate. "It was a very difficult decision but also a very easy one. We took it unanimously, straight away. We said, we're all three going," says Vasiliki.

Anna Maria puts it even more emotionally: "We really wanted to come back here. Our whole family is here, our home, our friends." After 14 years, the three sisters returned to Greece, knowing that this would not simply be a homecoming, but the start of an entirely new life.

Moving and training

This change also came with very practical challenges. "We moved, we brought 200 boxes to Greece," remembers Anna Maria, while at the same time the three sisters had to adjust to their new circumstances and maintain their competitive level.

They had only five months of preparation, at a time when most of the countries they would be competing against had a full season behind them. "We had five months of training, which is very little if you think that all the other countries have 12 months of training," explains Vasiliki.

Alexandri sisters performing in Fukuoka claiming the first artistic swimming World Championship title in their nation’s history in 2023. World Aquatics

For her, the build-up was even tougher, as a serious knee injury kept her out of the water at a stage when every training session mattered hugely, while just before the Europeans she also had tonsillitis.

In Paris, she did not manage to win the two medals she had set as a personal target, but she did not leave feeling she had left anything undone. "Of course I wanted two medals; it didn't happen. I was very upset," she admits, before adding, "I don't feel any guilt because, since I gave 100%, I couldn't have done anything more."

The next opportunity is already ahead of her, anyway, as she notes: "Next year we have the World Championships and the European Games, and there it is definitely my goal to win the two medals that, in inverted commas, I 'lost' this year."

Search for roots

For Anna Maria and Eirini Marina, Paris had a special emotional dimension. Before the championships, they had said they wanted very much to hear the Greek national anthem – and in the end, they experienced it twice.

"We had said before we went to the championships that we really wanted to hear the national anthem," says Anna Maria. That moment was not just the peak of a competition, but a distillation of their entire journey. "Our whole journey passed before us, before our eyes, especially from March when we came to Greece, because that was a big step and a big change for us," she recalls.

The emotion was also linked to the fact that this time they were competing for a country which, despite the years spent away, they still saw as home.

"Our whole family is here, our home, our friends. We are very happy and moved that we now compete for Greece," says Anna Maria, who admits that even everyday life in Greece feels different. "Even when I go out just for a walk, I feel differently than I did in Austria. [...] Here I enjoy it in another way."

The love of the public also played an important part in their return. They speak with particular emotion about the moments when people approach them in the street, congratulate them or talk to them about their achievements. "All of Greece has embraced us and we want to say a big thank you to everyone in Greece for the love we have received," says Anna Maria.

A mother behind the athletes

Behind the three sisters, however, there is another person who has played a decisive role throughout this journey: their mother. She was the one who saw her three children leave home to start their lives in another country, knowing that this choice would change her own life as well.

"Her home emptied: from having three children there, suddenly she was left alone," says Anna Maria, adding that, despite the hardship, their mother fully backed their choice: "She supported 100% our fight and our wishes [...] We owe her everything."

The relationship between the three sisters remains one of their greatest strengths. They are not just teammates, but people who, since childhood, have shared the same anxieties, the same sacrifices, the same joys, and the same disappointments. "I am very proud and blessed with what we have between us, the three of us, and with our mother," says Vasiliki, describing a family that stayed close-knit despite the distance and the changes.

The Alexandri sisters euronews/Δουλγκέρη

Now, though, their story is not only about their own past. The three sisters want their return to Greece to be an opportunity to help the new generation of artistic swimming, passing on to younger girls the experience they have gained from 14 years of elite sport abroad.

Eirini Marina says they have already spoken with younger athletes and believes that sharing what they have lived through is a way for everyone to move forward together. "We want to inspire in a positive way, to support the new generation," she says.

Looking back, she does not see the hardships as wasted time or as a chapter she would rather have skipped. On the contrary, she believes that everything that happened made them who they are today.

"Every difficulty, even the fact that we were forced to leave Greece, all that shaped us," she says. "I think we also went beyond our limits – and beyond limits we never even imagined we had."

The two gold medals in Paris, then, are not just the final line of a results sheet. They are the outcome of a journey that began when three girls left Greece at 14 and learned to grow up far from home, always having one another.

They are the continuation of a path that took them to the top of Europe with Austria and ultimately brought them back to Greece, this time with the desire to create here the next chapter of their lives and their careers.

And if there is one thing that best sums up their attitude today, it is that they do not see the golds in Paris as the end of the road. "I believe we still have a lot to give and that we haven't got there yet," says Anna Maria. Vasiliki, for her part, puts it in a way that encapsulates their whole philosophy: "My goal every time is to show up improved and to be the best version of myself. And then, if the medal comes, it is welcome."

Their gaze is now fixed on the next major events: the World Championships in Budapest in the summer of 2027, the European Games a little earlier, and finally, the Olympic Games in 2028 in Los Angeles.

World.title: Europe scrambles for eclipse glasses as solar power output set to dip
World.content:
The eclipse will be the first total solar eclipse visible from Europe since 2006. The path of totality will cross northern Spain, Portugal, Iceland, Greenland and northern Russia. London is expected to see around 90 per cent of the Sun obscured, while shoppers in Paris queued for more than two hours outside a specialist store on Rue de Rivoli.

 

In Spain, where several areas lie within the path of totality, many distribution points have already sold out. Pharmacies in central Madrid have been selling certified glasses for between €3 and €4 a pair, while prices in France range from €1.50 to €5.95.

In London, one shopkeeper was limiting customers to a single pair as stocks fell to around 100. In Brussels, optician Fouad Mehdaoui was taking orders by phone and adding customers to a waiting list after securing a last-minute restock.

The eclipse is also expected to cause a temporary drop in solar power generation across Europe. Grid operator association ENTSO-E estimates that output could fall by up to 9.7 gigawatts between 19:15 and 21:30 CET, with the largest reductions expected in Spain and Germany.

Solar power currently accounts for around 13 per cent of Europe’s electricity generation. Grid operators have prepared control rooms, arranged back-up generation and postponed planned maintenance to manage the temporary fall in output.

France’s grid operator RTE expects solar generation to drop by around 1.8 gigawatts, while German operators are preparing for a reduction of roughly 2 gigawatts. Despite the scale of the change, transmission system operators say they do not expect the eclipse to threaten the security of Europe’s electricity supply.

World.title: Solar eclipse: What to look forward to
World.content:
The last solar eclipse visible from the European mainland was in 1999. Here's what to expect, and how to prepare for this rare occasion.

On Wednesday, about 980 million people across parts of the Northern Hemisphere will have the chance to observe this upcoming solar eclipse.

They will be joined by hosts of researchers who will be taking advantage of the fleeting minutes when the sun's corona is visible from Earth to test specialized instruments and capture rare images. With them, they hope to gain a deeper appreciation of the material above the sun's surface .

What's going to happen?

During a solar eclipse, the moon orbits between Earth and the sun during the daytime, casting a shadow which temporarily darkens the sky and appears to blot out the sun. At the height of an eclipse, the moon's disk appears to align with the sun, revealing the sun's corona — its outermost atmosphere that flares outward like a crown (hence the name).

As the moon approaches and the sky darkens, you might also notice the temperature dropping, shadows appearing crescent-shaped, the wind beginning to shift and animals behaving unusually.

Eclipse fever sweeps Spain ahead of rare spectacle To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Solar panels will be able to produce less energy in this time. In Germany, this is expected to lead to a brief surge in electricity prices.

Right before the eclipse reaches its maximum point, known as totality, watch out for Baily's beads. These are the final rays of sun reaching Earth through valleys on the moon's surface. They appear as white specks encircling the moon like a string of pearls.

As night closes in during totality, keep an eye out for the stars that appear. Some might even be able to catch a glimpse of auroras or passing meteors.

Where will the eclipse occur?

If you live in Greenland, Iceland, northern Russia, northern Spain or northeastern Portugal, you're in luck! Viewers in these locations will be able to observe a total solar eclipse.

In most of Western Europe, as well as parts of northern Africa and northern America, astronomy enthusiasts will still be able to watch a partial solar eclipse.

And this is just the first of two eclipses in August. The second will take place on August 27-28, when Earth moves between the sun and the moon to create a lunar eclipse.

The next solar eclipse will happen February 2, 2027, over much of Africa, South America, as well as parts of Antarctica.

While eclipses themselves are fairly frequent occurrences, it's not that often that a total solar eclipse is visible on inhabited parts of the globe. The last solar eclipse visible for most of mainland Europe, for example, was in 1999.

What time is the eclipse happening?

The spectacle will begin at 15:34 GMT, with the moon slowly dimming the sun's light as it creeps into position. About two hours later, at 17:46 GMT, the eclipse will reach totality for about two minutes.

But where on the globe you are watching from will make a difference. While Icelanders will be able to observe the eclipse's totality at 17:48 GMT, viewers in Spain will have to wait until 18:27 for their chance.

Where can I watch the eclipse?

Since the eclipse is happening relatively late in the day, viewers are recommended to watch from high places to catch a good view of the sun as it dips toward the horizon. Most west-facing hills, towers and (safe) rooftops with an unobstructed view should do the trick.

If you're the kind who prefers crisper images, NASA is also offering a livestream .

Can I wear normal sunglasses to watch the eclipse?

In short, no. Looking directly into the sun can cause permanent damage to the retina at the back of your eye. Ordinary sunglasses, even polarized ones, are far too weak to provide enough protection.

Instead, you'll need certified ISO 12312-2 glasses, available at most pharmacies and opticians. Most are sold out already, but there are plenty of directions online for building a pinhole camera to safely watch the eclipse with small children.

You can also use a kitchen colander, or any other tool with small holes, to project tiny crescent-shaped shadows onto a safe surface.

Whether or not you are wearing eclipse glasses, never look at the sun through a camera, telescope or binoculars without a specialized filter, as the concentrated light can cause serious damage to your eyes.

Drones are increasingly being used in modern hybrid warfare Image: Felix Kästle/dpa/picture alliance

Several hundred security incidents involvingdrones have been registered by Germany's armed forces in the past years, a military spokesman has said.

"Since the start of the illegal full-scale Russian invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, reports on drone sightings affecting the Bundeswehr have greatly increased," the spokesman told the media outlet Redaktionsnetzwerk Deutschland.

"Over the past few years, several hundred suspected drone overflights in Bundeswehr-related areas have been reported," he said, adding that whole swarms of drones had been sighted on occasion.

Germany has seen a number of drone incidents in recent weeks, including one involving a drone carrying explosives at the Leipzig-Halle airport.

According to the newsmagazine Spiegel, the Hannover-Langenhagen airport was also closed several times overnight to Tuesday after a drone was sighted by employees.

Spiegel reported that the drone did not show up on police detection devices, suggesting that the object was possibly not a commercially available model.

The captain of an Air India flight from Phuket to Delhi that suddenly lost altitude last week tested positive for marijuana in a confirmatory drug test.

World.title: Pakistan says 3 nationals killed in Houthi Red Sea attack
World.content:
Pakistan's foreign minister has said Islamabad "strongly condemns" Houthi attacks on commercial vessels while offering condolences to the families of the dead.

At least three Pakistani nations were killed in an "incident involving an attack on a commercial vessel in the Red Sea," Pakistan's Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar said on Wednesday.

Another Pakistani national had sustained injuries.

"Pakistan strongly condemns the Houthi attack on a non-combatant commercial vessel. Such attacks endanger innocent lives, constitute a violation of international law, and pose a serious threat to freedom of navigation, maritime security, and the safety of commercial shipping in the Red Sea," the minister said in a post on X.

Pakistan's Foreign Ministry was in contact with Saudi Arabia and Yemen to ascertain further details of the incident, Dar said. Meanwhile, the Pakistani Embassy in Riyadh was coordinating the retrieval and repatriation of the mortal remains of their deceased nationals.

Vessels under attack amid Middle East conflict

On Tuesday, the US and Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi rebels reported separate attacks on shipping as peace negotiations between Washington and Tehran seemingly stagnated once again.

At the southern end of the Red Sea, a suspected Houthi attack on a small cargo vessel killed four crew members, Yemen's Transport Ministry said. It was not immediately clear is this was the same vessel Dar was referring to.

Commercial shipping and seafarers passing through the Middle East have increasingly come under attack by both the US and Iran since the conflict began earlier this year.

World.title: Australia approves new rules benefiting gig delivery workers
World.content:
Delivery drivers in Australia are to be guaranteed "world-leading" higher pay and insurance cover on the job. The move could be a model for other countries.

Food and grocery delivery workers in Australia will be paid at least A$31.30 (€19.15, $22.11) an hour and be given accident insurance on the job under new rules approved by Australia's industrial relations tribunal.

The hourly rate, set out in an order issued by the Fair Work Commission (FWC) on Tuesday, is above Australia's minimum wage of A$26.44.

The FWC's order, which could serve as a precedent for other countries, has been hailed by the Transport Workers Union (TWU) as "a landmark moment for the Australian gig economy." The union called the new rules a "world-leading set of standards."

What rights and protects did the FWC give gig delivery drivers?

The minimum hourly rate will be paid for "engaged" time, i.e. the time between taking on a delivery job and completing the commission.

The order, which takes effect on August 17, also requires companies to provide a "reasonable minimum level of cover" ​for personal accident insurance on the job, without specifying exactly how much.

The workers will, however, still be responsible for maintaining ⁠third-party ⁠insurance for the vehicles used for deliveries.

Unions and workers in Australia ​have long sought ⁠reforms benefiting gig workers.

They have previously not been covered by many of the protections given to other employees, being classified as "independent contractors."

The new rules are expected to affect some 250,000 workers.

Gig workers worldwide encounter exploitative work conditions To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

UN moves to protect gig workers

The FWC's order comes after the United Nations' International Labour Organization (ILO) in June adopted a new global treaty for decent working conditions in the gig economy.

The standards laid down in the treaty, the first global treaty of its kind, still need ratification by governments.

In Australia, the parliament passed legislation in 2023 and 2024 under the center-left Labor government that granted gig workers more negotiating rights over minimum pay and working conditions.

Those laws gave the FWC the power to set rules for pay and insurance.

World.title: Indonesia: Passengers rescued after Bali ferry catches fire
World.content:
Rescue officials said they didn't find out about the fire until half an hour after it began. A survivor claimed that help didn't arrive for hours after the blaze broke out.

Indonesian authorities rescued 172 people from a burning ferry on Wednesday near the tourist island of Bali.

At least one person, a 19-year-old woman, was killed in the incident, officials said.

The fire broke out on the Padang Bai-Lembar ferry route connecting Bali and Lombok and is also used by tourists travelling between the two popular destinations.

It is the second major ferry fire in Indonesia this month.

What Indonesian authorities said about the ferry fire

Muhammad Hariyadi, who heads the Mataram Search and Rescue Office, had initially told Metro TV that all passengers had been deboarded from the burning ferry.

"We have approached the ship and confirmed that all passengers are no longer on board," he said. "We visually see no passengers on the ship."

Visuals released by Indonesian authorities showed black smoke billowing from the burning ferry in Bali waters Image: BASARNAS/AP Photo/picture alliance

Later, Hariyadi told reporters that a woman had been declared dead.

The ferry was estimated to be carrying 114 passengers and 17 crew members, Hariyadi had said referring to the passenger manifest data released by Padang Bai's port authority.

However, the final tally of passengers and crew was significantly above the 131 people estimated.

The Indonesian National Search and Rescue Agency (BASARNAS), crew pull survivors to safety Image: BASARNAS/AP Photo/picture alliance

What else do we know about the fire and rescue efforts?

Fire broke out on board the Putri Yasmin Ferry at about 4:15 a.m. (1045 GMT) while it was en route from Padang Bai port in Bali to Lembar port on the adjacent island of Lombok, according to the search office in Mataram.

The agency received an emergency report nearly half an hour later and then deployed rescue vessels and personnel.

Survivor Kiky Okta Pradika, 25, told reporters in Lembar he had grabbed a life jacket before jumping overboard with several other passengers."There were a few hours before there was any help," he said.

The burning ferry was in the midst of rough seas with waves as high as 4 meters (13 feet), Hariyadi said, adding that conditions had complicated rescue efforts.

A ferry in the vicinity had evacuated 30 passengers and brought them to Bali. A search and rescue vessel was on its way to Lembar port with 59 of the rescued passengers. A naval vessel picked up another 17 passengers.

Some rescued passengers were taken to a port in Bali while others were taken to the Lombok island Image: Lana Priatna/AFP

Two of the rescued passengers were Australian tourists.

Marine safety in Indonesia

Marine accidents are a regular occurrence in Indonesia where ferries are a common mode of transport.

Last week, five people died in a ferry fire off the coast of Java Island. Last month, a ferry transporting more than 70 people sank while sailing near Seayar Island. The rescue operation had been closed after four bodies were recovered, but 14 were officially still missing.

And in July last year, a ferry sank while travelling between Java and Bali, killing nearly 20 people.

World.title: North Korea tests missile ahead of US-South Korea drills
World.content:
The suspected ballistic missile was launched towards Japan and likely fell just outside of its special economic zone, Tokyo said.

North Korea test-fired a ballistic missile off its east coast towards Japan early on Wednesday, its neighbors said, just days before US-South Korea Joint Military drills which Pyongyang views as invasion rehearsals.

This is the second such test in less than a week.

"Our military detected at around 6:00 am (2100 GMT on Tuesday) a ballistic missile launched by North Korea from the Wonsan area towards the East Sea," Seoul's Joint Chiefs of Staff said in a message to reporters.

Japan's Defence Minister Shinjiro Koizumi called the launch a "threat to peace and security in our region," adding that Tokyo had lodged a strong protest with North Korea through diplomatic channels in Beijing.

"It's a serious problem that affects the safety of the Japanese people," he said at a press conference.

Here's what we know about North Korea's test-launch from Japan:

North Korea launched at least one ballistic missile on Wednesday morning

Details were under close joint analysis between Japan, the US and South Korea

Missile estimated to have fallen outside Japan's exclusive economic zone in the Sea of Japan

Japan's prime minister issued instructions to maintain a complete state of readiness

No reports of damage have been confirmed

North's message ahead of joint military drills

The suspected ballistic missile launch came just two days after South Korea and the US announced that they will kick off their annual joint military drills on August 17.

The upcoming drills are a regular summer feature, designed to coordinate their defense against the nuclear-armed Pyongyang.

North Korea has condemned these drills on several occasions before, often staging missile tests before and after the exercises.

"North Korea has never simply let a South Korea-US joint military exercise pass without a response," said Lim Eul-chul, a North Korea expert at Kyungnam University.

"This is a message that Pyongyang is closely watching the upcoming drills and could stage a provocation if it deems one necessary," he said.

After last year's drills began, North Korean leader Kim Jong Un claimed the exercise had grown more provocative than before and showed Seoul and Washington's "will to ignite a war." He said it had prompted North Korea to respond with “proactive and overwhelming” countermeasures.

On August 6, the US, South Korea and Japan detected the launch of a short-range ballistic missile from the North in what was its first ballistic weapons testing activity since late June.

Pyongyang, which ususally releases details of tests a day later, did not initially confirm the launch.

World.title: Drone attack hits Libya's largest oil refinery
World.content:
Fires broke out at the Zawiya oil complex after explosives-laden drones struck the site. Hours later, fresh violence in Benghazi highlighted Libya's persistent security challenges.

Libya's National Oil Corporation (NOC) said Tuesday that fires at a fuel storage facility had been quickly brought under control after a drone attack.

The Zawiya oil complex west of Tripoli is home to the country's largest refinery and has been the scene of repeated armed clashes between warring factions fighting for primacy in the country since the fall of former strongman leader Moammar Gadhafi in 2011.

What happened in the drone attack on Libya's Zawiya oil refinery?

Monday's attack by an as yet undeclared actor targeted the Zawiya Oil Refining Company with explosives-laden drones, causing a tank containing about 4.5 million liters (1.2 million gallons) of gasoline to collapse after a fire.

Owner Brega Petroleum Marketing said the fires had been brought under control far faster than expected, with engineers telling Reuters news agency that damage had been limited, though operations were interrupted.

In a statement on X, Abdulhamid Dbeibah, Libya's internationally recognized prime minister, wrote that the crime of targeting civilian infrastructure would "not go unanswered."

Libya's UN-recognized Prime Minister Abdulhamid Dbeibah condemned the drone attack on the Zawiya oil complex, saying the targeting of civilian infrastructure would "not go unanswered" [FILE: October 13, 2022] Image: Yousef Murad/AP Photo/picture alliance

"The use of drones to strike vital facilities," wrote Dbeibah, "is not a random incident, but rather an organized and dangerous act that requires a firm response to protect the state and its institutions and prevent its recurrence."

Officials from Libya's electricity provider said two further drones targeted the Zawiya power plant early Tuesday morning, with one hitting the fire-fighting system but causing no damage.

What is the security situation in divided Libya?

Libya has remained divided since the 2011 uprising that toppled Gadhafi. Dbeibah's UN-recognized government is based in Tripoli in the west, while eastern and parts of southern Libya are controlled by the Libyan National Army (LNA), a military force led by commander Khalifa Haftar.

Amid those tensions, the LNA said its head of military intelligence, Fawzi al-Mansouri, was killed in a car bombing in Benghazi on Monday night.

According to the LNA, an explosive device attached to al-Mansouri's vehicle detonated as he left a mosque. Authorities have not identified those responsible.

Khalifa Haftar commands the Libyan National Army (LNA), which controls eastern Libya and parts of the country’s south [FILE: September 5, 2024] Image: Abdullah Doma/AFP/Getty Images

Khaled Haftar, one of Khalifa Haftar's sons, said an investigation had been opened, adding that initial "indicators point to a despicable terrorist tactic," according to AFP news agency.

His office later said authorities had arrested a "terrorist cell" in Benghazi that was allegedly preparing acts of sabotage, but did not say whether it was linked to al-Mansouri's killing.

Al-Mansouri was a prominent military figure close to the Haftar family and had played a key role in fighting jihadist groups in eastern Libya.

How has Libya's political division affected oil production?

The split between dueling administrations has stunted the country's oil producing progress and kept foreign investors wary as rival sides clash over control of the oil revenues that pour into the Central Bank of Libya.

In 2024, a standoff over control of the bank slashed the country's oil exports by more than half.

Libya holds Africa's largest proven oil reserves, yet has struggled to return to pre-2011 production levels of 1.6 million barrels per day. June production hit 1.44 million barrels per day, the highest output levels since 2013, but far short of its target of 2 million barrels per day.

World.title: Se acabó la espera: España vivirá su primer eclipse de Sol total del siglo
World.content:
Millones de españoles y turistas ultiman los preparativos para ver, sobre las 20.30, cómo la Luna cubre completamente el Sol. Estas son las claves de un fenómeno acompañado de un enorme desafío logístico

El ritual comenzará pasadas las 19.30 en los primeros puntos del noroeste peninsular. Millones de españoles y turistas levantarán la mirada hacia el horizonte para ver un evento astronómico ancestral y fascinante: comprobarán cómo se va haciendo de noche en pleno día, mientras la Luna cubre completamente el Sol en el primer eclipse total en cruzar la Península en 121 años, de Galicia a Baleares, que será visible en su totalidad en buena parte de la mitad norte peninsular.

El fenómeno astronómico, que se produce por la alineación de la Tierra con la Luna y el Sol, pasa de media una vez cada 18 meses en alguna parte del mundo. Lo extraordinario es que pase justo por encima de nuestras cabezas, sin tener que desplazarnos miles de kilómetros. Por eso, pocos quieren perdérselo y estos días las zonas más deshabitadas de la España interior, que ofrecen miradores privilegiados para el eclipse, están llenas de gente que busca el mejor punto para verlo. A los veraneantes habituales que llegan cada año de las ciudades y multiplican la población de pueblos y aldeas semivacías, se han sumado quienes eligieron estos municipios por sus cielos limpios, los miles que se desplazarán en estas últimas horas para no perderse el evento y los que cambien de ubicación en el último momento por temor a que las nubes les estropeen la fiesta.

Pero el fenómeno que desata la fascinación de la población es también un desafío logístico para las autoridades, que han anunciado un enorme despliegue para tratar que el eclipse se produzca sin incidentes. En primer lugar, está la recomendación para la salud de no mirar nunca a la luz del Sol —aunque esté parcialmente cubierto—, sin gafas especiales protectoras. A eso se le suma el plan de Tráfico para tratar de evitar atascos y accidentes en los hasta 1,5 millones de desplazamientos que se esperan y que se concentrarán en un puñado de carreteras y en pocas horas. Y también las recomendaciones para prevenir incendios en un mes en el que España está especialmente calurosa y seca, en riesgo extremo de incendios forestales. Porque, mientras miramos al Sol, no hay que olvidarse de cuidar la Tierra.

En EL PAÍS, les compartimos algunas claves del evento astronómico, que también se ha convertido en un movilizador social, económico y cultural para disfrutarlo con seguridad:

El enorme desafío logístico

En pleno 12 de agosto, los Gobiernos central, autonómicos y municipales deben hacer frente a las necesidades logísticas que generan millones de personas moviéndose a la vez y con un mismo objetivo. Será como una operación salida, pero en un solo día y con concentraciones en puntos inesperados.

El Gobierno prevé entre 400.000 y 1,5 millones de desplazamientos adicionales a los habituales desde zonas donde el fenómeno se observará parcialmente hacia el área de la totalidad, según ha señalado este martes el Ministerio de Ciencia y Universidades, citando una estimación de la Dirección General de Tráfico (DGT), que tendrá un dispositivo especial de vigilancia. En total, se desplegarán más de 24.000 guardias civiles y 9.400 agentes de la Policía Nacional para garantizar la seguridad.

La recomendación de las autoridades, para quienes tengan que desplazarse, es hacerlo “con mucha planificación”, hacer el regreso de manera escalonada, evitar paradas en arcenes que puedan interrumpir la actuación de los servicios de emergencias y llevar los suministros necesarios por si tuvieran que pasar más tiempo del esperado en la carretera. El riesgo es que se incrementen los atascos y accidentes como sucedió en otros países, como en los eclipses totales de Estados Unidos de 2017 y 2024.

También podrían caerse las comunicaciones por saturación. Y hay un temor especial por el riesgo de incendios. La ministra para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico, Sara Aagesen, ha dado este martes “varias recomendaciones sencillas y esenciales” a los ciudadanos para cuidar el entorno natural mientras observan el eclipse: “Prohibido encender fuego, no aparcar sobre vegetación seca, mantener los accesos libres para emergencias y consultar diariamente el nivel de peligro de incendios. El día del eclipse solar total es un día para disfrutar, pero también una llamada a la prudencia y a la precaución”, ha dicho.

Impacto económico y turístico

La expectación en torno al eclipse se traduce en beneficios para las provincias agraciadas por la lotería astronómica. Un informe del Ministerio de Economía, Comercio y Empresa presentado a finales de julio estima que las zonas de la totalidad recibirán 446.700 visitantes adicionales esta semana por el eclipse, que aportarán a la economía 347,6 millones de euros. Cerca del 37% son extranjeros.

También se ha visto un incremento en las reservas de plazas hoteleras y de restaurantes en la zona de la totalidad, donde los precios se han disparado. Según un análisis de más de 5.500 anuncios en Booking publicado la semana pasada por EL PAÍS, en 90 días, los precios se multiplicaron por seis en Soria, donde una habitación estaba en torno a unos 900 euros, o por ocho en Zaragoza, donde costaba en torno a los 500.

Dónde verlo

Para disfrutar de una experiencia plena, los astrónomos recomiendan, en primer lugar, estar en una zona de la totalidad, es decir, que se vaya a oscurecer al 100%. Dicen que las sensaciones en una zona en la que el Sol se cubre por completo no tienen nada que ver con aquellas en las que se cubre al 99%, aunque en la fase previa pueden ser muy similares. Lo que observaremos en ese punto álgido del fenómeno es la oscuridad total que, si el cielo está despejado, nos permitirá ver la desconocida corona solar con nuestros propios ojos. Esos filamentos plateados que rodean al Sol son la parte externa de su atmósfera, pero generalmente están ocultos por el propio brillo de la estrella.

Para quienes prefieren verlo acompañados o no han tenido tiempo de elegir un mirador propio cerca de su casa o su lugar de vacaciones, las comunidades autónomas y los municipios han seleccionado cientos de puntos oficiales. Son ubicaciones desde donde el eclipse tendrá buena visibilidad y que contarán con su propio dispositivo de seguridad y emergencias. En algunas de ellas, además, distribuirán gafas de protección.

Mapa de miradores oficiales donde ver el eclipse total de Sol EL PAÍS completa un buscador con casi 500 miradores oficiales

A qué hora es exactamente

Aunque en los primeros lugares de la península el Sol comenzará a eclipsarse sobre las 19.30 y la experiencia completa durará cerca de dos horas, el punto cumbre, el de la totalidad, no durará más de 1 minuto y 50 segundos para los más afortunados; y serán solo unos pocos segundos para los que estén en las zonas más periféricas de la totalidad.

Los primeros lugares de España que se oscurecerán completamente por la sombra de la Luna sobre el Sol son Cabo de Peñas, en Asturias, y Estaca de Bares, en A Coruña, pasadas las 20.26 de la tarde, y el último será el Faro de la Mola, en Formentera, sobre las 20.33, antes de que el eclipse desaparezca con la puesta de Sol.

Para saber las horas exactas en las que pasará el fenómeno en un lugar concreto, pueden consultar en el buscador del Instituto Geográfico Nacional (IGN). La web oficial creada por el Ministerio de Ciencia, Tecnología y Universidades para el Trío de Eclipses ofrece también un visor que simula dónde estará el Sol en una localización determinada a la hora del eclipse.

El lío de las gafas: entonces, ¿cuándo y cómo usarlas?

Las gafas para ver eclipses como hoy las conocemos fueron desarrolladas por astrónomos y ópticos en la década de 1970 para que podamos mirar directamente al Sol en estos fenómenos sin poner en riesgo nuestra vista, así que esta será la primera vez en la historia de nuestro país en que podamos ver un eclipse de Sol total en España con este elemento de protección, que en los últimos días ha sido altamente cotizado en tiendas y farmacias.

La clave es llevarlas siempre que miremos directamente al Sol, es decir, durante la mayor parte del fenómeno. Con ellas, podremos ver cómo la Luna va cubriendo el Sol poco a poco y, después, cómo el Sol va saliendo nuevamente. Las gafas de protección ISO 12312-2 solo se las pueden retirar quienes están en la zona de la totalidad cuando el Sol está completamente cubierto, es decir, en la oscuridad total. Solo así podrán apreciar la corona solar.

Para usarlas de manera correcta y no dañarse la vista, es importante saber cuánto va a durar la totalidad en el lugar donde se va a ver el eclipse y volvérselas a poner antes de que la luz solar aparezca de nuevo por detrás de la Luna.

El regalo de las perseidas

Al contrario de los precios astronómicos de muchos de los hoteles de la zona de la totalidad, mirar al cielo todavía es gratis y este 12 de agosto, el universo tiene reservado un regalo doble para quien se quede observando las estrellas poco después del eclipse, cuando anochezca: será el pico de máxima actividad de las Perseidas o ‘Lágrimas de San Lorenzo’, la lluvia de estrellas más conocida del año. Que coincidan los dos fenómenos en un solo día es, como explica Daniel Medavilla en el video que acompaña este artículo, “una coincidencia cósmica que se da cada muchos milenios”. De hecho, los últimos humanos que vieron los dos fenómenos juntos fueron los neandertales.

Y si se van a perder este fenómeno porque están fuera de la banda de la totalidad, pronto habrá una nueva oportunidad, porque España ha sido agraciada con una particular lotería astronómica estos años en los que vivirá lo que se ha llamado un Trío de Eclipses. El próximo año, en 2027, el extremo sur de la Península, Ceuta y Melilla recibirán otro eclipse de Sol total. Y en 2028, será el turno de otro anular.

World.title: 16 pueblos españoles que piden manga larga cuando cae la tarde
World.content:
Vielha (Lleida). La gran baza de los pueblos seleccionados radica, sobre todo, en la posibilidad de tener que taparse para descansar, algo que se ha convertido en todo un lujo durante la canícula. Es un requisito que cumple Vielha, a la vera de los ríos Garona y Nere, con su casco histórico construido a la manera aranesa, a golpe de piedra, pizarra y madera. Sus mínimas descenderán hasta los 12ºC la noche del domingo; las máximas alcanzarán picos de 33ºC en las horas centrales del jueves y viernes, pero bajarán a los 24ºC (y con probabilidad de lluvias) el lunes, según la Aemet. La capital del Valle de Arán se presenta como un buen campamento base para conocer este territorio del Pirineo catalán, con sus 33 núcleos de población, sus algo más de 10.000 habitantes y sus iglesias románicas. Es recomendable acercarse a la cascada Saut deth Pish, probablemente la más bonita de la zona. Más información: visitvaldaran.com/descubre-la-val-daran/pueblos/vielha/.

Los tres restantes, aplazados para que los equipos puedan contar con todos sus futbolistas, se disputarán a finales de mes: el Valencia-Real Betis, el día 25; el Real Madrid-Real Sociedad, el 26 y cerrará la jornada el 27 el FC Barcelona-Athletic Club, dos de los equipos que más jugadores aportaron al combinado español con 11 estrellas. Por su parte, el pistoletazo de salida a LALIGA HYPERMOTION será el viernes 14 con el duelo que enfrenta al filial de la Real Sociedad contra el CD Castellón, una de las revelaciones de la pasada campaña que se quedó a las puertas del ascenso.

Como cada temporada, los equipos ultiman sus plantillas. Llegan nuevas caras y viejos conocidos que elevan el nivel de LALIGA EA SPORTS. Nombres como el de Sergio Canales, que regresa al R. Racing Club tras una estancia en México; Anthony Gordon, estrella de la selección inglesa que llega al FC Barcelona o el de José Mourinho, en su vuelta al banquillo del Real Madrid.

Pasó por el Real Madrid, el Valencia CF y la Real Sociedad; brilló en el Real Betis (164 partidos ligueros, 30 goles y 25 asistencias) y ahora vuelve a su tierra tras tres años en la liga mexicana. Mandi, internacional con Argelia en 114 ocasiones y capitán, jugó 206 partidos en la máxima categoría del fútbol profesional español entre 2016 y 2024, primero en el Real Betis y luego en el Villarreal CF. En la imagen, el central, en una disputa con Lionel Messi durante el Mundial. La jornada empieza en el bar

Los aficionados que quieran vivir el fútbol en un ambiente diferente también pueden hacerlo en los miles de bares que cuentan con los paquetes oficiales de retransmisión. Con un doble valor añadido: los futboleros que decidan acudir a su establecimiento de confianza contribuyen al crecimiento y a la dinamización del sector HORECA y refuerzan, con su visita, la cultura de la previa y el pospartido, lo que demuestra que el fútbol también puede ser una experiencia social que va mucho más allá de los 90 minutos.

Además, a lo largo de la temporada, LALIGA llevará a las pantallas de los bares oficiales concursos, sorteos y premios exclusivos, ofreciendo a los aficionados nuevas formas de participar y disfrutar de la competición mientras viven el partido en su segunda grada.

Hazte fan de LALIGA y participa en sorteos para ganar premios

Ampuero, la primera activación de LALIGA BARES Tras 14 años de ausencia, el regreso del Racing a LALIGA EA SPORTS (domingo 16, 17.00 horas) servirá para la primera activación de la temporada de LALIGA BARES , la plataforma que pone a los bares en el corazón del fútbol profesional. Con motivo del partido, LALIGA se desplazará a Ampuero (Cantabria), localidad natal del capitán santanderino Íñigo Sainz-Maza, con el objetivo conectar el fútbol profesional con historias que entrelazan la identidad del territorio y la hostelería. Sainz-Maza, protagonista del segundo episodio de 42 Legados , un proyecto audiovisual de PRISA y LALIGA, no solo es uno de los vecinos más queridos de su puebluco, sino que personaliza la resistencia y la humildad que caracterizan a la afición santanderina. La activación guarda, además, una sorpresa: la presencia de una leyenda del club montañés.

World.title: Dos senderos idóneos para explorar el Valle de Arán en verano
World.content:
En la zona occidental de la comarca pirenaica esperan la Artiga de Lin y la Val de Toran. Cascadas, mariposas, pequeños pueblos y antiguos caminos para el contrabando que se disfrutan sin multitudes

Que levanten la mano quienes hayan estado en Baqueira, Salardú o Artíes. ¡Hala, cuánta gente! Ese es el Naut Aran (el Alto Arán, en aranés), al que más de un millón de personas acuden en invierno a esquiar. Que la levanten ahora quienes hayan estado en Es Bòrdes o en Canejan. Ni la décima parte. Esta zona occidental del Valle de Arán, por la que corren el río Garona y la carretera N230 poco antes de entrar en Francia, no es tan famosa como la oriental, pero por eso mismo está rodeada de montañas silenciosas, virginales, sin remontes ni aparcamientos para 1.600 vehículos.

Cuando la nieve se retira, aquí se ven flores, mariposas y cascadas. Hay dos senderos idóneos para explorarla: el que recorre el pasmoso valle de la Artiga de Lin, donde surgen a chorros las aguas del glaciar del Aneto después de circular casi cuatro kilómetros bajo tierra, y el camino del Contrabando, entre Canejan y Sant Joan de Toran, por el que los vecinos traficaban durante la posguerra con café y azúcar de la vecina Francia.

Los Ojos de Júpiter, del Diablo o del Judío

La Artiga de Lin es el paraje natural más espectacular de la comarca. En este valle glaciar hay dos lugares difíciles de creer: a 1.370 metros de altura, se encuentra la surgencia de los Uelhs deth Joèu (­los Ojos de Júpiter, del Diablo o del Judío, que de las tres formas lo traducen), donde brotan 1.580 litros de agua por segundo —y hasta 10.000 en pleno deshielo—. Cien metros más arriba, a 1.470, está el Plan dera Artiga, una gran pradera alpina rodeada de hayedos, abetales y escarpadas montañas calizas a casi 3.000 metros de altura donde lindan el Valle de Arán y el de Benasque, Lleida y Huesca, Cataluña y Aragón.

Surgencia de los Uhels deth Joèu, en la Artiga de Lin. Andrés Campos

A diferencia de lo que ocurre en la zona oriental del Valle de Arán, aquí no se puede aparcar a pie de pista porque no hay ninguna. Tampoco hay atascos porque los meses de mayor afluencia de visitantes en esta zona, los estivales, es obligatorio estacionar junto a la ermita dera Mair de Diu dera Artiga de Lin, tres kilómetros antes de llegar al final de la estrecha carretera que sube culebreando por el valle desde el pueblo de Es Bòrdes. Luego se puede continuar subiendo por el asfalto en un trenecito turístico o hacerlo a pie por el camino del Agua, que es una senda ribereña fácil y preciosa.

Siguiendo el camino, antes de una hora se verá la surgencia de los Uelhs deth Joèu. “¿De dónde sale tanta agua?“, se preguntan todos los que examinan por primera vez este nacedero torrencial, porque aunque su caudal medio se reduce en verano a 250 litros por segundo, sigue siendo mucha fuente. Pues resulta que sale del Aneto, el techo de los Pirineos, en la vecina Huesca. Y se sabe porque, en 1931, el espeleólogo francés Norbert Casteret vertió 60 kilos de colorante inocuo en el Forau d’Aigualluts —un sumidero kárstico del valle de Benasque donde las aguas recién fundidas del glaciar del Aneto desaparecen bajo tierra después de pegar un buen salto—, y comprobó que estas aparecían teñidas en los Uelhs. Así que estas aguas nacidas al sur de los Pirineos, en vez de ir al Ebro y al Mediterráneo, que sería lo lógico, corren cuatro kilómetros bajo las montañas para engrosar el río Garona y acabar en el Atlántico.

Indicador de rutas en la Artiga de Kin, en el Valle de Arán. Andrés Campos

Flores mil, más de 150 mariposas y dos guías excelentes

Al pie de la cascada tumultuosa, hay una pasarela metálica que permite cruzar el río Joèu para seguir subiendo por el abetal de la margen contraria y acabar saliendo, tras dos horas de paseo, al Plan dera Artiga de Lin. Es un rellano glaciar bellísimo, presidido por la mole rocosa del Malh dera Artiga (2.711 metros) y alfombrado de prados llenos de flores —gencianas, astrancias, violetas de los Pirineos, geranios silvestres, consueldas mayores, malvas moscadas…— y mariposas de montaña: la apolo, la mnemosine, la colias alpina, la erebia oeme, la común, la dentada…

Para distinguir las más de 150 especies que viven en este Shangri-La de las mariposas, es sumamente útil la guía ilustrada que ha publicado el Conselh Generau d’Aran. Otra guía excelente para explorar la Artiga de Lin es Sara Arjó, bióloga que dirige la empresa de ecoturismo y educación ambiental Verd e Blu y que es la autora de Parpalhòles dera Val d’Aran, un juego didáctico de papiroflexia con 14 recortables de mariposas de siete especies, las más llamativas del lugar.

Mariposa zygaena osterodensis en la Artiga de Lin. Andrés Campos

Todo es bonito en la Artiga de Lin, hasta el espléndido refugio donde Arjó se toma un refresco y algún tentempié con sus clientes, dejándolos disfrutar un rato largo de este paisaje embobador antes de acercarse al siguiente lugar destacado de la ruta: la cascada de Pomèro. En esta última, a solo 300 metros del refugio, les presenta la amapola amarilla (Papaver cambricum), una flor rara en España, pero muy abundante y estimada en las islas británicas, a tal punto que la usa como emblema Plaid Cymru, el partido nacionalista que ahora gobierna en Gales. Una microcentral eléctrica produce en este florido salto la energía de la que se abastece el refugio, que es grandecito, con habitaciones para 27 montañeros y un buen restaurante para cualquiera que pase.

Vista al Aneto desde el mirador de Vilamòs

Desde el refugio se baja cómodamente por la carretera asfaltada hasta la ermita donde se aparcó al principio. Como no se tarda mucho en completar la vuelta a pie (la ruta circular descrita, de algo menos de ocho kilómetros, lleva hacerla unas tres horas, cuatro con paradas contemplativas y de refresco), hay tiempo para acercarse en coche al mirador de Vilamòs, que está a solo siete kilómetros de la Artiga de Lin en línea recta, pero a 17 por una carretera loca (la LV5055) que sube desde El Pont d’Arròs trazando 16 revueltas. El mirador no está señalizado en la carretera, pero sí en Google Maps.

Vista del refugio de la Artiga de Lin, en el Valle de Arán. Andrés Campos

Desde aquí, con la ayuda del móvil y de la aplicación AR AlpineGuide (disponible en Google Play y en Apple Store), pueden identificarse las montañas que se alzan alrededor de la Artiga de Lin, arropando su formidable recuenco glaciar: la doble cima de la Forcanada, el Malh dera Artiga, la Tuca Blanca de Pomèro… Detrás de esta última cumbre asoman las nieves perpetuas y los riscos estratosféricos del macizo de la Maladeta, señoreados por el Aneto (3.404 metros).

Después de este atracón de montañas, apetece bajar a El Pont d’Arròs para darse otro de cocina aranesa en el restaurante del hotel Peña. Este es un cuatro estrellas cómodo y hogareño a más no poder, al que solo le falta aire acondicionado en las habitaciones para ser extraordinario. Pronto lo instalarán: el cambio climático obliga. Luego, un baño en la piscina climatizada y a la cama, que mañana hay que madrugar para explorar otra cara oculta de Arán, su rincón más desconocido y solitario: la Val de Toran.

Republicanos, judíos, maquis y contrabandistas

En Puntaut, poco antes de que el río Garona se cuele en Francia y de que la carretera N230 española se convierta en la N125 gala, se desvía a la derecha otra muy estrecha, sin eje central y sumamente virada que se adentra en la recóndita Val de Toran. Seis kilómetros y 38 curvas más arriba, se llega a Canejan, un pueblecito-balcón que domina desde su altura un inmenso panorama ­de las montañas donde España y Francia se besan.

Una cruz occitana en en suelo de la Plaça dera Castra, en Canejan. Andrés Campos

En la Plaça dera Castra, la mayor y más cuidada, la del Ayuntamiento, de pavimento decorado con una gran cruz occitana —la enseña aranesa—, dos paneles informativos recuerdan que por Canejan pasaban a Francia no pocos republicanos que huían de la represión franquista tras la Guerra Civil y judíos que escapaban en dirección contraria, de la Europa ocupada por los nazis, durante la Segunda Guerra Mundial. También recuerdan que esta fue la primera localidad atacada y tomada por los guerrilleros antifranquistas en octubre de 1944 durante la llamada Operación Reconquista de España, que pretendía deponer al dictador y restaurar la República. No dicen nada, en cambio, de los contrabandistas que trajinaban aquí en los años del hambre y del racionamiento, entre 1939 y 1952. Para decirlo, están los vecinos. No es que haya muchos en la Val de Toran (unos cien), pero casi todos están en Canejan. Una de ellas, Generosa Marqués, cuenta al que quiera oírla el caso de sus padres, Pedro y Palmira, que una vez al mes iban a la comuna gala de Fos y volvían cargados de café y azúcar, productos que escaseaban en el mercado regulado español y por los que sacaban un buen pico. Hasta que una noche los sorprendieron y pasaron las 15 siguientes entre rejas.

Difícil saber qué caminos usaban los contrabandistas para cruzar la raya. Como dice Generosa, “el tiempo, el del reloj y el atmosférico, los ha borrado”. Sin embargo, se conservan bien algunos de los que seguían para trapichear en este valle fronterizo, como el histórico que une Canejan, Porcingles y Sant Joan de Toran. Para andar por él solo hay que subir a lo más alto de Canejan y salir del pueblo siguiendo la calle Era Cau, que pronto se hace de tierra, asciende dejando a la derecha unas rústicas bordas y se vuelve prácticamente llana. Para más señas, hay indicadores de dirección y marcas de pintura blanca y roja a lo largo de todo el recorrido, pues coincide con el sendero GR-211. Y se puede consultar el mapa y descargar el track de la ruta en Wikiloc.

La soledad de Porcingles y Sant Joan de Toran

Tras una hora de paseo por este camino alto y horizontal, contemplando cómo desde una terraza el callejón sin salida montañoso de la Val de Toran, se entra en Porcingles, una aldea fantasma con solo dos casas temporalmente habitadas, calles impracticables y un lavadero cuyas aguas llevan tanto tiempo sin reflejar a un humano, que las mariposas (los sátiros del bosque y los ocelados, por citar dos especies que aquí se ven), se posan sobre las manos del recién llegado, sin saber qué es. Las ruinas de Porcingles son un recuerdo escalofriante de cuando a la Val de Toran llegó para quedarse una muchedumbre de 500 personas poseída por la fiebre del oro o, más bien, del zinc y del plomo, que eran lo que se sacaba de las minas de Liat, en la cabecera del valle, durante el siglo XIX y a principios del XX. Había incluso un teleférico de 13 kilómetros que transportaba todo lo extraído valle abajo, hasta el lavadero de mineral de Puntaut.

El camino, bastante llano hasta Porcingles, gana luego altura, cruza el barranco de Gotèrs y la pierde para llegar, al cumplirse dos horas de marcha, a Sant Joan de Toran. Tampoco es un lugar donde viva una multitud: solo tres personas. Pero junto a los prados que alguien se ha tomado la molestia de segar, hay una iglesia con macetas floridas a cada lado de la puerta y una docena larga de casas y bordas tradicionales de piedra en perfecto estado, en cuyos tejados de afilado caballete no falta una sola losa de pizarra: señal de que aquí viene a pasar cortas temporadas gente harta del mundanal ruido, que sabe lo que es bueno y que puede permitírselo. En este pueblo de postal se encuentra uno de los pocos negocios turísticos de la Val de Toran, el restaurante Estupendet, buen sitio para tomarse una ensaladilla rusa de verdad y una cerveza artesanal Refu. Este pulcro pueblecito rodeado de prados y montañas es lo más encantador del Valle de Arán, con permiso de la Artiga de Lin.

World.title: Fire station break-ins soar as criminals steal rescue gear
World.content:
Break-ins at Dutch fire stations, which have risen sharply this year, are threatening life-saving work, the police have said. Criminal gangs are stealing the cutting equipment crews use to free people trapped in crashed cars, which they can be used for robberies.

There were 17 break-ins or attempted break-ins at fire stations in 2024 and 18 in 2025, broadcaster NOS reported. So far this year there have been 50. Stations in Maassluis, Aalsmeer and Ten Boer were all targeted in the past week.

The police, the fire service and the public prosecution department have begun working together nationally to stop the thefts. “One way or another, we are going to put a stop to this,” Jos van der Stap of the national police told NOS.

Police believe experienced criminals have discovered a market for the specialist tools. Van der Stap said they are being used in raids on jewellers and, abroad, to break open cash machines, and have turned up in several places across Europe.

Steven van der Looij of Brandweer Nederland, the national fire service organisation, said staff who work day and night at stations find it terrible thatpeople are coming into the buildings. Both quiet rural stations and busy city ones staffed around the clock have been hit.

Locking the equipment away is not straightforward. Everything on a fire engine is laid out so it can be grabbed at speed, Van der Looij said, and every extra lock has to be undone again. “Every second counts.”

Security cameras are being installed at some stations and windows are being replaced with mirrored glass.

World.title: Mental health services lose track of 62,500 people, says report
World.content:
A quarter of adults with a severe mental illness in the Netherlands – an estimated 62,500 people – are receiving no or insufficient care and have dropped out of sight of mental health services altogether, according to a report from the sector body de Nederlandse GGZ.

The organisation puts the total number of adults with a severe mental illness at around 250,000. What goes wrong, it says, is rarely the treatment itself but the handover – the point at which someone leaves a clinic, moves house or finishes a prison sentence.

“A discharge from a clinic, a house move or the end of a period in detention must not become the moment at which someone loses their support,” GGZ chair Ruth Peetoom said in a statement on Tuesday. “A psychological vulnerability does not disappear when a care pathway or an assessment comes to an end.”

Nowhere to go

The housing crisis is one of the biggest obstacles in helping patients through the transition out of care. The report calculates that 3,980 social housing units are needed each year for people leaving sheltered accommodation, but only 1,320 came free in 2023.

Around 33,000 people aged between 18 and 65 were registered as homeless at the start of 2024.

The pattern is similar for people leaving prison. Of the roughly 5,000 people released each year after more than three months inside, 27% are homeless or have no known address immediately afterwards, and almost half reoffend within two years.

Outreach

The report calls for assertive outreach – teams that actively go looking for people who are not asking for help – to be made a statutory duty for councils again.

It has not been one since social care was devolved in 2015, and funding is now split between health insurers, councils and central government, on top of the pressure on waiting lists that has already prompted legal action against the state.

Debate about severe mental illness in the Netherlands is dominated by figures on nuisance and public safety, the report says. It puts the number of people who pose a safety risk to others at around 1,500, against 24,000 to 60,000 who are a risk to themselves, through self-neglect, homelessness or avoiding care.

If you are struggling with your mental health, support is available. The MIND Hulplijn offers free, anonymous advice on 0900-1450, on weekdays from 9am to 9pm, or via mindhulplijn.nl. In a crisis, contact your family doctor or call 113.

World.title: NEC close in on Champions League after knocking out Olympiacos
World.content:

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

NEC Nijmegen are one step away from reaching the Champions League group stages after a hard-fought 2-1 win against Olympiacos.

After a 0-0 draw in Piraeus last week, NEC fell behind straight after half-time when Ayoub El Kaabi fired the 48-time Greek champions in front.

Bryan Linssen equalised with a lunging volley in the 70th minute to take the match to extra time.

The fans in the Goffertstadion thought they were celebrating a winner when Kaj Sierhuis headed the ball into the net in the 93rd minute, but his effort was ruled out for offside.

But with Olympiacos reduced to 10 men following the sending-off of Kostas Fortounis just before the end of regular time, NEC found the breakthrough when Emre Mor dispatched a loose ball in the penalty area.

Standing between NEC and the lucrative Champions League group is Norwegian side Bodø/Glimt, who reached the last 16 of the competition last season.

Bodø/Glimt also needed extra time to overcome Belgian side Union Saint-Gilloise 3-2 in the home leg for an aggregate score of 6-5.

The first leg will be played in Nijmegen on August 19, with NEC travelling to the Arctic Circle for the return leg on Tuesday, August 25.

World.title: Visser bags second Dutch European athletics gold in photo-finish
World.content:
Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Nadine Visser won the Netherlands’ second gold medal at the European athletics championships in a dramatic final of the 100 metres hurdles.

Visser, 31, was awarded the victory on a photo-finish after edging out her Polish rival Pia Skrzyszowska with her lunge for the line.

Both athletes were awarded the same time of 12.67 seconds, but Visser was adjudged to have got there first by 1/1000 of a second.

It was a first outdoor title for Visser, who has two gold and two silver medals for 60 metres hurdles at the European indoor championships.

“I’ve been to so many championships but there was always something that got in the way,” she said. “But I didn’t want to think about it too hard, because that puts you under pressure.”

In other events, Elvis Afrifa reached the men’s 100 metres final, but just missed out on a medal in fourth place.

Koster sixth

Afrifa finished 0.03 seconds behind the bronze medallist, the fast-finishing German Owen Ansah. Gold and silver went to the British pair of Romell Glave and Jeremiah Azu as the defending champion, Italy’s Marcell Jacobs, pulled up halfway through the race with an injury.

Maureen Koster finished sixth in the women’s 5000m after leading the field in the closing laps, before being overtaken in the last 200 metres by a string of fast finishers led by Italy’s Nadia Battocletti.

Just behind her in seventh place was 23-year-old compatriot Amina Maatoug, running in her first European championships, while Jennifer Gulikers finished 13th.

Femke Broeders-Bol cruised through her heat of the 800 metres, winning in a time of 1:59.96 seconds. The 26-year-old, who switched from the 400 metres hurdles this season, will run again in the semi-finals on Thursday.

World.title: Biggest eclipse in 27 years to darken Dutch skies tonight
World.content:
The biggest solar eclipse over the Netherlands in 27 years will take place on Wednesday evening, when around 90% of the sun will disappear behind the moon.

The eclipse begins at about 7.15pm and reaches its peak around 8.10pm, when the moon appears to take its largest bite out of the sun. The two then set together roughly an hour later.

Because the sun will already be low in the sky by then, anyone hoping to watch will need a clear view towards the west or north-west. Forecasters expect a warm, largely clear evening, with some thin high cloud in the north that should not obscure the view.

Eye specialists have warned against looking directly at the sun. Sunglasses, welding goggles and CDs offer no protection and can cause permanent damage to the retina. Only eclipse glasses meeting the ISO 12312-2 safety standard are considered safe.

A simple alternative is to make a pinhole in a sheet of paper and project the image of the sun onto a white surface.

Public viewings have been organised around the country. The Radboud University observatory in Nijmegen will be open, and the Copernicus observatory in Haarlem is taking telescopes fitted with solar filters to the seafront at Bloemendaal. Eclipse watches are also planned on the Frisian islands.

Only in Iceland, northern Spain and a small part of Portugal will the sun vanish completely.

The last time this much of the sun was covered over the Netherlands was in August 1999 – an event that regional broadcaster L1 recalls was largely spoiled by cloud in much of the country. A comparable eclipse is not expected again until 2081, and the next total eclipse visible from the Netherlands will come on October 7, 2135.

Anyone still outdoors later has a second chance. The Perseid meteor shower peaks overnight into Thursday, and with a new moon the sky will be unusually dark.

World.title: Amsterdam transport chief hid €850m bridge costs before election
World.content:
Amsterdam’s former transport chief, Melanie van der Horst, knew before March’s local elections that a planned cycle and pedestrian bridge over the IJ would cost up to €850 million – more than double the sum set aside – but did not tell the city council, documents released under a freedom of information request show.

Van der Horst, who is now the city’s head of economic affairs and was also lead candidate for the social-liberal party D66 at the elections, had been told by officials that the estimate for the Oostbrug had risen to between €650 million and €850 million, compared with the €325 million budgeted. The papers were obtained by Amsterdam broadcaster AT5.

Officials circulated the final estimate internally around December 2 and, according to AT5, explicitly gave Van der Horst the choice of making the figures public before or after the vote. At a meeting on February 12 it was decided to keep the older, lower amounts in the city’s official investment note.

Eight days before the elections Van der Horst was given a presentation setting out how the new range had been calculated. During the campaign she cited the IJ crossings as one of her administration’s achievements.

The new estimates only surfaced in early June, when the city published the documents handed to coalition negotiators.

The bridge, which at 1.2 kilometres would be one of the longest in the country, is being paid for jointly by the council and the regional transport authority Vervoerregio Amsterdam.

Emergency debate

Seven opposition parties – PvdD, Volt, JA21, Denk, BIJ1, CDA and SP – said in a joint statement they were shocked by the revelations but were not yet drawing conclusions, and an emergency debate has been requested. The coalition party PRO and D66’s own council group have also said they want answers.

Van der Horst declined to comment, referring questions to Elise Moeskops (D66), who took over the transport brief. Moeskops said the provisional estimates carry wide margins and could still change, that work on the design is continuing and that a final figure is not expected until early next year.

World.title: Dutch navy to take part in Nato exercise in Greenland next month
World.content:
Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google
